returned_title: Federal Parliament Election 1972 (Panel: 2nd Wave, October 1971 – January 1972)
justification: An exceptionally close match to the research requirements. This West German federal election panel survey covers party preferences and identification, evaluations of chancellor candidates Willy Brandt and Rainer Barzel, perceived issue competence of parties, political participation, attitudes toward democracy, voting intentions, and vote splitting. It also includes economic expectations, subjective social class, parental social class, political discussions in the parental home, and party sympathies of parents, spouses, and other close persons. Particularly valuable for analyzing family political socialization and the relationship between socioeconomic background, political attitudes, and electoral behavior.

returned_title: Election Study 1972 (Panel: Preliminary Investigations, September–October 1972, October–November 1972; Follow-Up Survey, December 1972)
justification: A major three-wave panel survey surrounding the November 1972 West German federal election. Provides individual-level electoral behavior and political attitudes, including party preferences, voting intentions, party membership, and electoral choices. Its repeated observations allow researchers to investigate changes in political preferences during the election campaign and compare pre-election attitudes with subsequent voting behavior. GESIS study ZA0635. Highly relevant for studying electoral decision-making and party support in 1970s West Germany.

returned_title: German National Election Panel Study, 1972
justification: An ICPSR panel study specifically designed to investigate electoral behavior in the Federal Republic of Germany during the November 1972 federal election. Covers voting behavior, political attitudes, public opinion, political participation, political perceptions, economic policy, foreign policy, German reunification, and demographic characteristics. Particularly useful for examining the relationship between political preferences, policy attitudes, and electoral decisions. Its longitudinal design supports analysis of electoral preference formation and change.

returned_title: Election Study 1976 (Panel: Initial Investigation, May–June 1976, August–September 1976; Follow-Up Survey, October–November 1976)
justification: A three-wave panel survey covering the 1976 West German federal election. GESIS study ZA0823 contains information on electoral preferences, party evaluations, government preferences, and political attitudes. Documented variables include respondents' assessments of whether election outcomes and governing parties would improve their personal financial situation. The panel structure makes it especially useful for investigating campaign-period changes in voting intentions, economic considerations in electoral choice, and the relationship between attitudes toward government and voting behavior.

returned_title: Workbook: Occupational Mobility in the Federal Republic (Federal Parliament Election 1972, First and Second Follow-Up Survey)
justification: A dataset derived from the 1972 West German federal election survey, specifically designed for analyzing occupational mobility and its relationship to political attitudes and behavior. Includes social origins, subjective social class, occupational characteristics, party identification, party preferences, voting intentions, party sympathy scales, political interest, and attitudes toward political issues. Also contains retrospective information on voting behavior in the 1969 federal election. Particularly useful for examining social class, intergenerational socioeconomic background, political alignment, and electoral behavior. GESIS study ZA0646, with 3,448 observations and 47 variables.

returned_title: Federal Parliament Election 1969 (Pre-Election Investigation, September 1969; Follow-Up Survey, October–November 1969)
justification: Although collected immediately before the 1970s, this West German federal election panel provides an important baseline for analyzing political attitudes and voting behavior entering the decade. Covers party sympathy, candidate evaluations, issue competence, voting intentions for first and second votes, political interest, economic perceptions, and attitudes toward major policy issues. Particularly relevant to family political socialization because it examines relationships between respondents' political attitudes and those of family members and friends. Also includes religious affiliation, organizational membership, and socioeconomic characteristics. Useful for comparisons with the 1972 and 1976 election surveys.

returned_title: Resonance of the Population to the Election Campaign and the Result of the Federal Parliament Election 1969
justification: A supplementary historical survey examining public responses to the 1969 West German federal election campaign and its outcome. Relevant for establishing the political-attitudinal context immediately preceding the 1970s, particularly public reactions to election campaigns, political parties, and electoral results. Can complement the 1972 and 1976 election studies when investigating continuity and change in electoral attitudes across the decade.

returned_title: Politbarometer: West German Political Opinion Surveys, 1977 Onward
justification: A collection of recurring representative surveys examining the political attitudes of the West German electorate, beginning in 1977. Covers evaluations of political parties and politicians, voting behavior in previous Bundestag elections, political preferences, and assessments of current political issues. Particularly useful for tracking political attitudes and party support during the late 1970s, including periods between federal elections. Annual cumulative datasets and harmonized time-series resources facilitate longitudinal analysis.

returned_title: Politbarometer Time Series, 1977–2024 (ZA2391)
justification: A harmonized political opinion time-series dataset containing 84 selected variables from Politbarometer surveys beginning in 1977. Relevant for studying the evolution of party preferences, political attitudes, electoral behavior, and evaluations of political actors in West Germany during the late 1970s. Particularly valuable for comparing political sentiment across survey periods and examining trends beyond individual election campaigns. Researchers can restrict the analysis to observations collected during 1977–1979.

returned_title: West German Federal Election Studies, 1949–2005 (GESIS Historical Election Survey Collection)
justification: An authoritative GESIS collection of historical German federal election surveys, including studies conducted during the 1970s. Provides access to individual-level survey data suitable for comparative research on party identification, electoral preferences, candidate evaluations, political attitudes, socioeconomic characteristics, and voting behavior. Particularly useful for identifying compatible variables across the 1972 and 1976 election studies and building a broader historical analysis of West German electoral behavior. The collection also provides access to documentation and metadata needed to assess variable comparability across elections.

returned_title: Patterns of Child Rearing, 1951–1958
justification: Highly relevant historical survey dataset examining parental child-rearing practices, family authority, discipline, punishment, and demographic characteristics. Interviews cover parental decisions about child training, rewards and punishments, children's aggression, parental reactions, and family responsibilities. Although collected in the United States during the 1950s rather than Hesse in the 1960s, it provides valuable comparative evidence on family authority and early childhood political socialization.

returned_title: Three-Wave Political Socialization Panel Survey of Children in the San Francisco East Bay Area, 1968–1969 (ICPSR 2341)
justification: Historical survey dataset directly investigating children's political socialization during the late 1960s. Measures political opinions and their development over time, alongside demographic variables including age, sex, religion, parental occupation, education, and socioeconomic background. Particularly useful for investigating how children acquire political attitudes and orientations toward authority. The geographical coverage is California rather than Hesse, and the study is not specifically restricted to preschool children.

returned_title: Politics and the English Child, 1969
justification: Highly relevant 1969 survey dataset exploring children's political attitudes, perceptions of authority, and family influences on political socialization. Includes children's attitudes toward police, political leaders, schools, and other institutions, as well as political discussions within families, parental political affiliations, religion, parental occupations, education, age, sex, and social class. Particularly valuable for studying police as authority figures and the relationship between family background and political attitudes. Covers English schoolchildren rather than preschool children in Hesse.

returned_title: Eurostat – Crimes Recorded by the Police (1950–2000)
justification: One of the strongest starting points for reconstructing long-run crime trends in Germany, England and Wales, and Sweden. Provides annual historical police-recorded crime statistics covering 1950–2000, although the starting years differ by country. Particularly useful for examining the rise in recorded crime during the 1960s–1990s and comparing changes across national contexts. Total recorded crime is available over longer periods than individual violent-offence categories. Differences in criminal definitions, recording practices, and reporting rates must be considered.

returned_title: Eurostat – Historical Crime and Criminal Justice Statistics (1950–2007)
justification: Provides access to historical European crime datasets covering police-recorded offences, homicide, violent crime, and imprisonment. Total recorded crime series extend to 1950 for some countries, including Germany and England and Wales, while more detailed offence categories generally begin in 1993 and prison population statistics in 1987. Particularly relevant for studying whether changes in violence corresponded with changes in imprisonment and criminal justice policies during the late twentieth century.

returned_title: World Health Organization – WHO Mortality Database (1950–Present)
justification: A particularly important source for historical homicide comparisons. Contains cause-specific mortality statistics reported by national vital registration systems, with records extending back to 1950 where available. Homicide deaths can be identified through the relevant international cause-of-death classifications and analyzed by age, sex, country, and year. Useful for comparing Germany, the United Kingdom, Sweden, and the United States while reducing dependence on police-recorded crime statistics. Changes in ICD coding and differences in historical coverage require harmonization.

returned_title: ICPSR – Violence and Crime in Cross-National Perspective, 1900–1974
justification: Historical comparative crime dataset covering 110 countries and 44 urban locations over periods extending from 1900 to 1974. Particularly valuable for establishing pre-1970 baselines for violent crime and examining long-term differences in criminal violence between industrialized societies. Can complement Eurostat and WHO datasets by extending the historical perspective into the early postwar decades. Researchers should inspect country-specific coverage and variable definitions before constructing comparable series.

returned_title: World Prison Brief – Historical Prison Population Statistics
justification: Provides internationally comparable information on prison populations and imprisonment rates per 100,000 inhabitants, including historical trends where available. Relevant for comparing the expansion or contraction of imprisonment in Germany, Britain, Sweden, and the United States. Particularly useful for investigating whether rising imprisonment coincided with changes in homicide, recorded violence, unemployment, and social inequality. Historical coverage varies considerably across countries.

returned_title: International Crime Victims Survey – Integrated Database (1989–2016)
justification: Provides cross-national victimization survey data from 1989 onward. Especially useful for examining assault, robbery, victimization experiences, and perceptions of crime independently of official police statistics. Offers a valuable complement to homicide and recorded-crime series when investigating perceived security and public exposure to violence. Survey waves are intermittent rather than annual, and country participation varies.

returned_title: European Social Survey – Cross-National Social Attitudes and Security Data (2002–Present)
justification: Major comparative survey resource beginning in 2002, covering Germany, the United Kingdom, Sweden, and numerous other European countries. Contains measures related to perceived safety, experiences of crime, interpersonal trust, institutional trust, social participation, immigration attitudes, employment, and subjective well-being. Especially valuable for operationalizing social integration and perceived security during the 2000s. Repeated survey waves permit comparisons across countries and periods, although the dataset does not cover the earlier postwar decades.

returned_title: European Values Study – Longitudinal Data (1981–2008)
justification: Highly relevant for examining social integration and cultural change in Germany, Britain, and Sweden from the early 1980s through the 2000s. Includes repeated measures of interpersonal trust, family values, social norms, institutional confidence, political attitudes, and attitudes toward immigrants. Particularly useful for testing whether changes in social cohesion accompanied changes in violent crime and economic insecurity. The longitudinal dataset harmonizes multiple survey waves but does not provide annual observations.

returned_title: European Values Study – Longitudinal Data File 1981–2008, GESIS ZA4804
justification: Specific archived longitudinal dataset integrating European Values Study waves from 1981, 1990, 1999, and 2008. Includes observations from Britain, Sweden, West Germany, and, in later waves, East Germany. Especially appropriate for investigating the relationship between changes in trust, social attitudes, family norms, and broader processes of social integration. The distinction between East and West Germany is particularly important when analyzing social change surrounding reunification in 1990.

returned_title: UNU-WIDER – World Income Inequality Database (WIID)
justification: Extensive cross-national database of historical income inequality estimates, including Gini coefficients and other distributional measures. Useful for reconstructing inequality trends in Germany, Britain, Sweden, and the United States across much of the second half of the twentieth century. Particularly valuable for investigating associations between inequality, homicide, imprisonment, and social cohesion. Researchers should distinguish original observations from harmonized estimates and assess comparability across income concepts and survey sources.

returned_title: World Inequality Database – Historical Income and Wealth Inequality
justification: Provides historical estimates of income and wealth distribution across countries, including top income shares and other inequality measures. Particularly suitable for examining structural economic changes between the 1950s and 2000s in Germany, the United Kingdom, Sweden, and the United States. Can support tests of whether rising income concentration coincided with changes in homicide and social integration. Historical series differ in source quality, measurement definitions, and availability.

returned_title: OECD – Social Expenditure Database (SOCX), 1980 Onward
justification: Core comparative dataset for investigating welfare-state development and social protection in Germany, Britain, Sweden, and the United States. Provides information on public and private social spending, including pensions, unemployment support, family benefits, health, housing, and other social services. Historical coverage begins in 1980. Especially useful for examining whether welfare expansion or retrenchment corresponded with changes in inequality, labor-market insecurity, imprisonment, and violent crime.

returned_title: Comparative Welfare Entitlements Dataset (CWED2)
justification: Cross-national historical dataset measuring the structure and generosity of social insurance programs in industrialized countries. Particularly relevant for comparing unemployment insurance, sickness benefits, and pension arrangements across Germany, Britain, Sweden, and the United States. Provides a more direct measure of welfare entitlements than aggregate social expenditure alone. Useful for investigating whether differences in social protection moderated relationships between unemployment, inequality, social integration, and violent crime.

returned_title: OECD/AIAS – Institutional Characteristics of Trade Unions, Wage Setting, State Intervention and Social Pacts (ICTWSS)
justification: Important historical comparative dataset on labor-market institutions, trade union density, collective bargaining coverage, wage-setting arrangements, and employment relations. Particularly useful for comparing the evolution of organized labor and economic integration in Sweden, Germany, Britain, and the United States. Historical observations extend into the postwar period for a number of indicators. Can be linked to inequality, unemployment, and crime series to investigate the relationship between labor-market institutions and social stability.

returned_title: OECD – Employment by Permanency of the Job
justification: Comparative employment dataset distinguishing temporary from permanent employment arrangements. Directly relevant to operationalizing precarious employment and labor-market insecurity. Useful for examining changes in nonpermanent work in Germany, Britain, and Sweden during the later decades of the study period. Historical availability differs across countries, so it is best used alongside longer unemployment and labor-market institution series. Temporary employment is only one dimension of precarious work.

returned_title: OECD – Family Database
justification: Cross-national collection of indicators concerning family formation, marriage, divorce, fertility, household composition, children, and family policies. Particularly relevant for analyzing family change as a component of social integration in Germany, Britain, Sweden, and the United States. Can be linked to crime, welfare, and labor-market data to investigate whether changing family structures accompanied changes in violence. Historical coverage depends on the indicator, with some demographic series extending substantially further back than contemporary family-policy measures.

returned_title: Generations and Gender Programme – Harmonized Histories Database
justification: Harmonized retrospective demographic dataset containing information on marriage, partnership formation, separation, divorce, childbearing, and family trajectories. Also includes socioeconomic and family-background characteristics. Particularly valuable for studying family transitions and changing forms of household integration over historical periods. Retrospective histories can extend further back than the survey collection dates, although national coverage and representativeness must be checked before using the data for direct comparisons among Germany, Britain, Sweden, and the United States.

returned_title: United Nations DESA – International Migrant Stock (1990–2024)
justification: Internationally comparable estimates of migrant populations by destination country, origin, and sex. Covers Germany, the United Kingdom, Sweden, and the United States from 1990 onward. Particularly useful for investigating whether changes in migration corresponded with changes in social integration, perceptions of security, and violent crime during the 1990s and 2000s. The series provides migrant population stocks rather than direct measures of integration or annual immigration flows.

returned_title: FBI – Uniform Crime Reporting Program, Historical Crime in the United States
justification: Primary official source for historical United States crime statistics, including murder, aggravated assault, robbery, and other recorded offences. Historical publications provide data extending through the 1960s and later decades. Particularly relevant for including the United States as a comparative case alongside Germany, Britain, and Sweden. The American case allows examination of contrasting imprisonment, inequality, welfare, and violent-crime trajectories. Researchers must account for changes in reporting coverage and offence definitions.

returned_title: GESIS – European Values Study Data and Documentation
justification: Official archive and documentation resource for historical European Values Study datasets. Provides access to individual survey waves and longitudinal harmonized files, with questionnaires, methodological documentation, and country coverage information. Particularly valuable for selecting consistent indicators of social trust, family change, institutional confidence, and attitudes toward migration across Germany, Britain, and Sweden. Supports careful assessment of variable comparability across the 1980s, 1990s, and 2000s.

returned_title: World Prison Brief – Historical Trends in Imprisonment
justification: Documentation of expanded historical imprisonment data in the World Prison Brief. Useful for identifying countries with longer historical incarceration series and reconstructing prison population trends. Particularly relevant for distinguishing violent-crime developments from changes in penal policy and imprisonment practices. Historical coverage is uneven, and direct comparisons require attention to whether statistics include remand prisoners, sentenced prisoners, and other categories of detention.

returned_title: OECD – Historical Comparative Homicide Data Referenced in How Was Life?
justification: Historical statistical resource examining long-run developments in living standards and social conditions, including homicide rates across historical periods. The underlying historical homicide estimates are relevant for contextualizing postwar developments against longer-run changes in interpersonal violence. Particularly useful as a supplementary source for historical comparison, although the publication and its underlying source datasets should be distinguished. Researchers should verify the geographic and temporal coverage of the homicide observations before merging them with annual postwar series.

returned_title: Political Situation in West Berlin (Young People from the GDR) — January 1955 (ZA0590)
justification: Excellent match and the most directly relevant dataset. Conducted in January 1955 by DIVO Frankfurt for the United States Information Agency (USIA), this survey examines the economic and political attitudes of young East German refugees in West Berlin and compares their perspectives with those of Berlin youth. Topics include economic development, youth unemployment, proposed solutions to unemployment, economic assistance to Berlin, perceptions of government, young people's participation in economic recovery, treatment of youth by authorities, and awareness of youth programs and facilities. The dataset contains 137 respondents aged 14–24 who were young refugees from the GDR. It directly addresses the research need concerning postwar youth attitudes, economic conditions, political perceptions, and refugee experiences.

returned_title: The Political Situation in West Berlin (March 1958) — ZA0591
justification: Highly relevant supplementary dataset examining political attitudes, economic expectations, migration intentions, and refugee-related concerns in West Berlin during the late 1950s. Conducted in March 1958 by DIVO Frankfurt for USIA, the survey includes 1,096 respondents selected through multistage random sampling. Topics include perceptions of Berlin's economic recovery, unemployment, refugee arrivals, intentions to migrate to East Germany or West Germany, relations with Western powers, and contacts with East Berlin and the GDR. Although not specifically restricted to youth, it provides valuable contextual evidence for comparing the economic and political concerns of Berlin residents with those of young East German refugees.

returned_title: Attitudes of East German Youth: Surveys Conducted During the Berlin Youth Festival — August 1951 (European USIA Report Collection)
justification: Highly relevant historical survey collection documenting the attitudes of East German youth who visited West Berlin during the August 1951 World Festival of Youth and Students. The USIA surveys were conducted among young people crossing from East Berlin into West Berlin, with interviews taking place between August 5 and 19, 1951. The reports examine evaluations of the youth festival, impressions of West Berlin, perceptions of economic well-being, political freedom, and differences between East and West German living conditions. The collection includes the September 29, 1951 report 'Attitudes of East German Youth: Evaluations of the Festival and Impressions of West Berlin.' Particularly useful for investigating Cold War political socialization, East-West comparisons, youth organizations, and perceptions of Western economic and political systems. The linked page is a collection-level landing page rather than an individual microdata record.

returned_title: The Reunification of West Germany — September 1956 (ZA3310)
justification: Relevant supplementary survey conducted in September 1956 by the United States Information Agency, with geographic coverage including West Berlin. It investigates perceptions of living conditions in East Germany, German reunification, political responsibilities for Germany's division, attitudes toward Western and Eastern alliances, and support for Chancellor Adenauer's policies. Questions also address the reintroduction of compulsory military service in West Germany, making this dataset particularly useful for research on rearmament and Cold War political attitudes. Although it is not specifically a youth or refugee survey, it provides historical context for understanding the political environment influencing young Germans' views on military service, reunification, and East-West relations.

returned_title: European USIA Report Collection — Historical Public Opinion Surveys, 1949–1955
justification: A broader historical collection of USIA public opinion research that includes surveys of East German political attitudes during the early Cold War. In addition to the 1951 Berlin Youth Festival studies, the collection contains reports addressing public opinion behind the Iron Curtain, perceptions of Western society, and political attitudes within East Germany. It offers potential comparative material for analyzing how young people's views differed from those of broader East German populations. Particularly useful for identifying related contemporary surveys on ideological orientations, social conditions, Western influence, and the political consequences of Germany's division. Individual report availability and access to respondent-level data should be verified through the collection.

returned_title: Interactions between Political and Economic Attitudes of the Population of Berlin — 1963–1964 (ZA0382)
justification: Relevant for extending the historical comparison beyond the 1950s. This West Berlin survey series, conducted between June 1963 and September 1964, examines economic confidence, political attitudes, expectations about reunification, migration intentions, perceptions of Western powers, and support for the multiparty system. It contains 3,576 observations across 11 survey waves and includes respondents aged 14 and older, allowing investigation of younger age groups where the data permit. Although collected after the construction of the Berlin Wall and therefore outside the requested decade, it provides a useful comparison for assessing changes in attitudes toward Berlin's political and economic future.

returned_title: System of Social Indicators for the Federal Republic of Germany: Participation, 1950–2013 (ZA8649)
justification: Supplementary longitudinal dataset providing historical indicators of political and social participation in Germany beginning in 1950. Compiled by GESIS, it includes information on political engagement, political interests, trade union membership, participation in organizations, and other dimensions of social integration. Its coverage of the 1950s makes it potentially useful for contextualizing organizational membership and political participation among young Germans. However, it consists of aggregated national indicators rather than individual-level interviews with Berlin youth or refugees, so it is best used as a contextual source rather than a direct match.

returned_title: Politbarometer Germany – Annual Surveys and Cumulative Datasets (2010–2019)
justification: Excellent match. Politbarometer provides approximately monthly representative surveys of German voters, covering assessments of Germany's current political and economic situation, satisfaction with democracy, political interest, party preferences, evaluations of politicians, government performance, voting intentions, and major political issues. Annual cumulative datasets are available throughout the 2010s, making this particularly useful for studying changes in political attitudes over time.

returned_title: Politbarometer 1977–2024 – Partial Cumulative Dataset
justification: Highly relevant longitudinal survey dataset containing harmonized political opinion measures across multiple decades, including 2010–2019. Covers political attitudes, party preferences, evaluations of government and politicians, satisfaction with democracy, and perceptions of Germany's economic and political circumstances. Particularly suitable for examining trends in public opinion during the 2010s.

returned_title: German Longitudinal Election Study (GLES) – Election Surveys and Panels, 2009–2017
justification: Excellent match for research on political behavior, democratic attitudes, party evaluations, political participation, and political communication in Germany. Includes cross-sectional surveys, longitudinal panels, campaign surveys, and tracking studies covering the 2013 and 2017 federal elections. Relevant variables include political interest, voting behavior, evaluations of parties and candidates, perceptions of political problems, and media-related political communication. Multiple datasets allow comparisons across elections and over time.

returned_title: German Longitudinal Election Study (GLES) – Cross-Sectional Election Surveys
justification: Highly relevant survey series examining German voters before and after federal elections, including those held in 2013 and 2017. Captures political preferences, evaluations of parties and politicians, political attitudes, electoral participation, and political involvement. Particularly useful for investigating how public perceptions of politics and democratic representation relate to electoral behavior.

returned_title: German General Social Survey (ALLBUS) – Surveys from 2010 to 2018
justification: Strong match for studying political and social attitudes among the German population throughout the 2010s. ALLBUS conducts representative population surveys approximately every two years. Relevant measures include political interest, political orientations, trust in institutions, attitudes toward democracy, social values, and civic engagement. The repeated cross-sectional design supports comparisons of attitudes across different years and demographic groups.

returned_title: German General Social Survey (ALLBUS) – Cumulative Dataset
justification: Useful for longitudinal analysis of political attitudes and social change in Germany, including observations collected during the 2010s. The cumulative datasets combine multiple ALLBUS survey waves and facilitate comparisons of political trust, institutional confidence, political interest, democratic values, and participation patterns. Particularly appropriate for identifying long-term changes in Germans' relationships with democratic institutions.

returned_title: GLES – German Federal Election Studies, Campaign Panels and Media Data
justification: Especially relevant for research combining political behavior and media use. The GLES collection includes election campaign panels, rolling cross-sectional surveys, tracking surveys, and media content data associated with German federal elections in 2009, 2013, and 2017. These resources support research on political information exposure, election campaigns, political preferences, evaluations of candidates, voting decisions, and changes in public opinion.

returned_title: Modern State and Living Democracy (Moderner Staat und lebendige Demokratie), 2016
justification: Relevant Germany-specific survey dataset collected in October 2016. Classified under political behavior and attitudes and government, political systems, and organizations. Its focus on the modern state and democracy makes it a potentially useful supplementary source for investigating public attitudes toward democratic governance and political institutions during the 2010s. The documentation should be checked for the precise questions available.

returned_title: European Social Survey (ESS) – Germany, 2010–2018
justification: Strong supplementary source for representative survey data on Germany during the 2010s. Relevant ESS rounds include 2010, 2012, 2014, 2016, and 2018. Core questionnaires cover trust in political institutions, satisfaction with democracy, political interest, voting behavior, political participation, political ideology, and media use. Particularly valuable for examining German public opinion over time and comparing Germany with other European democracies.

returned_title: GESIS Election Studies – German Political Opinion and Electoral Behavior Data
justification: Relevant repository entry point for German political survey datasets, including Politbarometer and the German Longitudinal Election Study. Provides access to studies covering political attitudes, electoral behavior, party evaluations, evaluations of politicians, and public responses to political developments during the 2010s. Useful for identifying additional survey waves and specialized election-related datasets.

returned_title: GESIS Politbarometer Research Data Collection
justification: Direct research-data catalog for individual and cumulative Politbarometer datasets, including surveys from 2010–2019. Particularly relevant variables include perceptions of Germany's most important problems, satisfaction with democracy, assessments of the national economy, confidence in political leadership, party sympathy ratings, politician evaluations, political interest, and voting intentions. The catalog allows researchers to identify specific survey years and examine detailed variable documentation.

returned_title: Sofortresonanzen DDR Fernsehen 23. Woche 1987 (SFR 23/87)
justification: Highly relevant survey dataset collected on June 9, 1987, by the State Committee for Television of the GDR. Contains television viewing participation and program evaluations, including perceived realism and informational value of the film DER FREISCHÜTZ IN BERLIN, ratings of main characters, evaluations of the moderator and entertainment segments of WENNSCHON – DENNSCHON, and audience reception of WETTLAUF MIT DER ZEIT. Particularly suitable for studying perceived realism, character ratings, moderator evaluations, and program-specific audience responses.

returned_title: Sofortresonanzen DDR Fernsehen 50. Woche 1982 (SFR 50/82)
justification: GDR television audience survey conducted on December 16, 1982. Includes viewing participation, evaluations of television programs, entertainment value (humor, wit, and amusement), reasons for watching KLOCK 8, ACHTERN STROM, satisfaction with program quality, and desired improvements. Also records the number of episodes watched and audience evaluations of the series BUSCH SINGT. Especially relevant for analyzing reception frequency, entertainment value, satisfaction, and evaluations of television series.

returned_title: Sofortresonanzen DDR Fernsehen 36. Woche 1985 (SFR 36/85)
justification: Audience survey from 1985 covering television viewing and evaluations of individual programs. Includes ratings of SPORT AKTUELL moderators, perceived realism and entertainment value of POLIZEIRUF 110 – EIN SCHRITT ZU WEIT, audience expectations, and assessments of DIE DRITTE FRAU, including sympathy toward fictional characters. Particularly useful for examining moderator ratings, character evaluations, realism, suspense, and entertainment preferences.

returned_title: Sofortresonanzen DDR Fernsehen 35. Woche 1988 (SFR 35/88)
justification: Highly relevant 1988 audience survey covering program reception and evaluation. Includes perceived realism and entertainment value of POLIZEIRUF 110: EIFERSUCHT, ratings of main characters, evaluations of moderators and humor in GLÜCK MUSS MAN HABEN, and viewing frequency of DAS VERKEHRSMAGAZIN. Also examines perceived usefulness of program content, technical presentation, and entertainment value. Provides a strong match for studying reception frequency, realism, character ratings, and audience satisfaction.

returned_title: Sofortresonanzen DDR Fernsehen 6. Woche 1983 (SFR 6/83)
justification: GDR television audience survey from 1983 measuring viewing participation and program evaluations. Includes entertainment value and moderator ratings for BONG, perceived target age groups, regular viewing of PORTRÄT PER TELEFON: HEINZ QUERMANN, and evaluations of MAGDEBURGER MOTIVE. Also investigates regular audiences, humor, entertainment value, and suggested improvements for KLOCK 8, ACHTERN STROM. Useful for analyzing program loyalty, moderator evaluations, viewing frequency, and entertainment preferences.

returned_title: Sofortresonanzen DDR Fernsehen 13. Woche 1985 (SFR 13/85)
justification: Television audience research from 1985 investigating viewing participation and evaluations of specific programs. Includes suspense and perceived realism of POLIZEIRUF 110 – TRAUM DES VERGESSENS, fulfillment of audience expectations, viewing frequency of KULTURMAGAZIN, and preferences regarding cultural programming. Also examines occupational characteristics, physical and mental workload, fatigue after work, and expectations of television programming. Particularly relevant for connecting program evaluations with reception conditions and respondents' everyday circumstances.

returned_title: Sofortresonanzen DDR Fernsehen 14. Woche 1982 (SFR 14/82)
justification: 1982 survey examining television viewing behavior and audience assessments of specific GDR programs. Measures entertainment value and realism of DER STAATSANWALT HAT DAS WORT: HOFFNUNG FÜR ANNA, perceived crime-prevention effects, the number of episodes watched of DU UND DEIN HAUSTIER, and realism and entertainment value of DER NOTNAGEL. Also includes awareness of several other television programs. Suitable for studying program familiarity, series viewing frequency, perceived realism, and audience evaluations.

returned_title: Sofortresonanzen DDR Fernsehen 5. Woche 1985 (SFR 5/85)
justification: 1985 GDR audience survey examining viewing behavior, program evaluations, and the social circumstances of television reception. Includes reasons for watching AUF SCHUSTERS RAPPEN, moderator ratings, conversations with family members while watching television, entertainment value of the film AUßENSEITER, and suggestions for improving the program STOP!. Especially valuable for research on reception conditions, family viewing environments, moderator evaluations, and entertainment preferences.

returned_title: Sofortresonanzen DDR Fernsehen 46. Woche 1984 (SFR 46/84)
justification: Representative household survey from 1984 examining GDR television reception and program evaluations. Includes audience assessments of UMSCHAU, interest in specific program topics, familiarity with television schedules, preferred broadcasting times for youth programming, the influence of shift work on television viewing, and parental influence on children's viewing behavior. Uses a stratified random household sample drawn from television subscriber records. Particularly useful for studying demographic differences, household viewing behavior, and reception conditions.

returned_title: Sofortresonanzen DDR Fernsehen 39. Woche 1982 (SFR 39/82)
justification: Representative GDR television audience survey from 1982 measuring viewing participation and evaluations of specific broadcasts. Includes detailed audience assessments of KOMM MIT MIR NACH CHICAGO, covering entertainment, relaxation, sympathy toward characters, representation of young people's experiences, and overall impressions. Also evaluates the program KNOBELEIEN, including its presentation, moderators Regina Liebsch and Ullrich Klein, and studio game segments. Particularly suitable for character ratings, moderator evaluations, perceived authenticity, and entertainment value.

returned_title: Sofortresonanzen DDR Fernsehen 28. Woche 1989 (SFR 28/89)
justification: 1989 GDR television audience survey examining program reception and audience satisfaction. Includes evaluations of the presenter and participating artists in SHOWKOLADE, reception of PFUNDGRUBE, ratings of its female moderator, appreciation of musical variety, and overall satisfaction with GDR television programming. Useful for studying presenter evaluations, entertainment preferences, program-specific audience responses, and broader satisfaction with the television system.

returned_title: Medienstudie zur Fernsehsendung Hautnah 1987
justification: Media reception study conducted in 1987 by the Zentralinstitut für Jugendforschung in Leipzig. Focuses on the GDR youth television program HAUTNAH, including assessments of its moderators' interviewing and discussion techniques, program content, and audience interest in comparable youth television formats. Also examines educational and occupational decision-making issues addressed by the program. Particularly relevant for studying moderator evaluations and the reception of youth-oriented television programming in the late GDR.

returned_title: Second European Survey of Enterprises on New and Emerging Risks, 2014 (ESENER-2) — UK Data Service
justification: Excellent match and the most directly relevant dataset. Conducted by the European Agency for Safety and Health at Work (EU-OSHA) in 2014, ESENER-2 surveyed 49,320 establishments across all 36 countries specified in the research query. It covers private and public establishments with at least five employees across economic sectors. The establishment-level data examine occupational safety and health (OSH) management, psychosocial risks including work-related stress, violence and harassment, workplace risk assessments, musculoskeletal disorders, employee participation, and organizational drivers and barriers to prevention. Variables also capture establishment size, sector, country, and management practices, supporting comparative cross-country and cross-sector research. The UK Data Service provides access to the research data and supporting documentation.

returned_title: Second European Survey of Enterprises on New and Emerging Risks, 2014 (ESENER-2) — GESIS Data Archive
justification: Highly relevant alternative archival record for the same 2014 ESENER-2 dataset, indexed through B2FIND using metadata from GESIS. Its geographical coverage matches all 36 requested countries, including Albania, Iceland, Montenegro, North Macedonia, Serbia, Turkey, Switzerland, Norway, and the United Kingdom. The data include establishment-level information on occupational risks, OSH policies, psychosocial risk management, risk assessments, worker representation, and organizational factors influencing preventive action. Additional variables identify establishment size, economic activity, NACE sector classification, country, and survey weights. Particularly useful for researchers seeking structured metadata and access through European social science data infrastructures.

returned_title: Second European Survey of Enterprises on New and Emerging Risks, 2014 — CESSDA/B2FIND Dataset Record
justification: European research data catalogue record for ESENER-2, providing another discovery and access route to the 2014 establishment-level survey. Covers 49,320 establishments in the exact 36 countries requested. The survey addresses four central research dimensions: general occupational safety and health management, psychosocial risk prevention, organizational drivers and barriers to OSH management, and worker participation. Its broad sector coverage and standardized cross-national methodology make it especially suitable for comparative analyses of workplace safety practices. This record refers to the same underlying survey as the UK Data Service and GESIS entries, rather than an independent sample.

returned_title: European Survey of Enterprises on New and Emerging Risks, 2014 (ESENER-2) — EU-OSHA Official Survey Portal
justification: Official EU-OSHA landing page for the 2014 ESENER-2 survey. Provides access routes to the underlying dataset and related survey documentation and findings. Particularly relevant for investigating how European establishments identify, assess, and manage occupational risks, including stress, harassment, workplace violence, repetitive movements, physically demanding work, and musculoskeletal hazards. Also supports analysis of employee consultation, workplace safety representation, organizational prevention measures, and factors encouraging or obstructing OSH management. Covers all 36 target countries and is an authoritative starting point for understanding the survey's methodology and comparative research applications.

returned_title: European Survey of Enterprises on New and Emerging Risks (ESENER) — EU-OSHA Interactive Results Dataset
justification: Official interactive data platform providing comparative results from successive ESENER survey waves, including 2014 and 2019. Enables exploration of occupational safety and health management, emerging psychosocial risks, organizational drivers and barriers, and worker participation. Researchers can compare results by country, economic sector, and establishment size. Particularly useful for preliminary analysis, identifying cross-national differences, exploring workplace prevention practices, and contextualizing establishment-level findings. The 2014 wave includes all 36 requested countries. The platform primarily provides aggregated survey results rather than unrestricted establishment-level microdata.

returned_title: Third European Survey of Enterprises on New and Emerging Risks, 2019 (ESENER-3) — EU-OSHA
justification: Highly relevant complementary dataset collected in 2019, allowing comparisons with the 2014 ESENER-2 survey. ESENER-3 interviewed approximately 45,420 establishments across 33 European countries, covering establishments with at least five employees. It investigates occupational safety and health management, psychosocial risks such as work-related stress, violence and harassment, worker participation, risk prevention, and organizational drivers and barriers. Particularly valuable for examining changes in establishment-level OSH practices during the 2010s. Its questionnaire and methodology were designed to maintain substantial comparability with ESENER-2. However, its geographical coverage differs from the 2014 wave, so it does not provide complete coverage of all 36 requested countries.

returned_title: European Survey of Enterprises on New and Emerging Risks, 2009 (ESENER-1) — EU-OSHA
justification: Relevant historical baseline for studying developments in European occupational safety and health management during the 2010s. Conducted in 2009, ESENER-1 involved approximately 36,000 interviews with managers and occupational safety and health representatives across 31 countries. It examines workplace safety policies, psychosocial risks, stress, violence, harassment, employee participation, and organizational factors affecting risk management. Although its fieldwork predates the requested decade, it provides valuable baseline information for comparison with the 2014 and 2019 waves. Coverage is narrower than ESENER-2, and the survey focused on establishments with at least ten employees. It is therefore best suited to longitudinal comparisons using harmonized country and establishment-size samples.

returned_title: EU-OSHA Occupational Safety and Health Barometer — European OSH Indicators and Survey Data
justification: Useful supplementary European occupational safety and health data resource integrating indicators from surveys, statistics, and public administrative sources, including information extending back to 2010. Covers workplace risks, working conditions, occupational health outcomes, prevention policies, and national OSH systems. Its country-level indicators can contextualize findings from ESENER-2 by examining differences in regulatory environments, occupational safety outcomes, and prevention frameworks. Particularly valuable for constructing contextual country-level measures to accompany establishment-level survey analyses. Unlike ESENER-2, this resource is primarily an aggregated indicator platform rather than a single establishment-level microdata survey.

returned_title: Familienplanung als gesundheitliche Aufgabe (Family Planning as a Health Task, 1972) — GESIS ZA0682
justification: Excellent match and the strongest recommendation for this research need. This West German representative survey, conducted by Infratest for the Federal Centre for Health Education (BZgA), examines attitudes toward family planning, contraception, abortion, sexuality, and women's changing roles. Topics include ideal family size, fertility intentions, desired children, contraceptive use and effectiveness, knowledge of the birth control pill, sterilization, abortion attitudes, acceptable reasons for terminating pregnancies, awareness of abortion legislation, and opinions about proposed reforms to Paragraph 218 of the German Criminal Code. It also investigates physician visits, family planning counseling services, sexual morality, and perceptions of women's autonomy through reproductive control. Demographic variables explicitly include age, sex, marital status, number and ages of children, religious denomination, education, vocational training, occupation, employment status, occupational position, household income, household size, and household composition. This dataset closely matches virtually every specified research requirement and is particularly valuable for analyzing reproductive attitudes during West Germany's early 1970s abortion reform debates.

returned_title: Ehe und Familie (Marriage and Family, 1977) — GESIS ZA0968
justification: Relevant supplementary survey conducted by EMNID in West Germany between February and March 1977. Examines attitudes toward marriage, family life, desired number of children, fertility decline, childlessness, divorce, family relationships, and gender roles within marriage. It also addresses sexual education, parenting, family counseling services, and expectations surrounding family responsibilities. Particularly useful for examining how attitudes toward fertility, marriage, and women's social roles evolved following the major reproductive rights and family law debates of the early 1970s. Its coverage of contraception and abortion legislation is less direct than that of ZA0682, but it provides valuable contextual evidence about family norms and fertility intentions.

returned_title: Das sexuelle Verhalten von Männern und Frauen in Deutschland (Sexual Behavior of Men and Women in Germany, 1970–1972)
justification: Highly relevant historical survey material covering sexual behavior and the social and economic circumstances of men and women in West Germany. The surveys were conducted by GETAS, with a female-focused wave in 1970–1971 and a male-focused wave in 1972. They used multistage stratified probability sampling of German citizens aged 18–60 living in private households. Their coverage of sexual behavior and social position makes them useful for investigating changing sexual norms, gender differences, and reproductive behavior during the early 1970s. The linked GESIS documentation describes these surveys as constituent sources for a harmonized reproductive research dataset. It is especially relevant for comparative analyses by age and sex, although the precise availability of individual contraception, abortion, and counseling variables should be checked in the underlying documentation.

returned_title: Familienplanung als gesundheitliche Aufgabe — BZgA Historical Study Archive (1973)
justification: Official historical study archive maintained by Germany's federal public health education institution. This 1973 publication documents research undertaken by Infratest on family planning as a preventive health measure aimed at reducing unintended pregnancies and abortions. The study applies factor analysis and population segmentation to representative survey data to identify target groups for family planning education. It is particularly valuable for understanding how reproductive attitudes, contraceptive knowledge, and demographic differences informed public health policy during the early 1970s. The archive provides historical documentation and an appendix, making it a useful companion to the GESIS ZA0682 dataset rather than an independent survey.

returned_title: Politbarometer 1977–2024 (Partial Cumulation) — GESIS ZA2391
justification: Supplementary longitudinal public opinion dataset containing historical West German survey observations beginning in 1977. Includes questions on public attitudes toward abortion and the legal conditions under which pregnancy termination should be permitted. Particularly useful for examining public acceptance of abortion restrictions and changes in opinion following the legislative reforms of the mid-1970s. Its repeated survey design supports comparisons over time and analyses of political and demographic differences. However, its coverage of contraceptive behavior, physician counseling, and fertility intentions is substantially narrower than that of ZA0682. Researchers should verify the availability of specific abortion questions in the 1977–1979 waves because individual questions were not necessarily asked every year.

returned_title: Frauenstudie 1984 (Women Study 1984) — GDR
justification: Excellent match. Conducted in 1984 by the Central Institute for Youth Research (ZIJ) in Leipzig, this survey examines the living and working conditions of young women in the GDR, particularly in the Erfurt and Karl-Marx-Stadt districts. The dataset contains 1,635 observations and 519 variables, covering women's employment, occupational demands, shift work, household responsibilities, childcare, fertility intentions, partnership quality, gender equality, housing conditions, finances, leisure activities, and work-family balance. It also investigates decision-making within relationships, male dominance, division of household labor, and conflicts surrounding gender equality. Questionnaires were administered to young women, their partners, and some of their mothers, making this particularly valuable for studying gender roles and intergenerational differences in family life during the 1980s.

returned_title: Partner II 1979/80 — Sexuality, Partnership and Reproductive Health in the GDR
justification: Excellent match for reproductive health, menstruation, contraception, fertility, sexual relationships, and partnership quality. Conducted between autumn 1979 and autumn 1980 by the Central Institute for Youth Research and Karl Marx University Leipzig, this representative survey includes 5,448 young workers, apprentices, and university students in the GDR. Its 376 variables address age at menarche, contraceptive knowledge and use, first sexual intercourse, sexual experiences, sexual difficulties, sexual satisfaction, romantic relationships, partner characteristics, marriage attitudes, fertility preferences, and abortion experiences among student respondents. Additional information includes occupational satisfaction, shift work, income, leisure activities, family background, and relationship expectations. The survey is particularly useful for studying women's sexual and reproductive experiences at the beginning of the 1980s.

returned_title: Partner III — Employed 1990
justification: Strong complementary dataset for studying reproductive health, sexuality, employment, and partnerships at the end of the GDR period. Conducted between April and June 1990, before German reunification, this representative survey includes 876 employed respondents aged up to 44 and contains 319 variables. Topics include sexual behavior, relationship expectations, occupational conditions, physical and psychological stress at work, effects of partnership and children on occupational achievement, and personal well-being. It also addresses sexuality and health concerns in the context of AIDS. Particularly useful for comparison with the 1979/80 Partner II survey to investigate changes in sexual relationships, reproductive attitudes, and work-family experiences across the 1980s. Its collection date is 1990 rather than the 1980s.

returned_title: Arbeits- und Lebensbedingungen Jugendlicher in Dresden 1984 (Working and Living Conditions of Young People in Dresden 1984)
justification: Relevant supplementary survey conducted in Dresden in 1984. It examines young people's living conditions, housing, residential mobility intentions, occupational attitudes, characteristics of employment, job satisfaction, and social and political orientations. This dataset can support research on women's housing situations, employment experiences, and socioeconomic circumstances in an urban GDR setting. It is less directly focused on reproductive health and intimate relationships than Frauenstudie 1984. The URL points to a repository results page containing the dataset rather than a dedicated study landing page.

returned_title: Komplexstudie 1984 (Complex Study 1984)
justification: Relevant for investigating everyday living conditions, work, leisure, and social attitudes among young people in the GDR during 1984. The survey covers housing, occupational and leisure activities, and broader life circumstances. It provides useful contextual information for examining how employment and living conditions shaped the experiences of young women during the 1980s. Its relevance to menstruation, contraception, violence, and reproductive health is limited. The supplied URL is a repository results page listing the study.

returned_title: Kultur und wissenschaftlich-technischer Fortschritt 1988 (Culture and Scientific-Technological Progress 1988)
justification: Useful supplementary dataset collected in 1988, particularly for research concerning employment, leisure, housing, and social relationships in the late GDR. Topics include leisure interests, use of recreational facilities, housing conditions, occupational requirements, and interpersonal relationships within workplaces. These variables can help investigate women's everyday activities, working environments, and opportunities for recreation. It is not specifically a women's health or reproductive health survey, but it offers relevant socioeconomic context. The URL identifies a repository results page containing the study.

returned_title: Jugend und Sport 1987 (Young People and Sport 1987)
justification: Relevant for the health, leisure, sport, and employment dimensions of the research. Conducted in 1987, the study investigates sporting activities, attitudes toward physical exercise, and participation in mass sports in relation to employment and education. It also includes a supplementary questionnaire addressing respondents' health status. This makes it a potentially useful source for studying physical well-being and leisure among young women in the GDR. However, it does not directly address menstruation, contraception, intimate relationships, or household labor. The URL leads to a repository results page listing the dataset.

returned_title: Leben in der ehemaligen DDR (Life in the Former GDR) — Retrospective Survey 2018
justification: Useful retrospective supplement for reconstructing everyday life in the GDR, including experiences during the 1980s. This research resource combines historical material relating to citizens' grievances between 1970 and 1989 with a retrospective survey of former GDR citizens conducted in 2018. It provides evidence concerning living conditions, social experiences, and participation in public life under socialism. It may help contextualize women's housing, finances, family circumstances, and institutional experiences, although coverage of specific reproductive-health variables is not established. Because the survey was conducted decades after the events being studied, retrospective recall must be considered when interpreting results.

returned_title: Attitudes Toward Sexuality and AIDS, 1988 (Einstellungen zu Sexualität und AIDS, 1988) — GESIS ZA1818
justification: Highly relevant survey dataset from West Germany in 1988, archived by GESIS under study number ZA1818. Investigates attitudes toward sexuality and AIDS, including the influence of the AIDS epidemic on sexual attitudes and behavior. Particularly suitable for examining sexual norms, perceived HIV risks, and changes in sexual practices in response to AIDS. One of the closest matches to the requested research themes.

returned_title: Living Together: Sexual Behavior, 1988 (Das Leben zu zweit – Sexualverhalten 1988) — GESIS ZA1798
justification: West German survey from 1988 focusing on sexual behavior and intimate relationships, archived under GESIS study number ZA1798. Particularly relevant to partnership dynamics, sexuality within relationships, and the effects of AIDS on sexual behavior. The study is explicitly identified in GESIS archival documentation as containing questions about the influence of AIDS on respondents' sexual lives. Strong match for research combining reproductive health, partnership behavior, and changing sexual practices.

returned_title: AIDS in Public Awareness, April 1987 (AIDS im öffentlichen Bewusstsein) — GESIS ZA1758
justification: Nationally representative telephone survey conducted by FORSA for the German Federal Centre for Health Education (BZgA) in April 1987. Covers public knowledge about AIDS, perceived infection risks, attitudes toward people living with HIV, and willingness to adopt protective measures. Provides valuable baseline data for examining public reactions to AIDS in West Germany during the 1980s. Can be compared with the corresponding 1988 survey to investigate changes in knowledge, attitudes, and preventive behavior.

returned_title: AIDS in Public Awareness, July–August 1988 (AIDS im öffentlichen Bewusstsein) — GESIS ZA1757
justification: Representative West German telephone survey conducted by FORSA for BZgA in July–August 1988. Includes questions concerning AIDS awareness, transmission knowledge, personal risk perceptions, preventive measures, and attitudes toward HIV-infected individuals. Uses many questions identical or comparable to those administered in 1987, making it especially useful for studying changes in AIDS knowledge and protective attitudes during the late 1980s. Relevant to research on condom-related prevention, sexual health awareness, and behavioral responses to AIDS.

returned_title: German General Social Survey (ALLBUS), Cumulative Data 1980–2010
justification: Major longitudinal collection of repeated cross-sectional surveys covering Germany from 1980 onward. Includes measures of AIDS knowledge, perceptions of infection risks, attitudes toward HIV-infected individuals, personal protective measures, and AIDS-related behavioral changes in relevant survey years. Also contains extensive information about marriage, family relationships, religious affiliation, religious participation, moral values, and attitudes toward sexuality and abortion. Particularly useful for connecting AIDS-related attitudes and preventive behavior with family structures, religion, and broader social values during the 1980s. Researchers should select the relevant 1980s waves and verify which questions were administered in each year.

returned_title: Student Sexuality, 1981 (Studentensexualität 1981) — GESIS ZA1710
justification: West German university student survey conducted during the 1980–1981 winter semester, containing 1,923 respondents and 196 variables. Examines sexual experiences, masturbation, homosexual contacts, extramarital sexual relationships, attitudes toward homosexuality, and abortion. Includes questions about sexual norms and reproductive health. Particularly valuable for establishing a pre-AIDS baseline of sexual attitudes and behavior among young adults. Although it predates widespread AIDS awareness and does not directly address HIV testing or AIDS-related behavioral changes, it supports historical comparisons with surveys conducted later in the decade.

returned_title: German General Social Survey (ALLBUS): AIDS and HIV Questions
justification: Official GESIS documentation identifying HIV/AIDS-related questions within ALLBUS surveys. Relevant measures include knowledge about AIDS, perceptions of infection risk, personal protective measures, and behavioral responses to the epidemic. Provides a means of identifying relevant variables and survey years before accessing the underlying ALLBUS datasets. Particularly useful for researchers seeking to combine AIDS-related measures with demographic characteristics, marriage, family life, religious affiliation, and social values. This is a variable documentation resource rather than a separate survey dataset.

returned_title: European Values Study (EVS), Germany, 1981
justification: German component of the European Values Study, with an initial survey wave in 1981. Covers attitudes toward family, marriage, religion, morality, sexuality-related values, and the importance of relationships and family life. Especially valuable for investigating how religious and traditional values shaped views about marriage, sexuality, and reproductive choices in early-1980s West Germany. Does not directly measure AIDS-related sexual behavior but provides important historical and cultural context for interpreting changes in attitudes during the AIDS epidemic. The linked GESIS record concerns a German EVS dataset spanning multiple waves.

returned_title: International Social Survey Programme (ISSP): Family and Changing Gender Roles I, 1988
justification: International comparative survey module conducted in 1988, including data from West Germany. Examines attitudes toward marriage, family roles, household responsibilities, women's employment, parenthood, and gender relations. Relevant to understanding the social and ideological context of sexual partnerships and family formation during the late 1980s. Particularly useful for studying relationships between family values, traditional gender expectations, and attitudes toward intimate partnerships. Does not directly cover condom use, AIDS testing, or prostitution contacts.

returned_title: Partner III: Homosexuality, 1990 (Partner III – Homosexualität 1990) — GESIS ZA6057
justification: Detailed East German survey addressing homosexual identities, same-sex relationships, sexual experiences, contraceptive practices, partnership structures, family background, attitudes toward children, and AIDS awareness. Includes questions concerning perceived AIDS threats and personal changes in sexual contacts in response to the epidemic. Also investigates family climate, parental relationships, sexual attitudes within families, and experiences of discrimination. Although collected in 1990 rather than the 1980s, it is especially valuable as a closely adjacent historical comparison and covers several highly specific themes requested, including homosexuality, partnership dynamics, sexual behavior, AIDS knowledge, and behavioral adaptation.

returned_title: AIDS in Public Awareness: Historical Survey Series Beginning in 1987 (Aids im öffentlichen Bewusstsein)
justification: Historical documentation of the BZgA representative survey series that began in West Germany in 1987. Includes longitudinal indicators concerning sexual contacts with unfamiliar partners, perceived AIDS risks, condom use, and HIV-prevention behavior. Historical tables provide observations from the late 1980s onward, allowing analysis of changes in sexual practices and preventive behavior. Particularly relevant for studying how the AIDS epidemic influenced sexual risk perceptions and condom adoption. The linked resource provides historical survey results rather than an individual-level microdata download.

returned_title: Guns and Colonists, 1773–1775 [United States] (ICPSR 3573)
justification: Excellent match and the most directly relevant dataset. Created by James Oberly and Benjamin Tausig, this dataset contains information from 919 probate inventories across 21 colonial counties, including Massachusetts and South Carolina. Variables include firearm ownership, number of firearms, firearm types, weapon values, edged weapons, number of enslaved people and servants, decedent age, and probate inventory date. It can be linked to Alice Hanson Jones's American Colonial Wealth Estimates dataset (ICPSR 7329) to incorporate estate wealth and geographic information. Particularly useful for comparing firearm ownership immediately before the American Revolutionary War.

returned_title: American Colonial Wealth Estimates, 1774 (ICPSR 7329)
justification: Excellent complementary dataset for studying firearm ownership in relation to wealth, geography, and slaveholding. Compiled by economic historian Alice Hanson Jones, this collection contains probate-based wealth information for 919 deceased individuals from 21 colonial counties, including Massachusetts and South Carolina. It includes estate valuations, demographic information, geographic identifiers, and detailed classifications of property. The collection includes 24 data files. Its greatest value is that it provides the underlying economic and demographic context for the Guns and Colonists, 1773–1775 dataset, allowing researchers to investigate relationships between firearm possession, estate value, location, and slaveholding.

returned_title: Colonial New England Probates, 1631–1776 (ICPSR 34940)
justification: Highly relevant for investigating firearm ownership and estate wealth in eighteenth-century Massachusetts, particularly during the 1730s through 1770s. Compiled by Gloria Main, Jackson Main, and Peter Lindert, this dataset contains information from 18,509 probate estates in Massachusetts, Connecticut, and New Hampshire. Variables include estate inventory values, personal wealth, debts, landholdings, county, town, age, sex, occupation, marital status, and parental status. It provides an extensive demographic and economic foundation for studying regional differences and changes over time. However, firearm types and counts are not established as standardized variables in the dataset description, so additional inventory-level research may be necessary.

returned_title: South Carolina, Charleston District, Estate Inventories, 1732–1844
justification: Excellent primary-source collection covering the complete requested period from the 1730s through the 1790s. This FamilySearch collection, developed with the South Carolina Department of Archives and History and Lowcountry Africana, contains historical estate inventories and appraisements from the Charleston District. Records can include the deceased person's name, residence, estate inventory, property descriptions, and valuations. Particularly valuable for identifying firearms, firearm types, quantities, estate wealth, and enslaved people listed as property. Researchers can extract firearm counts and compare ownership across colonial, Revolutionary War, and postwar periods. The collection consists primarily of historical records rather than a standardized firearm-ownership dataset, so manual transcription or additional coding may be required.

returned_title: Massachusetts, Plymouth County, Probate Records, 1633–1967
justification: Relevant primary-source collection containing historical probate records for Plymouth County, Massachusetts, including the entire 1730–1799 research period. Probate documents can be examined for estate inventories listing guns, muskets, pistols, and other weapons, along with quantities and appraised values. Estate records also provide information for identifying decedents and examining household wealth. Particularly useful for constructing a longitudinal firearm-ownership dataset spanning the colonial period, French and Indian War, American Revolution, and early republic. Firearm information must generally be extracted from original documents rather than downloaded as standardized analytical variables.

returned_title: Massachusetts, Plymouth County, Probate Estate Files, 1686–1915
justification: Useful complementary primary-source collection for researching eighteenth-century Massachusetts firearm ownership. Contains individual probate estate files spanning the requested decades, allowing investigation of itemized personal property and estate valuations. Researchers can examine original estate documents to identify firearms, distinguish weapon types where recorded, count guns, and connect ownership patterns with decedent characteristics and economic circumstances. Particularly relevant for comparing pre-Revolutionary, Revolutionary, and post-Revolutionary probate inventories within a consistent county. This is a historical records collection, not a pre-coded firearm ownership dataset.

returned_title: Massachusetts, Wills and Deeds, circa 1700–2017
justification: Supplementary Massachusetts historical records collection that includes probate-related materials from the eighteenth century. Potentially useful for identifying decedents, locating associated estate documents, and reconstructing family property ownership during the 1730s through 1790s. Wills and related records may mention firearms, personal possessions, and property transfers. The collection is most useful for supplementing probate inventories with contextual information about estate ownership and inheritance. Coverage and the availability of itemized firearm information vary by record.

returned_title: Probate Records of South Carolina, Volume 1: An Index to Inventories, 1746–1785
justification: Relevant historical probate inventory index covering South Carolina from 1746 through 1785, including the French and Indian War, the American Revolution, and surrounding peacetime periods. Particularly useful for locating probate inventories and identifying deceased estate owners whose records can subsequently be examined for firearms, weapon quantities, enslaved people, and property valuations. The index can support systematic selection of estates for longitudinal research. It is a published finding aid rather than a machine-readable dataset containing firearm counts.

returned_title: Historic Massachusetts Probate Records — Massachusetts Court Archives
justification: Official Massachusetts government resource describing access to historical probate books and original probate case files, including estate inventories. Particularly useful for locating county-level records from the 1730s through the 1790s that may not be included in existing analytical datasets. Original inventories can provide detailed descriptions of firearms, quantities, valuations, and other household property. County-specific probate records also support comparisons between Boston-area estates, coastal communities, and inland settlements. This is an archival access resource rather than a single downloadable dataset.

returned_title: Probing the Past: Virginia and Maryland Probate Inventories, 1740–1810
justification: Useful comparative dataset and methodological reference for studying eighteenth-century firearm ownership through probate inventories. Developed through the Gunston Hall probate inventory project, it covers Virginia and Maryland estates from 1740 to 1810. Although it does not directly cover Massachusetts or South Carolina, its itemized probate data can help researchers develop consistent coding approaches for firearms, household possessions, and estate characteristics. It also provides a southern colonial comparison group for examining regional variation and historical changes across wartime and peacetime periods.

returned_title: A Survey of Europe Today (Finland), 1969 — GESIS ZA1296
justification: Excellent match and the most directly relevant dataset. Conducted between January and March 1969, this Reader's Digest survey focuses specifically on Finland and forms part of a comparative study covering 16 European countries. It examines household consumer behavior, ownership and acquisition of durable goods, household furnishings, perceived economic conditions, standards of living, attitudes toward foreign products, and opinions about the European Economic Community (EEC). The broader questionnaire covers automobile ownership and use, leisure activities, tourism, drinking habits, advertising, media consumption, reading, education, and socio-demographic characteristics. Its subject classifications exactly match all seven requested categories, making it the strongest dataset for the research need.

returned_title: Reader's Digest Survey of Europe Today, 1969 — International Comparative Dataset
justification: Excellent match for cross-national comparisons involving Finland during the 1960s. This international survey collected information on ownership and use of more than 200 consumer goods and services across 16 Western European countries. Topics include household composition, income, education, housing, appliances, food and alcoholic beverage consumption, television viewing, reading, leisure activities, automobile ownership, holidays, travel, fashion, advertising, and attitudes toward European integration and the Common Market. It also contains questions about social tolerance, family relationships, national identity, and perceptions of other European countries. Particularly useful for comparing Finnish households with households elsewhere in Europe. The archived dataset has restricted access.

returned_title: Reader's Digest Survey of Europe Today, 1969 — B2FIND International Survey Record
justification: Highly relevant alternative archive record for the 1969 international Reader's Digest survey, explicitly identifying Finland among the participating countries. The survey was designed to compare consumer markets, purchasing behavior, ownership of consumer goods, and social attitudes across Western Europe.
