It covers household possessions, automobile ownership, tourism, leisure activities, media, advertising, economic circumstances, and social characteristics. It is especially valuable for locating the multinational version of the survey and investigating differences between Finnish respondents and respondents in other European countries. This record refers to the same underlying 1969 survey as the international DANS record, rather than an independent data collection.

returned_title: Statistics Finland Household Budget Survey — Households' Consumption, 1966
justification: Strong supplementary dataset for examining Finnish household consumption during the 1960s. Statistics Finland's household budget survey series includes a nationally representative survey conducted in 1966. It provides information on household expenditure, income, ownership of durable goods, housing conditions, and socio-economic characteristics. Consumption categories include food, beverages, tobacco, clothing, housing, furnishings, transportation, culture, leisure, education, and hospitality. The 1966 observations offer valuable historical context for understanding Finnish consumer behavior before the 1969 Reader's Digest survey. However, this dataset is less suitable for studying attitudes toward the EEC, advertising, and European integration because its primary focus is household expenditure rather than social attitudes.

returned_title: Finland Household Consumption Survey Series, 1966–2006 — Eurostat CROS
justification: Relevant historical dataset series documenting household consumption patterns in Finland, beginning in 1966. The survey examines household spending, durable goods ownership, living conditions, income, and differences in consumption across population groups. Its coverage of transportation, household equipment, food, beverages, leisure, and economic circumstances makes it useful for investigating consumer lifestyles in Finland during the late 1960s. The series also supports comparisons with subsequent surveys conducted in 1971 and later years. It is particularly suitable for studying changes in consumption and living standards over time, although it does not provide the same breadth of questions about advertising, media, and attitudes toward the EEC as the Reader's Digest survey.

returned_title: Hochschulausbildung und Beruf (College Education and Profession) — GESIS Dataset, ZA1458
justification: Excellent match for the research need. This historical dataset examines graduates of the University of Munich and the Technical University of Munich who completed their studies in 1972. The survey was conducted in May–June 1975, making it directly relevant to employment and higher education in Bavaria during the 1970s. It provides individual-level information on university graduates and their transition from higher education into professional life. Its subject matter aligns closely with the requested investigation of educational backgrounds, study experiences, social origins, employment outcomes, and professional careers. The dataset was produced by Walter Hornstein and Georg Kärtner, with the German Youth Institute in Munich (Deutsches Jugendinstitut) identified as a contributing institution. It is archived by GESIS and classified under employment, higher education, and university research. This is the strongest identified dataset because its geographical coverage, graduate population, and historical period match the research requirements precisely. Access is restricted to academic research and teaching and requires written authorization from the data depositor. The detailed variable documentation should be consulted to confirm coverage of employer expectations, income, career prospects, and life and job satisfaction.

returned_title: Absolventenpanel 1979 (Graduate Panel 1979) — GESIS Dataset, ZA5185
justification: Relevant complementary dataset examining university graduates' educational experiences, professional orientations, and transitions into employment. Data collection took place between 1979 and 1984. The survey covers attitudes toward university education, academic careers, professional work, gender roles, social inequality, personal values, and expectations concerning employment. Participants were drawn from several academic disciplines, including medicine, economics, natural sciences, engineering, and modern languages. It is particularly useful for studying graduates' professional aspirations, perceptions of employment, and the relationship between university education and occupational expectations. However, its geographical coverage is not confirmed as specific to Munich or Bavaria, and part of the collection period extends into the 1980s. It is therefore a secondary match rather than a direct substitute for the Munich graduate dataset.

returned_title: Abiturienten-Follow-up 1976/77 (Abiturientenpanel) — Graduate Panel
justification: Historical longitudinal education dataset relevant to the transition from secondary schooling into university studies and professional life during the 1970s. It includes information on educational expectations, university admission, perceptions of academic requirements, intended fields of study, professional goals, anticipated earnings, social status, and expectations concerning graduates' labor-market opportunities. The dataset is valuable for analyzing school backgrounds, educational aspirations, academic trajectories, and early career expectations. It can provide contextual evidence for understanding the educational pathways of the generation entering higher education during the 1970s. However, it is not specifically restricted to Munich university graduates or Bavarian institutions, and its coverage of actual employment conditions, earnings, and job satisfaction is less directly established than that of a graduate employment survey.

returned_title: Politbarometer 1977–2024 (Partial Cumulation) (ZA2391)
justification: Highly relevant longitudinal survey dataset covering Germany throughout the 1990s, including the Federal Republic's 50th anniversary in 1999. Contains public attitudes toward democracy, satisfaction with the political system, government performance, party preferences, voting intentions, political expectations, economic conditions, and demographic characteristics. Includes separate East and West German samples for relevant periods, enabling analysis of political attitudes following reunification.

returned_title: German General Social Survey (ALLBUS) – Cumulation 1980–2014 (ZA4584)
justification: Comprehensive survey dataset covering political attitudes, social conditions, and demographic characteristics in Germany during the 1990s. Includes satisfaction with democracy, evaluations of political system performance, trust in government, political participation, party preferences, economic expectations, and subjective well-being. Particularly useful for examining changes in attitudes between East and West Germany following reunification and assessing the social and political climate around 1999.

returned_title: Political Attitudes, Political Participation and Voting Behavior in Reunified Germany 1994 (ZA3065)
justification: Directly relevant survey examining political attitudes and electoral behavior in reunified Germany during the 1990s. Includes satisfaction with democracy, assessments of economic conditions, expectations about future economic developments, party preferences, political trust, perceptions of political representation, and evaluations of the German political system. Also investigates differences between East and West Germans, making it valuable for studying reunification and democratic consolidation.

returned_title: Political Attitudes, Political Participation and Voting Behavior in Reunified Germany (Panel 1998–2005) (ZA4662)
justification: Particularly relevant because the panel begins in 1998 and extends across Germany's 50th anniversary in 1999. Provides longitudinal data on political attitudes, electoral behavior, party preferences, and political participation in reunified Germany. Its panel structure allows researchers to investigate individual-level changes in political orientations and expectations during the transition from the late 1990s into the early 2000s.

returned_title: Election Study 1998 (Politbarometer)
justification: Highly relevant survey conducted immediately before the Federal Republic's 50th anniversary. Covers satisfaction with democracy, party preferences, electoral expectations, government performance, political leadership, economic prospects, and attitudes toward German reunification. Also includes extensive demographic information such as age, gender, education, employment, household composition, and political identification. Especially useful for establishing the political context of the 1999 anniversary.

returned_title: ARD-DeutschlandTrend 1998 (ZA4590)
justification: Representative public opinion survey covering political attitudes in Germany immediately before the 1999 anniversary. Examines party preferences, evaluations of politicians, and attitudes toward contemporary political issues. Provides a useful complementary source for investigating public assessments of government, electoral preferences, and political expectations during the late 1990s.

returned_title: Attitudes to Current Questions of Domestic Policy (1995) (ZA2625)
justification: Relevant survey of German public opinion concerning domestic politics, democratic institutions, and political system performance during the post-reunification period. Includes satisfaction with democracy, party preferences, previous voting behavior, trust in public institutions, and evaluations of economic and social conditions. Provides valuable mid-1990s baseline data for comparisons with attitudes around 1999.

returned_title: Attitudes on Foreign and Security Policy in the Federal Republic (ZA2980)
justification: Relevant three-wave panel survey containing measures of satisfaction with democracy, party preference, voting intentions, assessments of personal and national economic conditions, and expectations about future economic developments. Particularly useful for analyzing attitudes toward reunification because respondents evaluate changes in economic circumstances since German unification and compare conditions in eastern and western Germany.

returned_title: System of Social Indicators for the Federal Republic of Germany: Participation (ZA8649)
justification: Historical social indicators dataset covering political participation and social change in Germany from 1950 to 2013, including the entire 1990s. Useful for contextualizing survey findings around the Federal Republic's 50th anniversary within longer-term developments in political participation, democratic institutions, and social conditions. It is an indicator dataset rather than a dedicated individual-level opinion survey.

returned_title: Growing Up in Germany: Everyday Life (Aufwachsen in Deutschland: Alltagswelten – AID:A), 2009
justification: Very strong thematic match. This German youth and family survey includes adolescents aged 13–17 and examines future life plans, educational and occupational aspirations, leisure activities, financial resources, family relationships, social participation, and migration background. Variables include desired occupations, plans after leaving school, preferred qualifications, importance of different life domains, monthly disposable income, civic responsibilities, friendships, and parental relationships. School type is recorded, potentially allowing identification of special-school students. The 2009 survey provides a baseline immediately preceding the 2010s. However, the availability of a sufficiently large subgroup attending special schools for emotional and social development requires verification.

returned_title: National Educational Panel Study (NEPS), Starting Cohort 4: Grade 9, 2010/2011
justification: Strong match for adolescents attending special schools and their educational and occupational futures. Starting Cohort 4 began in the 2010/2011 school year and includes ninth-grade students attending mainstream schools and students with special educational needs in learning at special schools. It investigates educational aspirations, vocational transitions, social background, migration characteristics, and subsequent educational and employment pathways. The dataset incorporates follow-up information from the FÖS2 project concerning former special-school students. Its main limitation is that the special-school sample focuses on learning difficulties rather than specifically emotional and social development.

returned_title: National Educational Panel Study (NEPS), Starting Cohort 3: Grade 5, 2010/2011
justification: Relevant longitudinal dataset following German adolescents who entered fifth grade in 2010/2011. It includes educational trajectories, aspirations, family and socioeconomic background, migration characteristics, and school experiences. Students with special educational needs were included during the early survey waves, making this dataset potentially useful for comparing educational expectations across school settings. Special-needs students were not followed throughout the entire longitudinal study, and the availability of a distinct emotional and social development subgroup needs verification.

returned_title: Socio-Economic Panel (SOEP-Core), 1984–2019, International Edition
justification: Excellent thematic match for adolescents' future life plans, particularly through the youth questionnaires administered to 16–17-year-olds during the 2010s. The 2019 questionnaire covers relationships, friendships, leisure, sports, education, vocational plans, future expectations, employment, money, attitudes, and self-perceptions. Household-level information adds parental education, income, family composition, and migration background. This allows investigation of relationships between socioeconomic circumstances and adolescents' aspirations. However, special-school attendance and emotional or social development needs may not be identifiable with sufficient precision.

returned_title: Socio-Economic Panel (SOEP-Core), 1984–2018, Version 35
justification: Relevant nationally representative longitudinal dataset containing youth interviews throughout the 2010s. The youth questionnaire addresses education, occupational plans, family relationships, leisure activities, social attitudes, and personal expectations. Household information provides financial resources, parental occupations, educational backgrounds, and migration characteristics. The dataset is useful for examining how social disadvantage and family circumstances influence adolescents' aspirations. It offers a valuable comparison population, although it does not specifically target special schools for emotional and social development.

returned_title: National Educational Panel Study (NEPS), Starting Cohort 4: Grade 9, 2010/2011, Version 16.0.0
justification: An expanded release of the longitudinal study of ninth-grade students initially surveyed in 2010/2011, including students from special schools with a focus on learning. Particularly valuable for investigating whether educational and occupational aspirations expressed during adolescence correspond to later educational qualifications and employment outcomes. The study includes demographic, family, and migration-related characteristics. Its longitudinal design makes it useful for researching transitions into adult life. However, the special-school sample does not specifically represent students with emotional and social development needs.

returned_title: National Educational Panel Study (NEPS), Starting Cohort 4: Grade 9, 2010/2011, Version 10.0.0
justification: A dataset release from 2019 containing longitudinal information on adolescents who entered ninth grade in 2010/2011. It is relevant for analyzing educational aspirations, occupational expectations, school-to-work transitions, demographic background, and migration characteristics during the 2010s. The sample includes students attending special schools with a learning focus, providing a useful comparison group for research on adolescents with special educational needs. The dataset does not specifically target emotional and social development.

returned_title: Students Receiving Special Educational Support in Germany, by School Year, School Type and Special Educational Needs (GENESIS-Online, Table 21111-0007)
justification: Highly relevant for identifying the target population. This official German education statistics dataset distinguishes special educational needs categories, including emotional and social development (Emotionale und soziale Entwicklung), and provides information by school year and school type. It supports analysis of the size and distribution of the relevant special-school population during the 2010s. Although it does not measure individual aspirations, family plans, leisure preferences, or civic participation, it provides essential contextual data for evaluating the representativeness of survey samples.

returned_title: Students Receiving Special Educational Support in Germany, by School Year, Gender, School Type and Special Educational Needs (GENESIS-Online, Table 21111-0008)
justification: Strong contextual match because it explicitly identifies pupils receiving special educational support in emotional and social development. The dataset provides information by gender, school type, and school year, with coverage beginning in the 2014/2015 academic year. It can be used to establish the demographic composition of the target population and compare special-school enrollment patterns across the 2010s. It does not contain individual-level information about future plans, migration background, family aspirations, financial expectations, or leisure activities.

returned_title: Socio-Economic Panel (SOEP-Core), 1984–2019, EU Edition
justification: A relevant alternative edition of the German Socio-Economic Panel covering the entire 2010s. It contains youth questionnaires addressing occupational plans, education, expectations, relationships, leisure, and social attitudes. Its longitudinal household structure allows adolescents' responses to be linked to parental socioeconomic characteristics, household finances, and migration background. This makes it useful for analyzing inequalities in future aspirations and family-related expectations. It is best suited to comparative analysis rather than identifying a specific sample of adolescents attending special schools for emotional and social development.

returned_title: Duisburger Bürgerumfrage – Frühjahr 2000 (Duisburg Citizen Survey, Spring 2000)
justification: Excellent match. This GESIS survey covers Duisburg residents aged 18–75 and directly addresses community life, housing, cultural participation, political attitudes, and municipal government. It is particularly relevant for investigating residential satisfaction, perceptions of local living conditions, cultural facilities, political preferences, and demographic differences among residents. Conducted in February–March 2000, it provides an early-2000s baseline for analyzing neighborhood and household characteristics.

returned_title: Duisburger Bürgerumfrage – Herbst 2000 (Duisburg Citizen Survey, Autumn 2000)
justification: Highly relevant survey of Duisburg residents conducted in October–November 2000. The dataset covers community living conditions, local government, political behavior, and attitudes. It is useful for studying residents' perceptions of Duisburg, satisfaction with municipal conditions, neighborhood identification, and political preferences. Together with the spring 2000 survey, it supports comparisons of public opinion and urban living conditions within the same year.

returned_title: Duisburger Bürgerumfrage – Herbst 2001 (Duisburg Citizen Survey, Autumn 2001)
justification: Strong match for the housing and neighborhood dimensions of the research. The survey examines residents' satisfaction with their own housing, immediate residential surroundings, environmental conditions, and Duisburg overall. It also measures attachment to neighborhoods and identification with the city. Results can be examined across demographic groups and municipal districts, including Rheinhausen and Walsum. Particularly valuable for studying neighborhood differences in perceived quality of life and residential satisfaction.

returned_title: Duisburger Bürgerumfrage – Herbst 2002, deutsche Befragte (Duisburg Citizen Survey, Autumn 2002, German Population)
justification: Directly relevant to housing, community life, and municipal government in Duisburg. This GESIS dataset surveys German residents aged 18–75 and is categorized under housing, community living environment, and government and political organizations. It provides an appropriate source for examining residential conditions, satisfaction with local life, and perceptions of municipal affairs. Its population definition is important when comparing results with surveys that separately sampled foreign residents.

returned_title: Duisburger Bürgerumfrage – Herbst 2003, ausländische Befragte (Duisburg Citizen Survey, Autumn 2003, Foreign Population)
justification: Relevant for investigating urban living conditions and neighborhood experiences among Duisburg's foreign population. This GESIS dataset focuses on community living environments and migration. It offers an opportunity to examine how experiences and perceptions of city life vary among residents with different citizenship backgrounds. It is particularly useful for research on demographic inequalities and the experiences of immigrant communities in Duisburg during the early 2000s.

returned_title: Duisburger Bürgerumfrage – Herbst 2004, deutsche Befragte (Duisburg Citizen Survey, Autumn 2004, German Population)
justification: One of the strongest matches across the requested research themes. The survey includes residential satisfaction, length of residence, satisfaction with housing and neighborhoods, environmental conditions, city attachment, and regional identity. It also records voting intentions for the 2005 North Rhine-Westphalia state election, voting behavior in the 2000 election, and party preferences. Cultural participation is measured through frequency of visits to recreational, educational, and cultural facilities in Duisburg. Demographic variables include age, gender, marital status, household size and composition, education, and employment. Particularly suitable for analyzing relationships between housing satisfaction, cultural participation, political attitudes, and household characteristics.

returned_title: Duisburger Bürgerumfrage – Herbst 2005, deutsche Befragte (Duisburg Citizen Survey, Autumn 2005, German Population)
justification: Excellent match for research on housing conditions, municipal services, local economic perceptions, and demographic characteristics. The survey examines residents' satisfaction with Duisburg and its residential environment, public facilities, and local living conditions. It includes assessments of municipal waste management, recycling facilities, street cleaning, wastewater disposal, and interactions with municipal service providers. Its questions on local services and public administration make it especially valuable for evaluating satisfaction with municipal government and neighborhood infrastructure.

returned_title: Duisburger Bürgerumfrage – Herbst 2005, ausländische Befragte (Duisburg Citizen Survey, Autumn 2005, Foreign Population)
justification: Exceptionally close match to the research specification, particularly for comparisons involving foreign residents. This GESIS dataset contains 571 respondents and 212 variables. It covers housing tenure, building type, satisfaction with housing and neighborhoods, neighborhood attachment, perceptions of economic conditions in Duisburg and Germany, local problems, municipal politics, and public services. Respondents evaluate public transport, bicycle infrastructure, employment opportunities, cultural facilities, parks, libraries, sports facilities, and municipal administration. Additional questions address adult education participation, recycling services, waste collection, and satisfaction with public authorities. Demographic variables include age, gender, nationality, household composition, education, occupation, income, political party preference, public transport use, and neighborhood of residence. It is particularly suitable for neighborhood-level and household-level analysis.

returned_title: Duisburger Bürgerbefragung – Historical Citizen Survey Collection, 1981–2009
justification: Official City of Duisburg resource documenting the municipality's representative population surveys conducted between 1981 and 2009. The historical survey program provides important context for investigating residents' living conditions, satisfaction with municipal services, neighborhood development, and public perceptions of local government. It is useful for locating additional survey waves from the 2000s and identifying municipal publications associated with the surveys. This is a collection-level resource rather than an individual survey dataset.

returned_title: Duisburger Bürgerbefragung – Municipal Open Data Catalog
justification: Official German government data catalog entry for the Duisburg citizen survey program. It provides a discovery point for municipal survey information and published results. Relevant to research on local living conditions, satisfaction with municipal administration, urban development, and residents' perceptions of public services. It complements the historical GESIS datasets by identifying the city government's own survey resources and documentation. Researchers should check the available survey years and data formats because this catalog entry is not itself a confirmed individual-level dataset from the 2000s.

returned_title: Flash Eurobarometer 10 (Managers) – Knowledge about European Institutions for Economic Support (1992)
justification: Excellent match for the research requirements. Conducted in April 1992, this dataset examines European managers' awareness, knowledge, and use of European Community institutions supporting small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs). It includes familiarity with economic support institutions, sources of information about these institutions, awareness of the 'European Week of the Economy' and associated information sources, and organizations considered helpful for establishing foreign business relationships. Company characteristics include business size, turnover, industry sector, and respondent position. The dataset covers all 12 requested countries: Belgium, Germany (West), Denmark, France, Greece, Ireland, Italy, Luxembourg, the Netherlands, Portugal, Spain, and Great Britain. It contains 2,440 observations and 88 variables. Published by the GESIS Data Archive, study ZA2146. This is the strongest match because its geographic coverage, time period, research subjects, and survey questions align directly with the stated research need.

returned_title: Flash Eurobarometer 40 (Managers Study) – Knowledge about EU Institutions for Support to Small and Medium-Sized Businesses (1995)
justification: Excellent match and particularly valuable for comparison with Flash Eurobarometer 10. Conducted in April 1995, this survey investigates managers' familiarity with European Union institutions providing economic assistance to SMEs, their awareness and utilization of specific support organizations, their most important information sources, and organizations considered useful for international business relationships. It also includes company size, turnover, business sector, and managerial position. Geographic coverage includes Belgium, Denmark, western Germany, France, Greece, Ireland, Italy, Luxembourg, the Netherlands, Portugal, Spain, and the United Kingdom. The dataset contains 2,492 observations and 43 variables. Published by the GESIS Data Archive, study ZA2614. Together with the 1992 survey, it provides an opportunity to investigate changes in managers' awareness and utilization of EU business support institutions during the 1990s, although differences in survey design and questions should be checked before making direct comparisons.

returned_title: Flash Eurobarometer 21 (Managers) – Knowledge about Information Sources for Businesses (1993)
justification: Highly relevant complementary dataset for studying how European business managers obtained information during the early 1990s. Conducted in October 1993, this survey focuses on managers' knowledge of information sources for businesses. It is particularly useful for examining the information-access dimension of the research question and complementing the institutional awareness measures available in Flash Eurobarometers 10 and 40. The dataset contains 2,487 observations and 56 variables. Published in the GESIS Flash Eurobarometer collection as study ZA2365. Researchers should consult the questionnaire and geographic coverage before treating its variables as directly comparable with the 1992 and 1995 surveys.

returned_title: Flash Eurobarometer 63 (Managers 13) – Small and Medium Enterprises and Their Information Requirements (1998)
justification: Strong complementary dataset for examining European SME managers' information needs and information-seeking practices toward the end of the 1990s. Collected in September 1998, it investigates information responsibilities within companies, sources of business information, Internet use, information requirements, evaluation of available information, and the relationship between online and conventional information sources. Company characteristics include business sector, size, turnover, and respondent position. Geographic coverage includes all 12 requested countries, alongside additional European countries. The dataset contains 2,047 observations and 46 variables. Published by the GESIS Data Archive as study ZA3143. Although it does not directly reproduce all questions about EU business-support institutions or European promotional events, it provides valuable evidence about the changing information environment experienced by European SME managers during the 1990s.

returned_title: Flash Eurobarometer 64 (Managers 14) – Cross-Border Trade and Services in the European Union and Trade Restrictions (1998)
justification: Relevant supplementary dataset for investigating the foreign-trade and European economic integration dimensions of the research. Conducted in September 1998, this managers' survey addresses cross-border trade, services, and trade restrictions within the European Union. It can help contextualize the need for institutional support and organizations facilitating international business activities. The dataset contains 4,057 observations and 285 variables and is identified as study ZA3144 in the GESIS Flash Eurobarometer collection. Its principal value lies in examining international business activity and trade barriers rather than directly measuring awareness of EU support institutions. Researchers should verify country coverage and specific questionnaire variables before combining it with the primary datasets.

returned_title: Arbeitsmarktpolitik im Deutschen Kaiserreich: Arbeitsvermittlung, Arbeitsbeschaffung und Arbeitslosenunterstützung 1890–1918 (GESIS ZA8423)
justification: Exact match for the research need. Compiled by Anselm Faust, this historical dataset examines German labor market policy between 1890 and 1918. It contains statistical tables covering unemployment, public and noncommercial employment exchanges, job placement, emergency public works, and unemployment compensation. It includes unemployment rates among trade union members (1904–1918), clerical employee associations (1908–1918), gender-specific unemployment (1914–1918), women's job placements (1910–1918), the establishment of public employment exchanges in Prussia (1864–1909), emergency employment projects (1891–1913), and unemployment assistance provided by free, Christian, and Hirsch-Duncker trade unions. This is the most directly relevant dataset.

returned_title: Arbeitsmarktpolitik im Deutschen Kaiserreich – Historical Statistics Database (HISTAT)
justification: Direct access to the historical statistical tables associated with Anselm Faust's study. The HISTAT collection organizes the data into three categories: unemployment, employment exchanges, and unemployment assistance. Relevant series include job applications per 100 vacancies (1907–1918), trade union unemployment rates (1904–1918), job placement outcomes (1913–1918), public employment exchange establishment dates in Prussia, women's employment placements (1910–1918), emergency public works (1891–1913), and unemployment benefit expenditures (1891–1918). Particularly useful for downloading and comparing historical time series.

returned_title: Entwicklung der Arbeitslosigkeit in Deutschland 1887–2000 / Development of Unemployment in Germany 1887–2000 (GESIS ZA8218)
justification: Highly relevant complementary dataset compiled by Jürgen Sensch. It provides historical unemployment and employment statistics beginning in 1887, covering the German Empire, World War I, and the Weimar Republic. The collection draws on historical statistical publications and includes information about unemployment measurement before nationwide standardized reporting existed. Useful for reconstructing unemployment trends during 1890–1918, comparing labor market conditions before and during World War I, and contextualizing the development of employment services and unemployment assistance.

returned_title: Historische Statistik: Arbeitslosigkeit, Arbeitsvermittlung und Gewerkschaftliche Unterstützung (HISTAT Time Series)
justification: Historical statistical tables covering employment, unemployment, trade unions, and unemployment assistance. Particularly relevant series include unemployment among workers and salaried employees based on trade union statistics (1908–1924), membership and expenditure on unemployment and travel assistance among free trade unions (1891–1914), and employment and unemployment in Germany (1913–1940). These series provide additional quantitative evidence on labor market conditions, union-based unemployment protection, and the transition from Imperial Germany to the Weimar Republic.

returned_title: Soziale Lage und Gewerkschaftsbewegung: Statistiken zur Geschichte der Gewerkschaften ab 1800
justification: Historical statistical collection documenting German trade unions, workers' economic conditions, wages, unemployment, and labor disputes. Relevant datasets include unemployment rates from 1887 to 1920, statistics on free, Christian, and Hirsch-Duncker trade unions from 1900 to 1931, and industrial workers' real wages during the German Empire from 1871 to 1913. Useful for analyzing the relationship between union organization, unemployment, labor market conditions, and the development of collective unemployment protection during the target period.

returned_title: Arbeitslosigkeit in der Weimarer Republik (GESIS Historical Study)
justification: Complementary historical unemployment dataset associated with Dietmar Petzina, covering 1919–1938. Although its primary period begins immediately after the requested 1890–1918 interval, it provides useful comparative evidence about unemployment trends, labor market institutions, and the development of standardized unemployment statistics following World War I. Particularly valuable for studying the institutional transition from Imperial Germany's fragmented employment exchanges and union-based assistance toward the more centralized employment administration and unemployment insurance system of the Weimar Republic.

returned_title: Historische Statistik: Erwerbstätigkeit und Arbeitsmarkt im Deutschen Reich (HISTAT)
justification: Historical statistics collection containing datasets related to employment, labor markets, industrial workers, and trade unions in Germany. Includes studies of the regional expansion of German trade unions during 1896–1918 and historical labor disputes. Useful for identifying supplementary quantitative datasets on regional labor market organization, trade union development, and employment conditions during the German Empire. This collection can support comparisons across regions and labor organizations, including the period preceding World War I.

returned_title: Duisburg Citizen Survey (Autumn 2005, Foreign Population) – Duisburger Bürgerumfrage (Herbst 2005, ausländische Befragte)
justification: Excellent match. This GESIS dataset (ZA4523) surveys foreign residents of Duisburg aged 18–75 in 2005. It covers housing satisfaction, residential conditions, neighborhood attachment, environmental quality, major urban problems, and satisfaction with municipal services and administration. Topics include employment opportunities, public transportation, healthcare, affordable housing, cultural facilities, recreational spaces, waste disposal, recycling, and interactions with municipal service providers. It contains 571 observations and 212 variables. Particularly valuable for examining immigrants' living conditions, experiences of local government, and integration into urban life. It can be compared with the parallel 2005 survey of German residents.

returned_title: Duisburg Citizen Survey (Autumn 2005, German Population) – Duisburger Bürgerumfrage (Herbst 2005, deutsche Befragte)
justification: Excellent complementary dataset for comparing immigrant and native residents. Conducted in Duisburg in autumn 2005, this survey examines housing satisfaction, housing tenure, neighborhood conditions, environmental quality, local identity, and satisfaction with public services. It includes assessments of municipal administration, transportation, healthcare, educational facilities, recreational infrastructure, and waste management. Political variables include participation in the 2005 federal election and 2004 municipal elections. Particularly useful alongside ZA4523 for analyzing differences between German and foreign residents in perceptions of urban living conditions and municipal governance.

returned_title: Duisburg Citizen Survey (Autumn 2004, German Population) – Duisburger Bürgerumfrage (Herbst 2004, deutsche Befragte)
justification: Highly relevant survey covering housing satisfaction, residential stability, neighborhood quality, environmental problems, urban identity, political preferences, and satisfaction with municipal services in Duisburg during 2004. Respondents evaluate living conditions, housing affordability, employment opportunities, transportation, healthcare, environmental cleanliness, and municipal administration. The survey also includes internet use and political attitudes relating to the 2005 North Rhine-Westphalia state election. Useful for investigating urban quality of life, local government evaluations, and socioeconomic differences among native residents.

returned_title: Duisburg Citizen Survey (Autumn 2003, Foreign Population) – Duisburger Bürgerumfrage (Herbst 2003, ausländische Befragte)
justification: Relevant Duisburg survey focusing on foreign residents during the early 2000s. Part of the GESIS Duisburg Citizen Surveys series, which provides information on urban living conditions and residents' evaluations of their municipality. Particularly relevant for investigating immigrant experiences in Duisburg and comparing survey results across years. The dataset can support longitudinal comparisons with the 2005 foreign-population survey. Researchers should inspect the questionnaire to establish which measures of discrimination, language proficiency, media consumption, and immigrant–native relations are available.

returned_title: Duisburg Citizen Survey (Autumn 2002, German Population) – Duisburger Bürgerumfrage (Herbst 2002, deutsche Befragte)
justification: Relevant early-2000s Duisburg municipal survey archived by GESIS. Its target population comprises German residents aged 18–75 selected from municipal population registers. It belongs to the recurring Duisburg Citizen Surveys series, making it useful for studying changes in urban satisfaction, residential conditions, and perceptions of municipal governance. The German-resident sampling frame makes it a potential comparison source for surveys of foreign residents. Detailed questionnaire documentation should be consulted to identify specific environmental, administrative, migration-related, and sociodemographic variables.

returned_title: Duisburg Citizen Survey (Autumn 2001) – Duisburger Bürgerumfrage Herbst 2001
justification: Strong geographical and temporal match. This 2001 Duisburg survey examines satisfaction with housing, immediate residential surroundings, neighborhood environmental conditions, and the city overall. It includes respondents' attachment to their districts and differences in satisfaction across demographic and political groups. The survey documents variations associated with age, education, political preferences, and residential location. Particularly useful for examining environmental inequalities, neighborhood belonging, urban satisfaction, and socioeconomic differences in Duisburg at the beginning of the decade.

returned_title: Duisburg Citizen Survey (Autumn 2000) – Duisburger Bürgerumfrage Herbst 2000
justification: Relevant baseline dataset for research on Duisburg during the 2000s. Conducted between October and November 2000, it surveys residents aged 18–75. Archived by GESIS, it covers community and residential-environment topics and can be used to investigate local living conditions at the beginning of the study period. Its inclusion in the Duisburg Citizen Surveys series makes it valuable for comparisons with later surveys addressing housing, urban satisfaction, and municipal issues. The questionnaire should be checked for the availability of specific migration, language, discrimination, and media-use indicators.

returned_title: Duisburg Citizen Survey (Spring 2000) – Duisburger Bürgerumfrage Frühjahr 2000
justification: Relevant municipal survey conducted in Duisburg between February and March 2000. The study covers adult residents aged 18–75 and belongs to the GESIS collection of Duisburg Citizen Surveys. Its thematic classification includes community life, residential environments, and housing. It provides an additional early-2000s observation point for examining urban living conditions and comparing resident attitudes across survey waves. Particularly useful for research designs requiring multiple observations within the same municipality.

returned_title: LebensRäume – Population Survey of the Federal Office for Building and Regional Planning, 1985–2007
justification: Highly relevant supplementary dataset for studying housing satisfaction, living conditions, migration, and immigrant–native relations. This German population survey series includes observations from the 2000s and examines residential circumstances, housing costs, neighborhood infrastructure, residential mobility, local attachment, and assessments of relationships between Germans and foreigners. It also contains employment information, household economic circumstances, general life satisfaction, and regional classifications. Particularly valuable for providing broader German or North Rhine-Westphalian comparisons to Duisburg-specific findings. Duisburg-level identification and the availability of particular questions vary and must be verified.

returned_title: LebensRäume – Population Survey of the Federal Institute for Research on Building, Urban Affairs and Spatial Development, 2002
justification: Relevant supplementary survey conducted in autumn 2002. It examines housing conditions, neighborhood characteristics, residential satisfaction, mobility, local infrastructure, socioeconomic circumstances, and relationships between German and foreign residents. Particularly useful for investigating how perceptions of immigrant–native relations relate to housing satisfaction and neighborhood socioeconomic composition. Its regional information may enable comparisons involving North Rhine-Westphalia, subject to geographic detail and access restrictions. It is not specifically a Duisburg municipal survey.

returned_title: Foreigners in Germany 2000 – Second Wave (Ausländer in Deutschland 2000 – 2. Welle)
justification: Relevant supplementary migration survey focusing on foreign residents in Germany in 2000, including Turkish, Italian, Yugoslav, Greek, and Spanish populations aged 15 and older. It examines migration histories, length of residence, intentions to remain in Germany, relationships with the country of origin, perceived attitudes of Germans toward foreign workers, employment satisfaction, political preferences, and economic circumstances. Particularly valuable for studying migrant integration, immigrant–native relations, and socioeconomic differences. It provides migration-specific context but does not offer the same Duisburg-focused coverage of housing satisfaction and municipal services.

returned_title: German General Social Survey (ALLBUS) – Cumulation 1980–2014
justification: Useful complementary dataset for examining discrimination, immigrant–native relations, neighborhood composition, and political attitudes during the 2000s. ALLBUS includes questions about attitudes toward immigrants, contact with foreigners in neighborhoods and workplaces, perceived discrimination, social distance, ethnic diversity, and immigration policy. Its extensive sociodemographic information supports analyses of how education, income, employment, and other characteristics relate to attitudes toward migrants. Relevant survey years can provide broader comparisons for North Rhine-Westphalia, although the dataset is not designed to represent Duisburg individually and does not provide the same detailed municipal-service measures.

returned_title: Sofortresonanzen DDR Fernsehen 36. Woche 1985 (SFR 36/85)
justification: Highly relevant dataset collected on August 31, 1985, by the GDR State Committee for Television. Contains television viewing participation, evaluations of specific programs, and assessments of presenters. Covers the entertainment value, suspense, and perceived realism of POLIZEIRUF 110 – EIN SCHRITT ZU WEIT and DIE DRITTE FRAU. Includes evaluations of SPORT AKTUELL presenters, preferences for films, and awareness of the television schedule through TIPS ZUM FERNSEHPROGRAMM. Particularly suitable for studying program reception, perceived realism, presenter popularity, and television schedule awareness.

returned_title: Sofortresonanzen DDR Fernsehen 23. Woche 1987 (SFR 23/87)
justification: Highly relevant audience research dataset collected on June 9, 1987. Measures television viewing participation and evaluations of programs broadcast during the preceding week. Includes assessments of the realism and informational content of DER FREISCHÜTZ IN BERLIN, audience opinions about the presenter and records featured in WENNSCHON – DENNSCHON, and evaluations of WETTLAUF MIT DER ZEIT. Examines perceived realism, persuasiveness, entertainment, and informational value. Useful for analyzing audience perceptions of television credibility and individual presenters.

returned_title: Sofortresonanzen DDR Fernsehen 46. Woche 1984 (SFR 46/84)
justification: Representative household survey conducted on November 16, 1984, covering television participation and program evaluations. Particularly relevant for television schedule awareness, as respondents were asked about their knowledge of current television programming. Includes evaluations of UMSCHAU, audience interest in program topics, preferred broadcasting times for youth programming, the impact of shift work on viewing habits, and parental influence on children's television viewing. Contains demographic variables including age, gender, education, employment, household size, and political affiliation.

returned_title: Sofortresonanzen DDR Fernsehen 50. Woche 1982 (SFR 50/82)
justification: Audience participation and television viewing dataset collected on December 16, 1982. Especially relevant for investigating reasons for watching television. Includes questions about viewers' motivations for watching KLOCK 8, ACHTERN STROM, perceptions of its humor and entertainment value, satisfaction with program quality, and desired improvements. Also examines preferences for Saturday evening entertainment, viewing opportunities during holidays, reception of VERKEHRSKOMPASS, and evaluations of the series BUSCH SINGT. Suitable for analyzing viewing motivations, program satisfaction, and entertainment preferences.

returned_title: Sofortresonanzen DDR Fernsehen 35. Woche 1988 (SFR 35/88)
justification: Representative GDR television audience survey collected on September 2, 1988. Records viewing participation and program evaluations, including the entertainment value and perceived realism of POLIZEIRUF 110: EIFERSUCHT. Contains audience assessments of the presenter, humor, and participants in GLÜCK MUSS MAN HABEN. Also examines viewing frequency, perceived usefulness, technical presentation, and entertainment value of DAS VERKEHRSMAGAZIN. Particularly useful for studying audience engagement, program evaluation, presenter appeal, and perceptions of realism during the late 1980s.

returned_title: Sofortresonanzen DDR Fernsehen 6. Woche 1983 (SFR 6/83)
justification: Television audience survey conducted on February 9, 1983, examining viewing participation and evaluations of programs broadcast during the previous week. Includes audience assessments of the presenter, entertainment value, and target age group of BONG, as well as the informational content of PORTRÄT PER TELEFON: HEINZ QUERMANN. Also investigates regular viewing of KLOCK 8, ACHTERN STROM, desired program improvements, and opinions about changes to television scheduling. Relevant for studying presenter reception, audience preferences, program loyalty, and television schedule evaluations.

returned_title: Sofortresonanzen DDR Fernsehen 13. Woche 1985 (SFR 13/85)
justification: GDR television audience dataset from 1985 covering viewing participation, program evaluations, and audience expectations. Examines the suspense, entertainment value, and perceived realism of POLIZEIRUF 110 – TRAUM DES VERGESSENS. Also investigates interest in cultural programming, preferred topics, frequency of watching KULTURMAGAZIN, and preferred broadcasting days. Includes questions about occupational demands, physical and mental fatigue after work, and expectations of television programming. Valuable for investigating how everyday working conditions influenced television preferences and viewing motivations.

returned_title: Sofortresonanzen DDR Fernsehen 14. Woche 1982 (SFR 14/82)
justification: Representative audience survey from 1982 examining television viewing and evaluations of individual programs. Includes assessments of the entertainment value and realism of DER STAATSANWALT HAT DAS WORT: HOFFNUNG FÜR ANNA and DER NOTNAGEL. Investigates whether viewers believed television programs could contribute to crime prevention. Also includes viewing frequency for DU UND DEIN HAUSTIER and awareness of several television programs, including youth programming. Particularly relevant for measuring perceived realism, educational value, viewing frequency, and program awareness.

returned_title: Sofortresonanzen DDR Fernsehen 39. Woche 1982 (SFR 39/82)
justification: GDR television audience dataset examining participation and evaluations of programs broadcast during the preceding week. Contains detailed audience assessments of KOMM MIT MIR NACH CHICAGO, including entertainment, relaxation, identification with characters, and the portrayal of young people's lifestyles. Also examines evaluations of KNOBELEIEN, including its presenters Regina Liebsch and Ullrich Klein, studio activities, and overall program design. Useful for studying entertainment motivations, perceived representations of everyday life, and assessments of television presenters.

returned_title: Sofortresonanzen DDR Fernsehen 28. Woche 1989 (SFR 28/89)
justification: Late-1980s GDR television audience research dataset covering viewing participation, program evaluations, and satisfaction with television programming. Includes assessments of the host and performers in SHOWKOLADE, evaluations of the presenter and musical variety of PFUNDGRUBE, and knowledge of literary works associated with television programming. Also measures satisfaction with the overall programming offered by GDR television. Relevant for examining presenter popularity, audience preferences, cultural knowledge, and satisfaction with state television shortly before reunification.

returned_title: Sofortresonanzen DDR Fernsehen 5. Woche 1985 (SFR 5/85)
justification: Part of the GESIS archive of representative GDR television audience surveys. Documents viewing participation and evaluations of television programs during a specific week in 1985. The survey belongs to a collection based on standardized household interviews with registered television households. Relevant for analyzing audience participation, program reception, and viewing patterns. The detailed questionnaire and variable documentation should be consulted to establish whether household media equipment, cinema attendance, and other specific research variables are included.

returned_title: Sofortresonanzen DDR Fernsehen 48. Woche 1984 (SFR 48/84)
justification: Original GESIS study documentation for a representative GDR television audience survey conducted in 1984. Includes a standardized questionnaire asking household members which television programs they watched and how they evaluated those programs. Particularly useful for reconstructing program-specific viewing participation, audience ratings, and differences in television consumption between household members. The associated questionnaire documentation can support detailed variable-level analysis of viewing behavior and audience characteristics.

returned_title: Schülerintervallstudie IS II (ältere Kohorte), 1979–1985, 1. Welle
justification: Longitudinal survey of young people in the GDR covering the late 1970s and early 1980s. Includes variables on media, film, and viewing habits, including frequency of watching particular GDR television broadcasts. Provides a complementary source for analyzing television consumption among younger audiences and relating media habits to demographic and social characteristics. Especially useful for studying youth television viewing behavior alongside the broader household-based Sofortresonanzen surveys.

returned_title: The Role of Women in the Informal Sector: The Case of Ajegunle, Nigeria (GESIS Study ZA5003)
justification: Excellent match and the most directly relevant historical dataset identified. Listed in the GESIS data archive under study number 5003. The study examines women's living conditions, occupational activities, and financial circumstances in Ajegunle, Lagos. Documented variables include household composition, marital status, housing conditions, rent, migration histories, education, occupations, food expenditure, bank accounts, savings associations, trade union membership, credit arrangements, and community services. It also investigates financial contributions, savings behavior, and economic activities among women in the informal sector. The linked 1990 GESIS archive publication confirms the dataset's existence, although it is not a direct microdata download page. This is the strongest candidate for obtaining the original historical survey data.

returned_title: The Informal Sector of Lagos: An Inquiry into Urban Poverty and Employment
justification: Highly relevant historical survey of informal-sector enterprises in metropolitan Lagos, conducted during the 1970s and published as an International Labour Organization working paper in 1977. Covers enterprise ownership, business size, employment, labor supply, rural-to-urban migration, working hours, wages, and occupational training. Provides valuable baseline information for understanding women's informal employment, small businesses, trading activities, and economic conditions immediately preceding the 1980s. The linked record describes a sample survey, but the availability of original respondent-level data is not established.

returned_title: The Informal Sector of Lagos
justification: Relevant historical research containing statistical information on Lagos informal-sector enterprises, including Ajegunle. Covers household income, migration, education, employment, occupations, enterprise ownership, capital equipment, wages, economic activities, manufacturing, and retail trade. Useful for reconstructing the economic environment of Lagos during the late 1970s and early 1980s, particularly the employment opportunities and business conditions affecting women. This is a publication containing survey-based statistics rather than a confirmed downloadable microdata dataset.

returned_title: African Migrants in Lagos Suburbs: A Demographic and Socio-Economic Survey of Rural-Urban Migration in the Main Migrant Areas of the Federal Territory of Lagos, Nigeria
justification: Historical demographic and socioeconomic survey relevant to household living conditions, rural-to-urban migration, settlement patterns, and urban community life in Lagos. Examines migrant household heads, reasons for migration, socioeconomic characteristics, residential adjustment, and experiences of urban living. Particularly useful for contextualizing migration histories, household structures, and neighborhood development in Ajegunle. The survey predates the requested 1980s period and is not specifically focused on women informal-sector workers. The repository provides access to the research publication, not necessarily the original survey microdata.

returned_title: Living Conditions and Public Health Status in Three Urban Slums of Lagos, Nigeria
justification: Directly relevant geographically because the underlying cross-sectional survey includes Ajegunle alongside Ijora Oloye and Makoko. The study surveyed 2,434 residents between June 2010 and October 2012, collecting information about demographic characteristics, migration histories, living conditions, and public health. Useful for investigating housing, household circumstances, and access to essential services in Ajegunle. Although substantially later than the 1980s, it offers comparative evidence for examining changes in neighborhood conditions. The repository record describes the survey findings but does not establish public availability of respondent-level data.

returned_title: The Millennium Development Goals in Lagos, Nigeria: A Time-Line Study of Ajegunle Community (1998–2008)
justification: Ajegunle-specific longitudinal research based on household surveys conducted in 1998, 2002, and 2008, using systematic random sampling of 390 household heads. Examines socioeconomic characteristics, housing quality, neighborhood infrastructure, and settlement development. Relevant to community living conditions, housing, and the availability of basic services. Its repeated survey periods offer opportunities to study changes in Ajegunle after the 1980s. It is not a direct historical match, and the availability of original household-level data is unconfirmed.

returned_title: Urban Poverty and Environmental Conditions in Informal Settlements of Ajegunle, Lagos, Nigeria
justification: Geographically specific survey-based research examining poverty, household income, housing, employment, and environmental conditions in Ajegunle. Reports occupational distributions across trading, artisanal work, civil service, farming, and fishing, alongside income patterns and neighborhood conditions. Relevant to reconstructing informal employment, household finances, and the availability of urban infrastructure and services. It also references earlier socioeconomic information from the 1990s. However, the underlying survey was conducted after the requested 1980s period, and the linked resource is a research publication rather than a confirmed microdata repository.

returned_title: The Home as Workplace: Investigating Home-Based Enterprises in Low-Income Settlements of the Lagos Metropolis
justification: Strong thematic match for women operating small businesses and informal enterprises from their homes. Survey-based research covering low-income Lagos neighborhoods, including Ajegunle, with information on gender, education, household size, housing tenure, employment, enterprise ownership, trading, manufacturing, business registration, savings, cooperative loans, rotating credit arrangements, and family financial assistance. Particularly useful for understanding the relationship between household living conditions and income-generating activities. The survey is considerably later than the 1980s, and the linked publication contains aggregate results rather than confirmed downloadable individual-level data.

returned_title: Socio-Economic Adaptation Strategies of the Urban Poor in the Lagos Metropolis, Nigeria
justification: Relevant survey-based evidence on gender differences in informal-sector occupations, income, business ownership, household assets, and financing strategies. Based on 2010 fieldwork involving 396 respondents, including 183 women, across low-income Lagos communities that include Ajegunle. Provides sex-disaggregated information on trading, services, manufacturing, savings, rotating credit, cooperative financing, household income, and asset ownership. Particularly relevant to examining the financial practices of informal-sector businesswomen. It is useful for comparison with historical Ajegunle research, but does not provide 1980s observations or confirmed public access to individual-level records.

returned_title: Historical Money and Capital Market Database of the Center for Financial Studies, Germany 1871–1914 (Historische Geld- und Kapitalmarktdatenbank des Center for Financial Studies, Deutschland 1871 bis 1914)
justification: Excellent match and the most directly relevant dataset. Compiled by Steffen Eube, Johannes Müller, and Anja Weigt at the Center for Financial Studies, Goethe University Frankfurt, and archived by GESIS (study ZA8286). Covers the German Empire from 1871 to 1914, including the 1870s, 1880s, 1890s, 1900s, and early 1910s. Contains more than 100,000 bond-market observations, including interest rates, securities prices, and associated yields, alongside extensive stock-market data. Covers six major German financial centers: Berlin, Frankfurt am Main, Hamburg, Leipzig, Cologne, and Munich. Stock exchange observations are organized by industry, including banking, insurance, transportation, electrical engineering, mechanical engineering, metals, mining, construction, chemicals, paper, glass, ceramics, brewing, textiles, and leather. Especially suitable for analyzing historical German financial markets, stock prices, investment returns, regional stock exchanges, and industrial capital markets before World War I.

returned_title: Historical Money and Capital Market Database: Original Stock Exchange Data and Documentation, 1871–1914
justification: Direct institutional repository for the historical financial database developed at Goethe University's Center for Financial Studies. Provides downloadable historical stock exchange datasets for Berlin, Frankfurt, Hamburg, Cologne, Leipzig, and Munich, with separate Excel files for each exchange. Contains approximately 700,000 stock-market observations and more than 100,000 bond-market observations for 1871–1914. Includes historical share prices, interest rates, securities yields, and supporting documentation. Particularly useful for researchers requiring original downloadable data, individual exchange records, comparisons across financial centers, and industry-level analysis.

returned_title: Historische Geld- und Kapitalmarktdatenbank, 1871–1914 — BERD@NFDI Longterm Company Data
justification: Highly relevant research data catalog entry describing German company-level stock market observations between 1871 and 1914. Includes end-of-month ordinary share prices, total share capital, and annual dividends for companies listed on the Berlin, Frankfurt, Hamburg, Leipzig, Cologne, and Munich exchanges. Data are distributed across six Excel files, each organized into 13 industry categories. Particularly valuable for constructing historical equity returns, examining dividend income, calculating market capitalization, and comparing industrial sectors and regional financial centers. The catalog identifies the data as available under a CC BY-SA 4.0 license.

returned_title: SAFE Historical Financial Data: German Stock Data Before World War I, 1871–1914
justification: Highly relevant collection of historical German financial datasets maintained by the Leibniz Institute for Financial Research SAFE. Its main historical stock dataset covers 1871–1914, and supplementary datasets include monthly historical stock market price and performance indices covering January 1871 through July 1914. Additional data cover early German initial public offerings, securities listings, and historical market index construction. Particularly useful for analyzing long-run German stock price movements, total investment performance, market development, and the evolution of listed companies before World War I. Access to some datasets requires submitting a data request.

returned_title: The German Finance and Banking Industry from 1876 until 1945 (Deutsches Geld- und Bankwesen 1876 bis 1945)
justification: Strong complementary dataset covering German money, banking, and capital markets, including much of the requested 1871–1914 period. Contains historical interest rates and yields for 1876–1944, securities turnover for 1870–1918, domestic securities issuance for 1883–1913, domestic company share capital and prices for 1870–1922, and a stock price index for 1870–1913. Particularly useful for studying financial market development, securities issuance, stock market valuations, and the relationship between interest rates and investment activity. The broader chronological coverage allows researchers to place pre-World War I observations in a longer historical context.

returned_title: Historical Statistics: German Finance and Banking, Interest Rates, Securities Markets, and Stock Prices
justification: Direct historical statistics catalog containing time series relevant to German capital markets before 1914. Includes selected interest rates and yields beginning in 1876, stock price indices covering 1870–1913, domestic securities issuance, securities turnover, and share capital statistics. Particularly useful for obtaining aggregated financial indicators to complement detailed company-level stock exchange data. Supports investigations of historical equity market movements, capital formation, securities activity, and changing interest rate conditions during German industrialization.

returned_title: The Price Formation in the Stock Market of the German Empire, 1870–1934
justification: Closely related historical German stock market research dataset archived by GESIS. Includes annual stock price levels, dividends, and equity returns for 1870–1913, directly overlapping the requested period. Particularly valuable for examining German equity market performance, comparing price appreciation with dividend income, and analyzing long-term investment returns before World War I. Also provides historical stock market indicators useful for placing German financial market developments in an international context.

returned_title: Index of Stock Prices for Germany, 1870–1913 — NBER Macrohistory Database / Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis
justification: Relevant historical monthly German stock price index covering January 1870 through December 1913. Distributed through the Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis using the NBER Macrohistory Database. Provides a consistent aggregate stock price series covering nearly the entire requested period. Particularly suitable for examining long-term market trends, business cycles, the aftermath of the 1873 financial crisis, and equity market movements during German industrialization. Does not provide individual company prices, sector-level dividends, or comprehensive bond yields, making it most useful as a supplementary benchmark.

returned_title: Time Series of Money in Circulation in Germany, 1870–1913 (Zeitreihen zum Geldumlauf in Deutschland 1870–1913)
justification: Complementary historical monetary dataset compiled by economic historian Richard H. Tilly and archived by GESIS (study ZA8230). Covers Germany from 1870 to 1913, including all five requested decades. Contains historical time series describing monetary circulation and the development of Germany's financial system. Useful for investigating the monetary conditions underlying changes in interest rates, banking activity, securities markets, and financial development. Although it does not directly provide the detailed stock exchange prices and investment returns requested, it offers valuable monetary context for interpreting German money and capital markets before World War I.

returned_title: Politbarometer 1988 (Cumulative Dataset), ZA1762
justification: German public opinion survey containing questions about support for introducing the death penalty, including for murder and politically motivated murder. Relevant to research on capital punishment attitudes and demographic differences. However, the survey was conducted in 1988 rather than the 1970s, making it a supplementary historical comparison rather than an exact match.

returned_title: German General Social Survey (ALLBUS) – Cumulation 1980–2014, ZA4584
justification: Large-scale German social survey dataset covering political attitudes, criminal justice opinions, and demographic characteristics. Includes questions concerning capital punishment for terrorists and harsher criminal penalties. Contains demographic variables useful for studying differences across social groups. Coverage begins in 1980, so it does not directly satisfy the requested 1970s period, and its death-penalty questions are not necessarily specific to murder.

returned_title: Political Attitudes in East and West, March 1990 (Comparative Survey FRG–GDR)
justification: Extremely relevant to the research need. This comparative survey examines political attitudes in East and West Germany immediately before reunification. It covers satisfaction with democracy, political and economic expectations, attitudes toward German unity, party preferences, sympathy toward major political parties (CDU, CSU, SPD, FDP, Greens, PDS and others), perceptions of social inequality, and personal economic circumstances. Particularly valuable for establishing a baseline of political attitudes before reunification.

returned_title: Political Attitudes, Political Participation and Voting Behavior in Reunified Germany 1994
justification: Highly relevant comparative dataset containing surveys conducted in East and West Germany in 1994. It examines satisfaction with democracy, trust in government institutions, evaluations of political parties, voting intentions and decisions, political participation, and citizens' perceived ability to influence government. It also includes economic assessments, perceptions of East–West differences, attitudes toward the former GDR, and identification with political organizations. Particularly suitable for examining political integration after reunification.

returned_title: ALLBUS/GGSS Baseline Survey 1991 (German General Social Survey)
justification: One of the most useful datasets for comparing East and West Germans immediately after reunification. Conducted in 1991, it covers satisfaction with federal and state governments, evaluations of the political system, voting behavior, party preferences, political participation, and attitudes toward German reunification. It also includes employment, occupational characteristics, economic circumstances, social inequality, and demographic information. Its coverage of political and socioeconomic conditions makes it especially valuable for the proposed research.

returned_title: Political Cultures in United Germany 1992
justification: Highly relevant to political attitudes and citizen participation during the early reunification period. The survey investigates East–West differences in democratic values, political trust, evaluations of federal and state governments, party preferences, political participation, and involvement in citizens' initiatives. It also explores political experiences under the GDR, attitudes toward socialism, economic expectations, employment circumstances, and perceptions of political influence. Particularly useful for studying changes in political culture following reunification.

returned_title: Attitudes on Current Questions of Domestic Policy (1990) – GDR
justification: Directly relevant to political attitudes within the German Democratic Republic during its final year. The dataset includes satisfaction with democratic developments, party preferences, previous voting behavior, attitudes toward municipal voting rights, citizen participation, economic systems, and political reunification. It also examines perceptions of public safety, social conditions, and differences between East and West Germany. Particularly valuable for studying political preferences and democratic expectations during the transition from the GDR to reunified Germany.

returned_title: Election Study 1990 (Trend Investigation) – Politbarometer
justification: Relevant for investigating voting decisions, political party evaluations, government approval, and attitudes toward reunification during 1990. Variables include electoral preferences, party identification, voting decisions, satisfaction with government performance, expectations about reunification, employment concerns, housing-related concerns, and perceptions of economic consequences. Particularly useful for analyzing electoral behavior and changing political preferences during the reunification process.

returned_title: ALLBUS/GGSS 1992 – German General Social Survey
justification: Relevant for examining political and social attitudes in reunified Germany during the early 1990s. The ALLBUS survey program provides representative social survey data that allow comparisons between residents of the former East and West Germany. It is useful for studying political orientations, participation, social conditions, employment, and demographic differences. It can also be combined with the 1991, 1994, and 1996 ALLBUS surveys to examine changes following reunification.

returned_title: ALLBUS/GGSS 1994 – German General Social Survey
justification: Relevant for studying changes in political attitudes and social conditions four years after reunification. The survey provides data on social attitudes, political orientations, employment and socioeconomic characteristics, and differences between eastern and western Germany. It is particularly useful when combined with earlier ALLBUS surveys to investigate whether political and social attitudes converged or remained distinct during the 1990s.

returned_title: ALLBUS/GGSS 1996 – German General Social Survey
justification: Useful for extending an analysis of East–West political and social differences into the mid-1990s. The dataset belongs to the established ALLBUS survey series and supports comparative research on political attitudes, social integration, employment characteristics, and socioeconomic differences. Combined with earlier survey waves, it allows researchers to investigate longer-term changes following reunification.

returned_title: Living Spaces – Public Opinion Survey of the BBR 1994 (LebensRäume – Bevölkerungsumfrage des BBSR 1994)
justification: Especially relevant to the community, urban and rural life, housing, and residential mobility components of the research need. The survey investigates housing conditions, residential satisfaction, neighborhood characteristics, mobility, employment, household economic circumstances, and social relations in residential areas. It provides a valuable complement to political attitude surveys by documenting everyday living conditions in Germany after reunification.

returned_title: Structures and Determinants of Labor Force Participation of Women and Men in the Former GDR (1991)
justification: Highly relevant to the employment transition experienced by residents of the former GDR. Conducted between September and December 1991, this survey investigates employment circumstances, labor market expectations, vocational qualifications, further vocational training, occupational characteristics, and participation in employment creation programs. It is particularly suitable for studying job mobility, retraining, and labor market restructuring following reunification.

returned_title: Interval Study Capabilities and Courses of Occupation 1985–1995, 8th Wave 1993
justification: Particularly valuable for examining occupational mobility, vocational training, unemployment concerns, and housing changes among people experiencing the transition from the GDR to reunified Germany. The 1993 survey includes changes in living conditions since the political turning point, employment expectations, job application difficulties, training experiences, willingness to relocate for work, housing circumstances, political orientations, party preferences, and trade union participation. Its longitudinal design is useful for investigating individual experiences of reunification.

returned_title: Attitudes to Current Questions of Domestic Policy (1995)
justification: Relevant for examining political attitudes and evaluations of social conditions in East and West Germany five years after reunification. The survey uses samples of eligible voters from eastern and western Germany and addresses political and domestic policy issues, including perceptions of economic conditions, employment problems, and social developments. It offers a useful mid-1990s comparison of political preferences and public attitudes.

returned_title: German Socio-Economic Panel (SOEP) – Longitudinal Household Survey, East German Sample from 1990
justification: One of the strongest complementary data sources for studying the socioeconomic consequences of reunification. The SOEP began surveying East German households in 1990, enabling longitudinal comparisons with West German respondents. Its repeated observations support research on employment transitions, unemployment, job mobility, occupational retraining, household income, housing, residential mobility, and political interest. Particularly useful for connecting changes in economic circumstances with political attitudes during the 1990s.

returned_title: Living in the GDR 1990 (Leben in der DDR 1990)
justification: Relevant for establishing the social and economic circumstances of people living in the GDR during the transition period. The dataset provides a historical source for examining everyday life in East Germany around 1990. It is potentially useful for contextualizing subsequent changes in housing, employment, social conditions, and attitudes during reunification. Its detailed variable documentation should be consulted to identify which aspects of the research need are covered.

returned_title: Decatur Study: Personal Influence, 1945
justification: Excellent match. Conducted by Paul F. Lazarsfeld and Elihu Katz in Decatur, Illinois, between June and August 1945, this landmark survey investigates interpersonal influence, opinion leadership, mass media, and social stratification.
