Particularly useful for studying changes in political trust, social values, immigration attitudes, religious identification, and differences between eastern and western Germany. Because the cumulative file focuses on repeated indicators, the standalone ALLBUS 2018 dataset remains preferable for investigating the complete set of 2018-specific questions on populism, refugees, and right-wing extremism.

returned_title: Ausländer in Ostdeutschland 1990 (Foreigners in Eastern Germany 1990) — GESIS Study ZA6342
justification: Excellent match and the most directly relevant dataset. Conducted in 1990 by the Berliner Institut für Sozialwissenschaftliche Studien (BISS), this survey examines foreign citizens living in East Germany during the transition from the GDR to reunified Germany. It covers migration behavior, reasons for immigration, living conditions, and relationships between Germans and foreigners. The study includes 327 foreign respondents (114 variables) and a comparison group of 173 German respondents (104 variables). Foreign respondents included Soviet, Vietnamese, Polish, and Hungarian citizens, primarily residing in East Berlin and Dresden. Particularly relevant for investigating migration histories, employment and socioeconomic circumstances, residence status, integration, and attitudes toward German society. Its timing also makes it valuable for studying foreign citizens' experiences during the transition to a market economy. The dataset is archived by GESIS under study number ZA6342.

returned_title: Monitor Digitalisierung 360° – WiSe 2023/24
justification: Excellent match. This GESIS research dataset directly addresses the status, practices, trends, and challenges of digital teaching and learning at German universities. Data were collected between November 2023 and March 2024 through standardized online questionnaires targeting university leadership, teaching staff, students, and support personnel. Topics include university policy, digitalization strategies, artificial intelligence, university development, teaching practices, and digital infrastructure. The dataset is explicitly classified as a longitudinal trend study, allowing comparisons with the preceding 2022 survey. It covers German higher education institutions and provides quantitative survey data for secondary analysis. Published in 2025 by GESIS, the dataset is available free of charge with registration. This is the strongest match for the research requirements.

returned_title: Monitor Digitalisierung 360° – Befragung 2022
justification: Highly relevant baseline survey for longitudinal analysis of higher education digitalization in Germany. Conducted between June and October 2022, the study surveyed 74 university leaders, 127 support staff, 399 lecturers, and 1,008 students. Questions covered digital teaching formats, blended learning, technological infrastructure, institutional support, university digitalization strategies, and organizational challenges. The survey was designed for repeated measurement, making it directly comparable with the 2023/24 Monitor Digitalisierung 360° study. The landing page provides research findings and methodological documentation. GESIS identifies the 2022 study as the predecessor of its 2023/24 dataset, although access to the underlying anonymized individual-level responses should be verified separately.

returned_title: Monitor Digitalisierung 360° – Longitudinal Higher Education Digitalization Monitoring
justification: Official landing page for the Hochschulforum Digitalisierung monitoring program, which examines digital transformation in teaching and learning at German universities. The program uses repeated surveys to track changes in institutional strategies, digital infrastructure, teaching practices, student experiences, and implementation challenges. It includes survey waves from 2022 and winter semester 2023/24, with a stated objective of measuring developments over time. Its multidimensional approach incorporates perspectives from students, educators, university administrators, and support services. Particularly valuable for identifying comparable survey waves and studying longitudinal developments in German higher education digitalization. This is a monitoring-program landing page rather than a separate downloadable microdata dataset.

returned_title: Monitor Digitalisierung 360° – Survey Results and Historical Data Archive
justification: Relevant historical resource for comparing quantitative findings across successive waves of the German higher education digitalization survey. The archive documents results from the 2022 baseline and the 2023/24 follow-up, including changes in digital teaching formats, student preferences, university digitalization policies, infrastructure, and artificial intelligence adoption. The 2023/24 survey included 93 university leaders, 246 support staff, 729 lecturers, and 1,084 students. It is particularly useful for identifying trends and contextualizing longitudinal analyses. The archive primarily provides published results and documentation; researchers seeking anonymized respondent-level numeric data should use the associated GESIS dataset.

returned_title: HEIM UND WERK Readers (Leisure Time)
justification: Highly relevant historical West German survey examining the leisure activities and reading habits of subscribers to the magazine HEIM UND WERK. Variables include media consumption, reading habits, library use, book ownership, book club membership, and attitudes toward work, employers, trade unions, and working hours. Occupational and employment information enables comparisons between groups of workers. Particularly useful for researching the relationship between employees' reading preferences, workplace attitudes, and magazine readership. The precise survey year and whether it evaluates an employer's company magazine should be verified.

returned_title: Education Expectations and Knowledge Interests (1958) / Bildungserwartungen und Wissensinteressen
justification: West German survey investigating cultural participation, magazine use, and interest in subscription clubs and book clubs. Includes occupational information, employment characteristics, education, and demographic variables. Although conducted in 1958 rather than the 1960s, it provides valuable baseline evidence for studying reading habits and book club participation immediately before the target decade. It does not specifically address evaluations of company magazines.

returned_title: Readers' Digest Survey of Europe Today, 1969
justification: Cross-national survey conducted in 1969 covering sixteen Western European countries, relevant to studying media consumption and leisure activities in the Federal Republic of Germany. Contains information on occupational structures, employment, education, household characteristics, cultural activities, and consumer preferences. German respondents may be isolated for analysis, subject to the dataset's country coverage and coding. Useful for contextualizing employees' reading and media habits, although specific questions about book clubs and company magazines are not confirmed. Dataset access is restricted.

returned_title: German Reader Analysis Surveys (Leser-Analyse), 1960–1971
justification: The historical Leser-Analyse survey series provides potentially valuable data on newspaper and magazine readership in West Germany throughout the 1960s. Its surveys preceded the German Media-Analyse series and collected information about print-media audiences. These data are particularly relevant for analyzing newspaper reading, magazine preferences, and differences in media consumption across occupational groups. The linked GESIS record is for the later Media-Analyse 1991 survey, which identifies the historical survey family; it is not itself a 1960s dataset. Individual 1960s survey records and their availability require further identification.

returned_title: Politbarometer 1977–2024 (Partial Cumulation) – GESIS ZA2391
justification: Best overall match. This longitudinal dataset combines selected variables from approximately monthly Politbarometer surveys conducted by Forschungsgruppe Wahlen for ZDF. It covers the entire 1990s and includes political opinions, voting intentions, party preferences, evaluations of politicians, electoral behavior, government performance, economic conditions, and major political issues. The series includes separate East and West German surveys for 1990–1995 and from 1999 onward. Geographic identifiers include federal states, supporting analysis of Berlin, Baden-Württemberg, Bavaria, Bremen, Hesse, Hamburg, Lower Saxony, North Rhine-Westphalia, Rhineland-Palatinate, Saarland, and Schleswig-Holstein, subject to sample availability. The partial cumulation contains a selected set of recurring variables rather than every question asked in the original surveys.

returned_title: GESIS Politbarometer – Annual Cumulative Survey Datasets (1977–2025)
justification: Official GESIS collection providing annual cumulative datasets of the Politbarometer surveys. Each annual dataset combines approximately monthly representative surveys of Germany's voting-age population and retains the questions and variables collected that year. Topics include voting behavior, party and politician evaluations, political attitudes, government performance, economic policy, international affairs, security, and current events. Separate Politbarometer East and West surveys are available for 1990–1995 and from 1999 onward. From 2003, additional short Politbarometer surveys are incorporated into the annual cumulative files. This collection is particularly suitable for researchers requiring the complete monthly survey content rather than selected longitudinal indicators.

returned_title: GESIS Politbarometer Research Data Catalogue – Annual Cumulations and Historical Surveys
justification: Official research data catalogue containing individual Politbarometer datasets, including annual cumulations from the 1990s, separate East and West German surveys, and later surveys incorporating short questionnaires. Enables researchers to locate year-specific datasets and documentation covering party preferences, politician evaluations, voting intentions, government satisfaction, social attitudes, crime, international politics, economic conditions, and major public issues. Particularly useful for assembling a detailed 1990–1999 monthly survey dataset while preserving the full range of questions asked in individual years.

returned_title: Politbarometer East 1993 (Cumulated Data Set) – GESIS ZA2390
justification: Directly relevant historical dataset containing the cumulative Politbarometer East surveys conducted in 1993. Covers voting intentions in federal and state elections, previous electoral behavior, party preferences, evaluations of political parties and politicians, and major political issues. Provides a complementary eastern German sample for comparative analysis with western German surveys. Especially useful for studying political attitudes during the early post-reunification period, although its eastern geographic coverage does not directly match most of the specified western federal states.

returned_title: 1998 Election Study (Politbarometer) – GESIS
justification: Historical cumulative dataset combining monthly Politbarometer surveys from 1998, a significant federal election year in Germany. Covers voting-age Germans' political opinions, party and politician evaluations, electoral preferences, voting behavior, and current political issues. Relevant to research on political attitudes and electoral change in the specified German federal states during the late 1990s. The 1998 surveys precede the resumption of separately conducted East and West Politbarometer surveys in 1999.

returned_title: Politbarometer West 2003 (Cumulated Data Set, Including Short Politbarometer Surveys) – GESIS ZA4004
justification: Highly relevant methodological and temporal extension of the 1990s Politbarometer series. Combines the regular 2003 Politbarometer West surveys with additional short Politbarometer questionnaires introduced into annual cumulative datasets from 2003 onward. Covers political opinions, party and politician evaluations, voting behavior, and current issues among the voting-age population. Particularly relevant to the specified western German federal states, including Baden-Württemberg, Bavaria, Bremen, Hesse, Hamburg, Lower Saxony, North Rhine-Westphalia, Rhineland-Palatinate, Saarland, and Schleswig-Holstein, as well as western Berlin where represented. Although outside the requested 1990s period, it directly matches the requirement for short surveys from 2003 onward and supports longitudinal extensions.

returned_title: Hochschulen in der Bundesrepublik Deutschland 1949–2001 (Universities in the Federal Republic of Germany, 1949–2001) – GESIS
justification: Excellent match and the most directly relevant dataset. Compiled by Peter Lundgreen and Gudrun Schwibbe and published through the GESIS Data Archive, this historical dataset provides longitudinal statistics on West German higher education from 1949 to 2001. It includes enrollment figures differentiated by university type: traditional universities, technical universities, comprehensive universities, theological colleges, pedagogical universities, art and music colleges, universities of applied sciences (Fachhochschulen), and administrative universities of applied sciences. Data cover individual institutions, German federal states, student gender, nationality, and institutional development. Particularly valuable are the methodological explanations of historical classification changes, including the consistent separation of technical universities from traditional universities and the retrospective reassignment of institutions to appropriate categories. An important caveat concerns pedagogical institutions: student enrollment before 1967 is missing from certain electronic time series because teacher-training institutions were not consistently included in official university statistics. Supplementary figures are available in the associated historical handbook. Geographic coverage distinguishes West Germany before reunification from the expanded Federal Republic after 1990.

returned_title: Berufliche Schulen und Hochschulen in der Bundesrepublik Deutschland 1949–2001 – Datenhandbuch zur deutschen Bildungsgeschichte, Band VIII (Historical Statistics / HISTAT)
justification: Excellent match. This historical education statistics collection, associated with Peter Lundgreen's research and the German educational history data handbook, provides extensive time-series tables covering vocational schools and higher education institutions between 1949 and 2001. Its university section includes the number of institutions by university category, enrollment at individual universities, and student participation by institution type. Relevant tables include student enrollments by university type and gender for 1949–2001, enrollments at technical universities for 1949–2001, theological universities for 1949–2001, pedagogical universities for 1950–2001, art and music universities for 1949–2001, and universities of applied sciences for 1972–2001. The collection is especially useful for studying the expansion and restructuring of the West German university system. Its historical documentation provides context for changing institutional definitions, the integration of teacher-training colleges, and the emergence of Fachhochschulen during the 1970s.

returned_title: Hochschulen in der Bundesrepublik Deutschland 1949–2001 – B2FIND Research Data Catalogue
justification: Excellent match. This catalogue record provides an alternative discovery and metadata entry for the GESIS historical university dataset covering 1949–2001. It is particularly valuable because its detailed documentation describes how different university categories were standardized across changing official statistical classifications. The dataset explicitly distinguishes technical universities, traditional universities, comprehensive universities, theological institutions, pedagogical universities, art and music universities, universities of applied sciences, and administrative universities of applied sciences. It also explains historical adjustments made to maintain comparability and identifies limitations in the electronic dataset, notably the absence of pedagogical university enrollment figures before 1967. The record documents geographical treatment of West Berlin, the former West German states, and the post-reunification federal states. This is an alternative access point to the first dataset rather than an independent statistical series.

returned_title: Hochschulentwicklung in der Bundesrepublik und in der DDR (1960–1990) – German History in Documents and Images
justification: Strong supplementary match for the period 1960–1990. This historical statistical resource provides comparative quantitative evidence on university development in West Germany and East Germany. It includes institutional counts, total student enrollments, new entrants, university examinations, doctoral qualifications, and academic personnel. Its statistics help contextualize the expansion of West German higher education during the 1960s, 1970s, and 1980s and provide a comparative perspective on the two German educational systems before reunification. Although it does not offer the same detailed classification of university types as the GESIS dataset, it is useful for validating aggregate enrollment trends and examining broader structural changes.

returned_title: Studierende nach Hochschularten, Ländern und Geschlecht – BMFTR Data Portal, Table 2.5.22
justification: Relevant official supplementary dataset from Germany's federal research ministry statistical portal. The table reports student enrollments differentiated by university type, federal state, and gender. Institutional categories include universities, pedagogical universities, theological universities, art colleges, universities of applied sciences, and administrative universities of applied sciences. It provides a useful official classification framework for comparing institutional categories and checking enrollment statistics against federal education reporting. Its historical coverage should be verified before using it as a complete 1949–2001 series. In particular, technical universities may be included within the broader university category rather than separately identified, so it is less suitable than the GESIS historical dataset for studying technical universities independently.

returned_title: Hochschulen nach Hochschularten und Ländern – BMFTR Data Portal, Table 2.5.1
justification: Useful supplementary official dataset for studying the institutional structure of German higher education. It records higher education institutions by type and federal state, including universities, pedagogical universities, theological universities, art colleges, general universities of applied sciences, and administrative universities of applied sciences. Although it measures institutional counts rather than student enrollment, it can help explain changes in enrollment patterns associated with institutional expansion, consolidation, and reclassification. It is particularly relevant when interpreting historical transitions involving pedagogical universities and universities of applied sciences. Historical coverage must be checked before using it to reconstruct the complete 1949–2001 period.

returned_title: Studentinnen/Studenten sowie Gasthörerinnen/Gasthörer an Hochschulen im Wintersemester 2008/09 – Statistisches Landesamt Rheinland-Pfalz
justification: Strong regional historical time-series resource covering university enrollments in Rhineland-Palatinate from winter semester 1948/49 through 2008/09. The statistical publication includes a longitudinal table of students by university type, distinguishing traditional universities, theological colleges, other academic institutions, universities of applied sciences, and administrative universities of applied sciences. Particularly relevant are its methodological footnotes concerning classification adjustments: pedagogical universities were included within university figures for specified historical periods, and the classification changed as teacher-training institutions were reorganized. This makes the resource useful for examining how administrative changes affect longitudinal comparability. Although geographically limited to one West German state, it provides an independently published official historical series covering the entire requested timeframe.

returned_title: Hochschulen in Nordrhein-Westfalen 2019/2020 – Historical University Enrollment Statistics
justification: Strong supplementary regional dataset for North Rhine-Westphalia, one of West Germany's major higher education regions. The statistical publication includes a historical enrollment series by university type beginning with winter semester 1950/51 and continuing through 2019/20. It is particularly useful for reconstructing university enrollment growth during the 1950s through the 2000s. Its methodological notes document significant institutional changes, including the dissolution of pedagogical universities in 1980 and their incorporation into universities or other higher education institutions. These adjustments are important for interpreting apparent discontinuities in university-type enrollment statistics. The dataset can support regional validation of the national GESIS series and provide historical evidence of institutional restructuring.

returned_title: The Growth of the German Economy since the Middle of the 19th Century: Population and Employment (1850–1959) — Walther G. Hoffmann
justification: The strongest direct match for the research requirement. This GESIS HISTAT dataset (ZA8256) contains historical German population and employment statistics covering 1850–1959. It forms part of Hoffmann's comprehensive reconstruction of German economic growth and provides demographic and labor-force information for national income analysis. Particularly relevant for examining long-run employment, labor-force composition, and relationships between population growth and economic development. The dataset covers historical German territories, the German Reich, and postwar West Germany. Researchers should account for changes in territorial definitions, particularly after 1918 and 1945.

returned_title: The Structure of Regional Labor Force in the German Reich and the Federal Republic of Germany, 1895–1970 — Rüdiger Hohls and Hartmut Kaelble
justification: Highly relevant GESIS dataset (ZA8212) providing extensive historical employment statistics, with 5,134 time series. Includes labor-force distribution by industry, economic sector, gender, and occupational status. National summary tables extend from 1882 to 1982, while detailed regional series cover 1895–1970. Particularly useful for examining sectoral workforce changes, female employment, self-employment through occupational-status classifications, and regional differences in industrialization. Some series reconstruct historical employment using consistent territorial boundaries, making the collection especially valuable for longitudinal comparisons and economic growth analysis.

returned_title: Historical German Employment Statistics: Occupational Censuses, Female Labor, and Establishment Censuses (1875–1982)
justification: A particularly relevant historical employment dataset (ZA8180) combining occupational census statistics and establishment census information. Includes historical female labor-force participation, employment by economic sector, occupational distribution, and employment status. Its documented tables include female employment rates for 1882–1970, female workers by economic sector for 1882–1971, and the changing female share of employment across industries for 1882–1982. The associated research also draws on establishment censuses beginning in 1875, making it useful for investigating industrial organization and the relationship between employment structures and economic development.

returned_title: The Growth of the German Economy since the Middle of the 19th Century: Production of Industry and Crafts — Walther G. Hoffmann
justification: An important complementary dataset from Hoffmann's historical reconstruction of the German economy. Covers industrial and craft production within the broader series extending from the mid-19th century to the postwar period. Useful for combining sectoral production measures with workforce statistics to investigate industrial productivity, structural transformation, and economic growth. Particularly valuable alongside Hoffmann's population and employment dataset (ZA8256) when constructing industry-level output-per-worker estimates.

returned_title: The Growth of the German Economy since the Middle of the 19th Century: National Accounts, Production, and Value Added by Economic Sector — Walther G. Hoffmann
justification: A complementary GESIS historical national accounts dataset (ZA8260) from Hoffmann's reconstruction of German economic growth. Covers production, value added by economic sector, and net national product at market prices and factor costs. Especially useful for connecting historical changes in employment, female labor, and industrial workforce composition with national income growth. Provides the output-side information necessary to examine sectoral contributions to economic development alongside historical workforce datasets.

returned_title: The Growth of the German Economy since the Middle of the 19th Century: Labor and Capital Income — Walther G. Hoffmann
justification: A related GESIS dataset (ZA8257) covering labor and capital income within Hoffmann's long-run reconstruction of the German economy. Relevant for assessing income distribution between labor and capital, changes in labor remuneration, and relationships between workforce structure and national income. Useful for integrating historical employment and sectoral workforce series with factor-income measures in economic growth analysis.

returned_title: The Growth Cycles of the German Economy, 1840–1880 — Reinhard Spree
justification: Historical economic time-series dataset (ZA8052) covering the transition from pre-unification German territories to the early German Reich. Includes population and aggregate economic indicators alongside industry-specific series for agriculture, textiles, food processing, mining, metallurgy, machinery, construction, and railways. Particularly useful for analyzing German industrialization during the 1850s, 1860s, and 1870s. Provides supplementary economic indicators for studying how sectoral expansion, population change, and economic cycles interacted during early industrial growth.

returned_title: Selected Historical Time Series on Wages, Salaries, and National Income in Germany, 1850–1985
justification: A historical dataset compilation containing selected German wage, salary, and national income series from 1850 to 1985. Includes Hoffmann's annual average labor income by economic sector for 1850–1959, net national product at factor costs, national income per capita, and gross value added. Particularly useful for connecting long-run employment statistics with compensation, sectoral economic performance, and national income growth. Provides a valuable economic context for workforce and industrial-structure research.

returned_title: Historical Statistics (HISTAT) — GESIS Historical Economic and Social Statistics Database
justification: A comprehensive historical statistics repository maintained by GESIS, containing more than 250,000 historical time series from hundreds of studies, primarily concerning Germany. Particularly relevant for locating additional datasets on historical population, employment, occupational structures, female labor-force participation, industrial development, and enterprise organization. Its chronological coverage includes all requested decades from the 1850s through the 1950s and extends considerably further. The repository provides access to historical datasets suitable for constructing long-run German economic and social indicators. This is a database rather than a single dataset.

returned_title: Historical German Industrial Working Time, 1800–2010 — Jürgen Sensch
justification: GESIS dataset (ZA8503) containing 248 historical time series documenting the development of industrial working time in Germany from the 19th century onward. Includes historical German territories, the German Reich, and modern Germany. Particularly useful as a complementary source when converting historical employment counts into measures of labor input and analyzing changes in labor productivity. Working-time statistics can help distinguish productivity growth arising from workforce expansion from changes in hours worked.

returned_title: Poverty and Unemployment During Industrialization: Düsseldorf, 1850–1900 — Bernd Balkenhol
justification: Historical regional dataset (ZA8497) containing 167 time series covering Düsseldorf between 1850 and 1900. Based on occupational censuses, population censuses, administrative reports, trade chamber records, health insurance records, and trade union documentation. Useful for examining industrial employment, unemployment, occupational structures, and changing labor-market conditions during German industrialization. Although geographically narrower than the requested national series, it provides regional evidence that can supplement aggregate economic growth analysis.

returned_title: The Growth of the German Economy since the Middle of the 19th Century: Agricultural, Forestry, and Fisheries Production — Walther G. Hoffmann
justification: A sector-specific dataset (ZA8242) from Hoffmann's reconstruction of German economic development. Provides historical production information for agriculture, forestry, and fisheries. Relevant for investigating the movement of economic activity and employment from agriculture toward industry and services during German industrialization. Particularly useful alongside historical employment-by-sector series for estimating agricultural labor productivity and examining long-run structural change.

returned_title: The Growth of the German Economy since the Middle of the 19th Century: Mining and Saltworks Production — Walther G. Hoffmann
justification: A historical sectoral production dataset (ZA8253) from Hoffmann's German economic growth series. Covers mining and saltworks, industries that played an important role in 19th- and early-20th-century industrialization. Relevant for comparing industrial production trends with mining employment, sectoral workforce expansion, and productivity changes. Particularly useful for research on the contribution of resource extraction to German industrial and national income growth.

returned_title: The Growth of the German Economy since the Middle of the 19th Century: Transport Production — Walther G. Hoffmann
justification: A complementary historical sectoral dataset (ZA8244) covering transport production within Hoffmann's reconstruction of German economic growth. Useful for investigating the contribution of transportation to industrialization and national income. Can be combined with historical transport employment and occupational statistics to examine productivity, infrastructure-related economic expansion, and the changing role of transport in the German economy.

returned_title: The Growth of the German Economy since the Middle of the 19th Century: Trade, Banking, Insurance, and Hospitality Production — Walther G. Hoffmann
justification: A sectoral economic history dataset (ZA8245) covering production in trade, banking, insurance, and hospitality. Relevant for studying the long-run expansion of service industries and their contribution to German national income. Particularly useful when combined with occupational census information on employment by industry, female labor participation, and the changing distribution of workers between agriculture, manufacturing, and services.

returned_title: Social Structure in the Lignite Area West of the Rhine (Neutral Villages) / Sozialstruktur im linksrheinischen Braunkohlengebiet (Neutrale Orte) (1963) — GESIS ZA0168
justification: Excellent match. This dataset directly investigates the social effects of lignite-mining-related relocation in communities west of the Rhine in North Rhine-Westphalia. Collected in September 1963, it contains standardized interviews with 403 individuals aged 18–75 in communities across the districts of Bergheim, Cologne, Jülich, Aachen, Düren, Euskirchen, Bonn, and Grevenbroich. Variables include social integration, sociability, leisure activities, geographic mobility, housing conditions, rent, homeownership, personal economic circumstances, employment changes, local labor market evaluations, transportation use, media consumption, political party preferences, savings attitudes, and credit purchases. The study examines neutral villages, providing a comparison group for communities affected by resettlement. It uses the same questionnaire as the related relocation-village studies ZA0166 and ZA0167, making it particularly valuable for comparative research.

returned_title: Social Structure in the Lignite Area West of the Rhine (Relocation Villages) — GESIS ZA0166
justification: Highly relevant companion study identified in the GESIS documentation for ZA0168. It covers 299 respondents from villages designated for relocation in the lignite-mining region west of the Rhine. The study used the same standardized questionnaire as ZA0168, enabling comparisons of social integration, mobility, housing, economic circumstances, transportation, media use, and political preferences between communities facing relocation and unaffected communities. It is particularly useful for investigating social conditions associated with anticipated displacement. The study number and sample size are documented in ZA0168; the individual landing page was not independently verified.

returned_title: Social Structure in the Lignite Area West of the Rhine (Relocated Villages) — GESIS ZA0167
justification: Highly relevant companion study identified in the GESIS documentation for ZA0168. It includes 296 respondents from communities already relocated because of lignite mining west of the Rhine. The shared questionnaire allows comparison with relocation villages and neutral villages. Particularly important for the research question, the questionnaire includes an overall evaluation of the resettlement process among respondents who had already relocated. Together, studies ZA0166, ZA0167, and ZA0168 provide a framework for examining differences in social integration, residential conditions, economic well-being, mobility, transportation, and political preferences across communities with different relocation experiences. The study number and sample size are documented in ZA0168; the individual landing page was not independently verified.

returned_title: Residential Buildings, Dwellings, Households and Population per Dwelling within the Territory of North Rhine-Westphalia, 1870–1970 — GESIS ZA8706
justification: Relevant supplementary historical dataset for evaluating changes in housing conditions in North Rhine-Westphalia during the 1960s. It provides information on residential buildings, dwellings, households per dwelling, and population per dwelling, using historical population and housing censuses. Its geographic coverage includes urban and rural districts in North Rhine-Westphalia, and its historical coverage includes the 1960s. It can support contextual analyses of housing availability, residential density, and housing quality in districts affected by lignite mining. Unlike the primary relocation surveys, it does not directly measure individual experiences of displacement or satisfaction with resettlement.

returned_title: Historical Development of Independent Towns, Counties and Their Population within the Borders of North Rhine-Westphalia, 1871–1987 — GESIS ZA8681
justification: Useful supplementary dataset for examining long-term demographic and geographic changes in North Rhine-Westphalia, including the 1960s. It documents population totals, population density, administrative areas, and municipal structures across districts and independent towns. Because the historical data are harmonized to consistent geographic boundaries, researchers can investigate demographic changes before and after the relocation period. It is especially useful for contextualizing community-level population shifts associated with lignite extraction, although it does not independently identify mining-related displacement or measure residents' social integration.

returned_title: District Database / Kreisdatenbank (1939–1975) — GESIS ZA1212
justification: Relevant contextual dataset containing historical aggregate statistics for districts in West Germany, including North Rhine-Westphalia, across selected years between 1939 and 1975. It contains 542 geographic units and 219 variables characterizing district-level conditions. The dataset can help researchers examine broader structural and socioeconomic changes surrounding the 1963 relocation surveys. It is suitable for supplementing individual-level findings with district-level historical context, although it cannot directly measure the experiences or evaluations of relocated residents.

returned_title: Socioeconomic, Political and Fiscal Data for the German Federal States (1960 and 1970) — GESIS ZA0920
justification: Supplementary historical dataset containing socioeconomic, political, and fiscal indicators for German federal states in 1960 and 1970. It includes North Rhine-Westphalia and provides contextual information on population characteristics, employment, transportation, elections, and economic conditions. These indicators may help situate lignite-mining resettlement within broader regional economic and political developments. However, the federal-state level of aggregation is too broad to identify individual mining communities or directly assess relocation outcomes.

returned_title: Urban Planning Data Collection (1968) / Städtebauliche Datenerfassung (1968) — GESIS ZA0488
justification: Relevant comparative dataset examining residential satisfaction, housing conditions, leisure activities, neighborhood relations, transportation, and social environments in selected newly developed residential areas in West Germany. Data were collected in 1968 and include locations in North Rhine-Westphalia, such as Marl. Variables cover housing costs, dwelling characteristics, neighborhood interactions, access to local facilities, transportation choices, and satisfaction with residential environments. Although it does not specifically investigate lignite-mining resettlement west of the Rhine, it provides useful contemporary comparison data for evaluating residential experiences and social integration in newly developed communities during the 1960s.

returned_title: Bildung und Lebenslauf (Gymnasiasten-Studie, 2. Welle) / Education and Life Course (Cologne High School Panel, Second Wave, 1984–1985)
justification: Excellent match and the most directly relevant dataset. This longitudinal follow-up surveyed approximately 1,987 former high school students who had attended the 10th grade at Gymnasium schools in North Rhine-Westphalia in 1969–1970. Conducted in 1984–1985, when respondents were approximately 30 years old, it reconstructed educational and occupational trajectories since leaving school. It covers university education, vocational training, employment histories, occupational advancement, income, marriage, family formation, social background, political and social attitudes, and life satisfaction. Particularly valuable for examining transitions from secondary education into higher education, vocational training, employment, and adult family life in West Germany during the 1970s and 1980s.

returned_title: Lebenserfolg und Erfolgsdeutung im frühen Erwachsenenalter (Gymnasiasten-Studie, 3. Welle) / Life Success and Interpretations of Success in Early Adulthood (Cologne High School Panel, Third Wave)
justification: Excellent longitudinal match. This dataset belongs to the same North Rhine-Westphalia high school cohort originally surveyed in 1969–1970 and followed up in 1984–1985. The third wave, conducted in 1996–1997, extends participants' educational, professional, and personal histories into middle adulthood. It examines occupational careers, educational qualifications, professional success, partnership and family development, social mobility, subjective assessments of success, values, attitudes, and life satisfaction. Although collected after the 1980s, it provides retrospective and longitudinal evidence for understanding how educational and career decisions made during that decade influenced later outcomes.

returned_title: Strukturanalyse der Schule – Schülerbefragung (Gymnasiasten-Studie) / Structural Analysis of Schools – Student Survey (Cologne High School Panel, Baseline)
justification: Essential baseline dataset for longitudinal analysis. Conducted in 1969–1970 among approximately 3,240 students attending Gymnasium schools in North Rhine-Westphalia, this survey established the original cohort subsequently followed during the 1980s. It documents educational aspirations, school performance, family and social origins, relationships with parents, occupational expectations, personal values, social attitudes, and future plans. Linking this baseline with the 1984–1985 follow-up allows researchers to investigate how adolescent socioeconomic circumstances, aspirations, and attitudes shaped later educational attainment, vocational pathways, employment, family formation, and life satisfaction.

returned_title: Soziale Herkunft und Schullaufbahn von Gymnasiasten (Gymnasiasten-Studie) / Social Origins and School Careers of High School Students
justification: Highly relevant supplementary longitudinal dataset documenting educational progression among the original North Rhine-Westphalia Gymnasium cohort. Information collected from school records and supplementary inquiries during the early 1980s reconstructs students' secondary-school trajectories, school changes, completion of educational qualifications, Abitur attainment, and examination outcomes. The dataset can be connected conceptually and through the original study framework to the 1969–1970 baseline and 1984–1985 adult follow-up. It is especially useful for examining relationships between social origin, academic achievement, access to higher education, vocational alternatives, and subsequent employment opportunities.

returned_title: Strukturanalyse der Schule – Elternbefragung (Gymnasiasten-Studie) / Structural Analysis of Schools – Parent Survey
justification: Relevant baseline companion dataset from the Cologne High School Panel, covering parents of students attending Gymnasium schools in North Rhine-Westphalia in 1969–1970. It provides additional information on parental and family circumstances relevant to understanding social origins, educational opportunities, and intergenerational inequality. Used alongside the student baseline and subsequent longitudinal follow-ups, it supports analysis of how family background influenced higher education participation, vocational training decisions, occupational attainment, and social mobility during the 1980s. Its primary value is as a source of explanatory background variables rather than as an independent 1980s follow-up.

returned_title: Strukturanalyse der Schule – Direktorenbefragung (Gymnasiasten-Studie) / Structural Analysis of Schools – School Directors Survey
justification: Complementary institutional dataset from the original North Rhine-Westphalia Gymnasium study. Surveyed in December 1969 and January 1970, school directors from 68 schools provided information about educational organization, school characteristics, educational approaches, student socioeconomic composition, and local school environments. Although this is a cross-sectional baseline dataset rather than a follow-up, it can provide institutional context for analyzing subsequent educational and occupational trajectories of the original cohort during the 1980s. Particularly useful for investigating how school environments and social composition contributed to educational inequality and later career outcomes.

returned_title: Cologne High School Panel (CHiSP) / Kölner Gymnasiastenpanel
justification: Official project landing page for the longitudinal study that most closely matches the research requirements. The Cologne High School Panel began with 3,240 students from 68 Gymnasium schools in North Rhine-Westphalia in 1969–1970. Subsequent follow-ups in 1984–1985, 1996–1997, 2010, and 2019–2020 trace participants' educational achievements, university and vocational training experiences, employment histories, occupational careers, marriage and family formation, social origins, values, attitudes, and subjective well-being. The project provides a framework for identifying related survey waves and understanding the longitudinal design. The 1984–1985 wave is especially relevant to the requested historical period.

returned_title: Chancenzuweisung durch Ausbildung (Längsschnitt 1971–2002) / Allocation of Opportunities Through Education (Longitudinal Study, 1971–2002)
justification: Strong supplementary longitudinal dataset examining how educational opportunities and social background shape occupational and personal trajectories in West Germany. Beginning in 1971–1972, the study followed young people and their families across successive survey waves, including observations during the 1980s. Topics include parental socioeconomic circumstances, educational aspirations, school careers, vocational training, occupational expectations, employment biographies, family circumstances, social networks, values, and attitudes. It is particularly useful for investigating intergenerational educational inequality and school-to-work transitions. Its geographic coverage and sample differ from the Cologne High School Panel, so it should be treated as a complementary source rather than an exact cohort match.

returned_title: Jugend, Ausbildung und Beruf / Youth, Vocational Training and Employment (1984)
justification: Relevant contemporary dataset collected in October 1984 among apprentices in West Germany, including the Federal Republic and West Berlin. It focuses on vocational choices, apprenticeship experiences, training occupations, applications for training positions, employment expectations, and perceived career opportunities. The study also examines influences on occupational decision-making and attitudes toward education and employment. It provides useful comparative evidence on vocational education and school-to-work transitions during the same period as the Cologne High School Panel's first adult follow-up. However, it is not restricted to North Rhine-Westphalia, does not specifically follow former Gymnasium students, and is not itself a longitudinal panel.

returned_title: ALLBUS/GGSS 1984 – Allgemeine Bevölkerungsumfrage der Sozialwissenschaften / German General Social Survey 1984
justification: Useful contextual dataset for examining social attitudes, family life, social inequality, and political orientations in West Germany during the 1980s. Conducted between March and June 1984, the survey interviewed approximately 3,004 adults in the Federal Republic of Germany and West Berlin. Its subject areas include social conditions, political behavior and attitudes, marriage and family life, social inequality, and social values. It can support comparisons between the former high school students in the Cologne panel and the broader West German adult population. However, it is a cross-sectional survey rather than a longitudinal follow-up, and North Rhine-Westphalia-specific analysis depends on the availability of suitable geographic identifiers.

returned_title: Cologne High School Panel – Fourth Follow-up and Cumulative Longitudinal Data
justification: Highly relevant for extending analysis of the original North Rhine-Westphalia high school cohort across the adult life course. This dataset corresponds to the 2010 follow-up, when participants were approximately 56 years old, and includes cumulative longitudinal information from earlier waves. Topics include educational attainment, occupational careers, employment transitions, marriage and family histories, financial circumstances, social identification, personal attitudes, and life satisfaction. Although the follow-up was conducted considerably later than the 1980s, it enables researchers to examine the long-term consequences of educational and occupational transitions that occurred during that decade. It is particularly valuable for studying career development, family trajectories, and the persistence of social inequalities.

returned_title: CROCorp: Corpus of Parliamentary Debates in Croatia (v1.1.1, 2003–2020)
justification: Exact match. Created by Michal Mochtak, Josip Glaurdić, and Christophe Lesschaeve (2022), this dataset provides a cleaned and preprocessed corpus of debates from the Croatian Parliament (Sabor) covering 2003–2020. It includes five complete parliamentary terms, over 500,000 speeches, and metadata on elected representatives and their political parties. Version 1.1.1 is available through Zenodo and directly satisfies all specified research requirements.

returned_title: CROCorp: Corpus of Parliamentary Debates in Croatia — Zenodo Dataset Record
justification: Official Zenodo landing page for CROCorp version 1.1.1. Provides access to the cleaned parliamentary debate corpus, accompanying metadata, documentation, and citation information. Covers Croatian parliamentary proceedings from 2003 through 2020, encompassing five complete terms and more than 500,000 speeches. This is an alternative access point for the exact-match dataset.

returned_title: CROCorp: Corpus of Parliamentary Debates in Croatia — GESIS Data Catalogue
justification: GESIS research data catalogue entry documenting the CROCorp dataset. Confirms its coverage of Croatian parliamentary debates from 2003–2020, five complete parliamentary terms, more than 500,000 speeches, and associated metadata on parliamentary representatives and political parties. Useful for dataset discovery, verification, and research documentation.

returned_title: CROCorp: Corpus of Parliamentary Debates in Croatia — University of Luxembourg Research Repository
justification: Institutional repository record maintained by the University of Luxembourg for CROCorp version 1.1.1, published in 2022. Documents the cleaned and preprocessed corpus of Croatian parliamentary debates spanning 2003–2020, including metadata about elected representatives and political parties. Provides access to the accompanying codebook and bibliographic information.

returned_title: ParlaCAP: Dataset for Tracking Political Agenda-Setting Across European Parliaments
justification: Related multilingual parliamentary debate dataset that includes Croatia. Extends the ParlaMint parliamentary corpus by providing automatically classified speech topics and sentiment information. Useful for supplementary research on political agendas, parliamentary discourse, and party-level differences. Its scope extends beyond Croatia and the requested 2003–2020 period, so it is a complementary resource rather than an exact replacement for CROCorp.

returned_title: Krisenmonitor (Woche 8/2024) / Crisis Monitor (Week 8/2024) — GESIS Study ZA8738
justification: Exact match to the research need. This representative telephone survey (CATI) was conducted by forsa from February 19–21, 2024, among German-speaking residents aged 14 and older in Germany. Commissioned by the Press and Information Office of the German Federal Government, it examines public perceptions of ongoing crises, personal concerns about developments in Germany, political disagreements, democratic participation, perceived conflicts between political and social groups, and attitudes toward democracy. It belongs to the Crisis Monitor series, which continues the Ukraine War Trend Questions surveys initiated in March 2022. The dataset is particularly suitable for investigating political attitudes, crisis perceptions, democratic values, political polarization, and changes in German public opinion in the context of the Ukraine war. Available through the GESIS Data Archive under study identifier ZA8738.

returned_title: Krisenmonitor (Woche 8/2024) / Crisis Monitor (Week 8/2024) — B2FIND Dataset Record
justification: Alternative discovery record for the exact February 2024 dataset, providing detailed German-language metadata about the survey population, telephone interview methodology, collection dates, and questionnaire topics. The record documents questions about personal experiences of current crises, political disputes, democratic engagement, perceived threats to democracy, and ideological conflicts between political groups. Particularly useful for verifying the dataset's suitability for research on government, political systems, political behaviour, political attitudes, and political ideology in Germany. This is the same underlying survey as GESIS ZA8738, not an independent sample.

returned_title: Krisenmonitor (Woche 16/2024) / Crisis Monitor (Week 16/2024)
justification: Highly relevant follow-up survey from the same Crisis Monitor series, conducted April 18–22, 2024, using telephone interviews with German-speaking residents aged 14 and older. Although collected after the requested February period, it provides complementary information on public anxiety about the Ukraine war, perceptions of responsibility for the Russia–Ukraine conflict, attitudes toward negotiations, evaluations of Germany's response to the Russian invasion, and opinions about Western sanctions. Suitable for examining changes in crisis perceptions and foreign-policy attitudes during 2024.

returned_title: Trendfragen Ukraine (Woche 48/2022) / Ukraine War Trend Questions (Week 48/2022) — GESIS Study ZA7924
justification: Relevant historical comparison dataset from the predecessor series to the 2024 Crisis Monitor. Conducted November 28–30, 2022, through representative computer-assisted telephone interviews with German-speaking residents aged 14 and older. The survey examines public attitudes toward Germany and the Ukraine war. It uses the same target population and general survey approach as the February 2024 Crisis Monitor, making it useful for longitudinal comparisons of public opinion about the war and related political developments. Questionnaire differences should be checked before conducting trend analyses.

returned_title: Einstellungen zu Hochschule und Politik 1969 (Attitudes to College and Politics 1969) — GESIS ZA0363
justification: Excellent match for research on West Germany's student protest movement. This 1969 survey of University of Cologne students examines attitudes toward the Socialist German Student Union (SDS), Extra-Parliamentary Opposition (APO), student demonstrations, political protest, violence, and government sanctions against students. It includes assessments of APO effectiveness, political participation, university politics, and satisfaction with Chancellor Kiesinger's government. Demographic variables include age, gender, marital status, religion, social background, and educational characteristics. Political variables include respondents' party preferences, parental party preferences, and sympathy ratings for CDU, SPD, FDP, NPD, and DFU. Particularly valuable for investigating relationships between student activism, political affiliations, and attitudes toward government intervention.

returned_title: Student and College Politics — University of Cologne, 1967–1968 (GESIS ZA0286)
justification: Highly relevant historical student survey conducted among students enrolled at the University of Cologne during the 1967–1968 winter semester. This dataset represents the first wave of a panel study, with the second wave available as GESIS ZA0363. It offers an opportunity to investigate student political attitudes during the emergence of West Germany's protest movement and compare them with responses collected in 1969. Researchers should examine the questionnaire and variable documentation to establish which SDS, APO, demonstration, government-response, and party-preference measures are available in this earlier wave.

returned_title: Public Opinion Surveys: West Germany, November 1968 — ICPSR 7090
justification: Relevant nationally oriented public opinion survey conducted in West Germany in November 1968, during the period of major student demonstrations and political controversy. Based on interviews with 666 adults, the dataset covers attitudes toward the federal government, Chancellor, President, political parties, community problems, and government responses. It provides historical public opinion evidence beyond university populations. Particularly useful for studying political evaluations during the student protest era, although the published summary does not confirm questions specifically addressing SDS, APO, student demonstrations, or an SDS ban. The German-language questionnaire should be consulted before treating it as a direct measure of protest attitudes.

returned_title: Public Opinion Surveys: West Germany, December 1968 — ICPSR 7091
justification: Historical public opinion survey of 712 adults conducted in West Germany in December 1968. It examines public evaluations of government officials, political parties, economic conditions, and administrative responses to public concerns. Its timing makes it relevant for analyzing political attitudes following the major student demonstrations of 1968. It can complement the November 1968 survey when examining changes in political opinion. However, specific measures of attitudes toward SDS, APO, protest organizers, or prohibiting student organizations are not established in the published description and require verification against the questionnaire.

returned_title: Issue-Dimensionen und Wahlentscheidung (April 1969) — GESIS ZA0395
justification: Relevant West German survey examining political issues and electoral decision-making in April 1969, shortly after the peak of the 1967–1968 student protest movement. Classified by GESIS under political behaviour and attitudes, government, political systems and organisations, and elections. It is potentially useful for connecting public opinion on political controversies to electoral preferences and party identification. Researchers should inspect the questionnaire to determine whether student demonstrations, SDS/APO activities, protest restrictions, and government responses were explicitly measured. Its principal value is as a complementary dataset for analyzing the political and electoral context of the student movement.

returned_title: Preconditions of the Formation of Public Opinion in the Federal Republic of Germany, 1964 — ICPSR 7014
justification: Useful historical baseline for understanding West German political attitudes before the student protest movement intensified. The collection contains four national cross-sectional surveys of the West German electorate conducted between May and July 1964. Variables cover attitudes toward the federal government, political parties, domestic and international political issues, knowledge of politicians, and evaluations of political figures. Although it predates the major SDS/APO demonstrations and therefore cannot directly measure reactions to the 1967–1968 protests, it provides comparative evidence on earlier political orientations and public trust in government.

returned_title: Partner III - Apprentices 1990 (Partner III - Lehrlinge 1990)
justification: Excellent match. Conducted in 1990 by the Central Institute for Youth Research (ZIJ) in Leipzig, this survey investigates romantic relationships, attitudes toward love and sexuality, and sexual behavior among young apprentices in the German Democratic Republic during the AIDS era. It covers sexual development, first intercourse, contraception, homosexuality, sexual experiences, partner relationships, pregnancy-related issues, family background, relationships with parents, and social integration. Particularly relevant for studying adolescent sexuality and reproductive health in the final year of the GDR.

returned_title: Partner III - Students 1990 (Partner III - Studenten 1990)
justification: Excellent match. Conducted between April and June 1990 by the Central Institute for Youth Research in Leipzig and collaborating sexual research institutions, this dataset examines romantic partnerships, sexual attitudes, and sexual behavior among students in the GDR. It addresses sexual experiences and relationships in the context of AIDS, including sexual initiation, contraception, partner selection, homosexuality, reproductive attitudes, and family relationships. It is especially useful for comparing university students with apprentices and employed young adults surveyed through the Partner III research program.

returned_title: Partner III - Employed 1990 (Partner III - Berufstätige 1990)
justification: Excellent match. This 1990 survey by the Central Institute for Youth Research in Leipzig investigates the development of romantic and sexual relationships among young employed adults in East Germany. Its central focus includes attitudes toward love and sexuality, sexual behavior during the AIDS epidemic, partnership development, and reproductive health. The survey also examines personal well-being, occupational and social integration, attitudes toward children, and the interaction between employment, family life, and relationships. It provides a valuable comparison group for the student and apprentice samples.

returned_title: Partner III - Homosexuality 1990 (Partner III - Homosexualität 1990)
justification: Highly relevant supplementary dataset. Conducted in autumn 1990, this survey investigates the everyday lives, relationships, and sexual experiences of homosexual people in the former GDR. It contains 535 observations and 321 variables. Topics include coming out, parental acceptance, family environment, first homosexual experiences, sexual activities, contraception, romantic partnerships, attitudes toward children, experiences of discrimination and violence, and knowledge and perceived risks of AIDS. It also covers the consequences of AIDS for sexual behavior and experiences with sexually transmitted diseases. Particularly valuable for examining homosexuality, sexual minority experiences, family relationships, and HIV-related attitudes during the political transition of 1990.

returned_title: Partner III - Homosexual Women 1991–1993 (Partner III - Homosexuelle Frauen 1991/93)
justification: Relevant supplementary dataset from the Partner III research program, specifically focusing on homosexual women during the early post-reunification period. Identified in GESIS documentation as a comparison study to Partner III - Homosexuality 1990, it offers an opportunity to investigate lesbian experiences and relationships in the context of East Germany's social transformation. It is particularly relevant to research on sexual orientation, intimate relationships, and the experiences of sexual minorities during the early 1990s. The precise questionnaire coverage should be checked before assuming that all requested reproductive health and AIDS-related variables are available.

returned_title: AIDS Awareness among the Population of the GDR 1990 (AIDS im Bewusstsein der Bevölkerung der DDR 1990)
justification: Relevant complementary dataset examining awareness and perceptions of AIDS among the population of the German Democratic Republic in 1990. It is particularly useful for contextualizing sexual behavior and HIV-related attitudes during the final phase of the GDR. The survey provides a potential basis for studying public understanding of AIDS and the social environment in which young people formed intimate relationships. Unlike the Partner III studies, its primary focus is AIDS awareness rather than the full range of adolescent romantic relationships, sexual experiences, and family dynamics.

returned_title: Partner II 1979/80
justification: Highly relevant historical comparison dataset, although collected before the requested 1990s period and before the AIDS epidemic became a major public health concern. Conducted in the GDR in 1979–1980, this study investigates romantic relationships, first intercourse, contraception, homosexual experiences, sexual development, partner relationships, and attitudes toward marriage and sexuality. It also includes information about family background, parents' education, sexual education within the family, and relationships with partners. Particularly useful for comparing the sexual attitudes and behavior of East German young people before the AIDS era with those documented by the Partner III surveys in 1990.

returned_title: Group-Oriented Animosity Against People (GMF Survey 2011) / Gruppenbezogene Menschenfeindlichkeit 2011
justification: Excellent match and the strongest single dataset for the research need. This German population survey examines perceptions of the financial and economic crisis, authoritarianism, xenophobia, racism, antisemitism, sexism, homophobia, anti-Muslim attitudes, discrimination, devaluation of minorities, political alienation, nationalism, and social integration. It includes perceptions of economic insecurity, social inequality, political effectiveness, democratic dissatisfaction, national identification, and attitudes toward immigrants. Socioeconomic and demographic information supports comparisons across social groups. Particularly valuable for examining how economic insecurity and perceived social threats relate to prejudice and exclusion in Germany in 2011.

returned_title: Group-Oriented Animosity Against People (GMF Survey 2010) / Gruppenbezogene Menschenfeindlichkeit 2010
justification: Very strong match. This survey investigates group-focused prejudice and hostility in Germany during the aftermath of the global financial crisis. Relevant themes include xenophobia, racism, antisemitism, sexism, homophobia, authoritarian attitudes, social exclusion, economic insecurity, and negative evaluations of minority groups. The dataset is useful for investigating relationships between perceived economic threats, social status, political dissatisfaction, and discriminatory attitudes. Its demographic and socioeconomic variables allow analysis of differences across population groups. Particularly useful for comparisons with the 2011 GMF survey.

returned_title: Group-Oriented Animosity Against People (GMF Surveys 2002–2011) / Gruppenbezogene Menschenfeindlichkeit
justification: The GMF research program is an especially relevant source for studying changes in prejudice, authoritarian attitudes, political alienation, and social integration in Germany. Its annual surveys provide opportunities to compare attitudes before and after the 2008 financial crisis, including observations from 2010 and 2011. The research program covers racism, xenophobia, antisemitism, sexism, homophobia, hostility toward Muslims, perceived economic disadvantage, national identity, and devaluation of socially disadvantaged groups. The linked record identifies the 2011 wave; earlier waves are available as separate datasets.

returned_title: German General Social Survey (ALLBUS) 2010
justification: Highly relevant nationally representative German survey for studying political attitudes, socioeconomic stratification, national identification, and social integration around 2010. ALLBUS provides detailed demographic and socioeconomic variables, including education, employment, occupation, income-related measures, and migration-related characteristics. Its recurring questions enable comparisons of political orientations, economic evaluations, social inequality, and attitudes toward immigrants across time. The 2010 wave provides an important baseline for examining German society immediately after the financial crisis.

returned_title: German General Social Survey (ALLBUS) 2012
justification: Relevant for examining social inequality, political attitudes, economic perceptions, national identification, and attitudes toward immigrants in Germany during the early 2010s. The survey contains extensive demographic and socioeconomic information that enables stratified analysis by education, occupation, employment, income, and migration-related characteristics. Its standardized measurements are especially useful for comparisons with the 2010, 2014, 2016, and 2018 ALLBUS waves. Specific prejudice and identity measures should be checked against the wave questionnaire.

returned_title: German General Social Survey (ALLBUS) 2014
justification: Strong complementary dataset for investigating political behavior, social stratification, economic evaluations, and cultural and national identity in Germany. It provides detailed socioeconomic indicators and recurring measures of political and social attitudes. The survey is useful for identifying differences between social classes, educational groups, and people with different migration-related characteristics. It also supports longitudinal comparisons of public attitudes during the period between the financial crisis and the 2015 refugee migration developments.

returned_title: German General Social Survey (ALLBUS) 2016
justification: Highly relevant for examining German public attitudes toward immigration, minority groups, political institutions, national identity, and social integration during the refugee migration period. It offers extensive socioeconomic and demographic information and can support analyses of how education, occupational status, economic circumstances, and migration-related characteristics correlate with political and cultural attitudes. The 2016 survey also has a supplementary dataset containing responses to an open-ended question about foreigners, making it particularly useful for research on immigration-related perceptions.

returned_title: German General Social Survey (ALLBUS) 2018
justification: Valuable nationally representative dataset for studying political attitudes, perceptions of inequality, immigration, identity, and social divisions in Germany toward the end of the 2010s. It contains detailed socioeconomic information and recurring attitude questions that facilitate comparisons with earlier ALLBUS waves. The dataset supports examination of differences in political orientations and social attitudes across educational, occupational, economic, regional, and migration-related groups. Especially useful for identifying longer-term changes during the decade.

returned_title: German General Social Survey (ALLBUS) Cumulation 1980–2014
justification: Particularly useful for studying changes in German political attitudes, social inequality, national identification, and perceptions of minority groups across multiple survey years. The cumulative dataset combines harmonized variables from repeated ALLBUS surveys, including observations from the early 2010s. Relevant measures cover political participation, democratic attitudes, redistribution, economic evaluations, immigration, and social attitudes. Its demographic and socioeconomic variables make it suitable for examining how social stratification and political orientations change over time. It is especially valuable for placing the economic crisis period within a longer historical context.

returned_title: German General Social Survey (ALLBUS) – Complete Dataset Collection
justification: Useful for identifying specific ALLBUS variables measuring xenophobia, antisemitism, attitudes toward immigration, national pride, national identification, perceived inequality, and political orientations. The official thematic overview provides crosswalks showing which variables were collected in particular survey years. This helps researchers identify the most suitable 2010s survey waves and construct comparable measures across time. Particularly valuable when combining prejudice and identity measures with detailed socioeconomic and migration-background information.

returned_title: German Longitudinal Election Study (GLES)
justification: Relevant complementary source for political behavior, democratic attitudes, political alienation, nationalism, and immigration-related political preferences in Germany during the 2010s. GLES provides election-related surveys covering political participation, party preferences, political trust, ideological orientations, and evaluations of political issues. Its demographic and socioeconomic variables support analyses of relationships between social inequality, migration-related attitudes, and political behavior. It is particularly useful for examining how concerns about immigration and economic insecurity relate to electoral preferences and political dissatisfaction.

returned_title: Politbarometer – German Political Opinion Surveys
justification: Relevant repeated German political opinion surveys covering government evaluations, political dissatisfaction, economic expectations, party preferences, democratic satisfaction, and attitudes toward asylum and immigration. The series provides frequent observations throughout the 2010s, making it suitable for investigating changes in political attitudes during economic uncertainty and periods of heightened migration-related debate. Demographic and socioeconomic variables allow comparisons between population groups. Although less comprehensive than the GMF surveys for specific forms of prejudice, it is especially useful for political alienation and economic crisis perceptions.

returned_title: GESIS Panel – German Longitudinal Population Survey, 2013–2019 Waves
justification: Relevant longitudinal survey infrastructure for investigating how political attitudes, social integration, perceptions of inequality, and social identities change within the German population. Beginning in 2013, the panel offers repeated observations and demographic background information that can support analyses of attitudes across socioeconomic and migration-related groups. Depending on the selected modules and waves, researchers can investigate immigration-related attitudes, social trust, political orientations, and perceived social divisions. Particularly valuable for studying individual-level changes rather than relying exclusively on repeated cross-sectional surveys.

returned_title: German System of Social Indicators: Participation, 1950–2013
justification: Useful supplementary dataset for contextualizing political participation and social integration in Germany during the early 2010s. It provides long-term quantitative indicators of social change, participation, and quality of life, extending through 2013. Unlike the GMF and ALLBUS surveys, this is primarily a social-indicator dataset rather than individual-level survey microdata. It can therefore provide historical and structural context for research on political alienation, participation, and social inequality, but is not a direct substitute for surveys measuring specific prejudices.

returned_title: German System of Social Indicators: Labour Market and Employment Conditions, 1950–2013
justification: Relevant contextual dataset for investigating economic insecurity, employment conditions, and social stratification surrounding the financial crisis and its aftermath. It contains historical indicators of labour market conditions and socioeconomic change in Germany through 2013. Researchers can use it to contextualize the economic circumstances associated with perceived threats, political dissatisfaction, and minority-related attitudes measured in individual-level surveys. Its main limitation is that it does not directly measure racism, xenophobia, antisemitism, or authoritarianism.

returned_title: Schülerintervallstudie Gesundheitserziehung und Gesunderhaltung 1987 bis 1991 (Welle 1 bis 3)
justification: Excellent match and the most directly relevant dataset identified. This longitudinal survey of schoolchildren in the German Democratic Republic, conducted between 1987 and 1991, examines health education, self-reported health, dental hygiene, dental examinations, nutrition, dietary preferences, and preventive health behaviors. The questionnaires include questions about seeking information on illness, injuries, first aid, alcohol and nicotine risks, sexually transmitted diseases, skin conditions, toothaches, and diabetes. They also investigate parental responsibility for healthy eating, smoking, and dental care, as well as health education provided by parents, teachers, doctors, dentists, and nurses. The study is particularly valuable for investigating health knowledge, family influences, school-related experiences, and changes in health behavior during the transition from the GDR to reunified Germany.

returned_title: Gesundheit 1990 (Health 1990)
justification: Highly relevant survey dataset collected in the former German Democratic Republic beginning in June 1990 by the Department of Medical Sociology at the Institute for Social Hygiene and Health Care Organization in Berlin. The survey covers individuals aged 14 and older and provides evidence for examining population health and health-related attitudes during the transition from the GDR to reunification. It is particularly relevant to research on general health and well-being, health-related behavior, and the social context of health care. Its detailed questionnaire should be consulted to determine which measures of medical treatment, prevention, and specific health conditions are available.

returned_title: Leben in der DDR 1990 (Life in the GDR 1990)
justification: Relevant survey conducted in January 1990 in the GDR districts of Potsdam, Leipzig, and Schwerin. It examines social conditions and attitudes during the political and economic transformation of East Germany. The questionnaire includes the importance of health as a domain of life, knowledge about healthy lifestyles, social security, education, family relationships, and general life satisfaction. It is useful for examining health-related knowledge, perceived well-being, and the social and family contexts influencing health behavior. Although less focused on clinical conditions or dental hygiene, it provides valuable contextual measures for research on health education and well-being in the final year of the GDR.

returned_title: Alltagsprobleme Jugendlicher in der DDR 1988 (Everyday Problems of Young People in the GDR 1988)
justification: Relevant historical youth survey conducted in the German Democratic Republic in 1988 by the Central Institute for Youth Research in Leipzig. It provides contemporary evidence on the everyday experiences and concerns of young people in the late GDR period. It is a potentially useful complementary dataset for investigating adolescent well-being, family relationships, educational experiences, and the social circumstances surrounding health behavior. Its relevance to specific questions about nutrition, dental care, substance use, and illness prevention requires verification against the questionnaire and variable documentation.

returned_title: Jugendstudie mit Gesundheitszusatzfragebogen (Youth Study with Supplementary Health Questionnaire)
justification: Relevant GDR youth research dataset that includes a supplementary health questionnaire.
