The study examines young people's orientations and activities, including physical culture, sports participation, and health-related topics. It is useful for studying adolescent health behavior, physical activity, health awareness, and associations between lifestyle and educational or social characteristics during the 1980s. The supplementary health questionnaire makes it a promising source for additional measures of health and well-being, although the availability of specific nutrition, dental hygiene, and medical-treatment variables should be checked.

returned_title: Lebensbedingungen und Lebensweise von Schülern – Elternbefragung (Living Conditions and Lifestyles of Schoolchildren – Parent Survey)
justification: Relevant survey of parents conducted between September 1989 and April 1990 as part of the broader GDR research project on the living conditions and lifestyles of schoolchildren. It provides a complementary parental perspective for studying family environments, educational experiences, parental involvement, and children's everyday lives during the final months of the GDR. It is especially useful for research on family responsibility and the relationship between parental attitudes and children's development. Its coverage of specific health education, nutrition, dental care, or preventive health practices needs to be established from the questionnaire.

returned_title: Schülerintervallstudie Fähigkeiten – Längsschnittuntersuchung (Longitudinal Study of Schoolchildren's Abilities)
justification: Relevant longitudinal schoolchildren's survey associated with research on adolescent development, abilities, and risk situations in the GDR. The study belongs to a series of surveys that continued after reunification in eastern Germany through the project on adolescent risk situations and risk behavior. It is particularly useful for examining school performance, developmental outcomes, and educational factors that may be associated with health behavior and family influences. It offers a complementary perspective to the health education survey, although detailed coverage of nutrition, dental hygiene, and specific diseases is not established.

returned_title: Gesellschaftliche und politische Einstellungen 2024 (Social and Political Attitudes 2024)
justification: Excellent match for the research need. This 2024 German survey covers social and political attitudes, including respondents' satisfaction with their personal financial situation, overall life satisfaction, perceptions of federal government policies, satisfaction with democracy, and assessments of political and social conditions. The questionnaire also addresses international political issues, including European and global developments. It is particularly relevant for studying political behaviour and attitudes, government and political systems, and international politics in Germany.

returned_title: Gesellschaftliche und politische Einstellungen 2024 – GESIS Survey Documentation
justification: GESIS provides access to the 2024 Social and Political Attitudes study, which closely matches the requested telephone survey of Germany's population aged 14 and older. The study includes assessments of personal finances, satisfaction with different areas of life, perceptions of federal government communications and policies, and views on European and global political developments. Search for 'Gesellschaftliche und politische Einstellungen 2024' to locate the dataset and associated documentation.

returned_title: Sofortresonanzen DDR Fernsehen 36. Woche 1985 (SFR 36/85)
justification: Highly relevant survey dataset from 1985 examining television viewing participation and program evaluations in the German Democratic Republic. Includes audience reactions to the police drama POLIZEIRUF 110 – EIN SCHRITT ZU WEIT, specifically its suspense, entertainment value, perceived realism, and fulfillment of viewer expectations. Also evaluates other television films and sports programs. Based on a representative household sample, with demographic information suitable for analyzing differences between viewer groups.

returned_title: Sofortresonanzen DDR Fernsehen 35. Woche 1988 (SFR 35/88)
justification: Excellent match for research on audience reactions to police dramas and entertainment programming. This 1988 DDR television survey evaluates the POLIZEIRUF 110 episode EIFERSUCHT, including entertainment value, realism, audience appreciation of main characters, and specific narrative elements. It also examines audience evaluations of the entertainment show GLÜCK MUSS MAN HABEN, including its host, humor, participating couples, and program components. Contains weekly viewing participation and program ratings collected through representative household sampling.

returned_title: Sofortresonanzen DDR Fernsehen 13. Woche 1985 (SFR 13/85)
justification: Directly relevant to evaluations of police drama episodes and preferred television scheduling. The survey investigates audience reactions to POLIZEIRUF 110 – TRAUM DES VERGESSENS, including suspense, perceived realism, and whether the episode met expectations. Additional questions explore interest in cultural programming, preferred broadcast days, viewing frequency, working conditions, fatigue after work, and expectations of television entertainment. Useful for studying relationships between viewing preferences, employment circumstances, and audience demographics.

returned_title: Sofortresonanzen DDR Fernsehen 50. Woche 1982 (SFR 50/82)
justification: Particularly relevant to Saturday evening entertainment and music programming in the early 1980s. Contains weekly television viewing participation and program evaluations, including audience assessments of KLOCK 8, ACHTERN STROM, its humor and entertainment value, suggestions for improvement, and preferences for suitable Saturday evening programming. Also examines viewing and evaluations of the musical series BUSCH SINGT, preferred broadcast days for VERKEHRSKOMPASS, and television viewing opportunities during holidays. Includes demographic variables for audience segmentation.

returned_title: Sofortresonanzen DDR Fernsehen 39. Woche 1982 (SFR 39/82)
justification: Strong match for research on Saturday evening entertainment and music shows. Includes questions evaluating whether coverage of an international Schlager music festival was appropriate for Saturday evening television. Also examines audience assessments of the entertainment production KOMM MIT MIR NACH CHICAGO, including relaxation, enjoyment, character identification, representation of young people's experiences, and overall impressions. Further questions evaluate the quiz show KNOBELEIEN, its presenters, format, and studio games. Provides valuable evidence on viewer preferences and entertainment program reception in the DDR.

returned_title: Sofortresonanzen DDR Fernsehen 28. Woche 1989 (SFR 28/89)
justification: Relevant survey dataset covering television participation, program evaluations, and music entertainment near the end of the DDR. Includes audience ratings of performers and the host of SHOWKOLADE, reception of PFUNDGRUBE, evaluations of a presenter, and satisfaction with the diversity of musical offerings. Also examines general satisfaction with DDR television programming and other cultural and informational content. Particularly useful for studying audience preferences for music shows, presenter appeal, and entertainment formats.

returned_title: Sofortresonanzen DDR Fernsehen 46. Woche 1984 (SFR 46/84)
justification: Especially relevant to preferred viewing times, household viewing practices, and demographic influences on television consumption. Includes questions about desired broadcast times for a new youth television program, parental influence on children's viewing behavior, knowledge of television schedules, and the effects of shift work on viewing opportunities. Also measures weekly program participation and evaluations. Demographic variables include age, gender, education, employment, household size, and political affiliation. Particularly valuable for investigating how social and occupational characteristics shaped television preferences.

returned_title: Sofortresonanzen DDR Fernsehen 6. Woche 1983 (SFR 6/83)
justification: Relevant to entertainment programming, musical and cultural formats, and age-specific audience preferences. Investigates evaluations of the youth-oriented program BONG, including entertainment value, presenter appeal, and perceived target age group. Also examines regular viewing and evaluations of KLOCK 8, ACHTERN STROM, audience opinions about program improvements, and attitudes toward scheduling entertainment across different weekdays. Suitable for studying age-related preferences and audience responses to entertainment formats.

returned_title: Sofortresonanzen DDR Fernsehen 14. Woche 1982 (SFR 14/82)
justification: Useful supplementary dataset on television participation, entertainment evaluations, and program awareness in the DDR. Includes audience assessments of DER STAATSANWALT HAT DAS WORT: HOFFNUNG FÜR ANNA, focusing on realism, entertainment value, and perceived crime-prevention effects. Also investigates the reception of television drama, awareness of youth-oriented programming, and viewing of recurring television series. Provides comparative material for studying audience responses to crime-related fictional television and other program genres.

returned_title: Sofortresonanzen DDR Fernsehen 23. Woche 1987 (SFR 23/87)
justification: Relevant to audience evaluations of entertainment programs, films, presenters, and television content. Includes assessments of the entertainment show WENNSCHON – DENNSCHON, particularly its presenter, featured records, and informational value. Also examines viewers' reactions to films, characters, realism, and program themes. The survey records weekly viewing participation and program evaluations and uses representative household sampling. Useful for comparative analysis of entertainment preferences during the late 1980s.

returned_title: Sofortresonanzen DDR Fernsehen 5. Woche 1985 (SFR 5/85)
justification: Useful for investigating television viewing as a household and family activity. Includes questions about reasons for watching AUF SCHUSTERS RAPPEN, evaluations of its presenter, conversations with family members during television programs and films, and assessments of entertainment value and interesting program elements. Also records weekly viewing participation and program evaluations. Offers supplementary evidence for studying social viewing practices, audience engagement, and demographic differences.

returned_title: IAB/ZEW Start-up Panel (Germany, 2008–present)
justification: Excellent match and the strongest overall dataset for the research question. This nationally representative longitudinal survey of German start-ups began in 2008 and includes businesses founded during the 2000s. It collects detailed information about founders' backgrounds, previous entrepreneurial experience, education, employment, business formation, financing, profitability, revenues, employment growth, innovation, and firm survival. Firms are followed across multiple years, enabling analysis of business success during the first five years after establishment. Particularly relevant psychological variables include the Big Five personality traits, risk attitudes, and entrepreneurial orientation, although these were introduced in later survey waves rather than collected throughout the 2000s. The dataset supports investigating relationships between founder characteristics and business performance. Access is available to researchers through the ZEW Research Data Centre.

returned_title: IAB/ZEW Start-up Panel – Scientific Use Files and Researcher Access
justification: Official access page for the IAB/ZEW Start-up Panel, particularly useful for obtaining individual-level data rather than published aggregate statistics. The Scientific Use Files cover longitudinal information about German start-ups, including founder demographics, educational qualifications, entrepreneurial backgrounds, employment, organizational characteristics, revenues, expenditures, and indicators of business success. The documentation also identifies variables measuring entrepreneurial orientation and the Big Five personality dimensions. Researchers can investigate whether psychological characteristics predict profitability, survival, and employment growth over the first five business years. The 2008–2022 Scientific Use Files span the relevant historical period, although psychological measurements are concentrated in later waves. Access options include scientific-use files, secure remote access, and on-site research.

returned_title: German Socio-Economic Panel (SOEP-Core), 1984–2022
justification: Highly relevant longitudinal household survey covering Germany throughout the 2000s. It contains detailed employment histories, transitions between paid employment and self-employment, occupational status, earnings, education, household characteristics, age, gender, and other demographics. The survey introduced a short Big Five personality inventory in 2005, with subsequent measurements in 2009 and later years. These features allow researchers to identify young individuals transitioning into entrepreneurship, examine their prior employment experiences, and study relationships between personality and subsequent economic outcomes. Additional psychological measures include attitudes toward risk, locus of control, and subjective well-being. Particularly suitable for investigating how founder personality and employment history relate to entrepreneurial persistence and income trajectories over five years. A limitation is that detailed firm-level financial performance is less comprehensive than in dedicated business panels.

returned_title: KfW Entrepreneurship Monitor (KfW-Gründungsmonitor), 2000–present
justification: Strong historical match because this representative German entrepreneurship survey has operated annually since 2000. It provides information about newly established businesses, founder demographics, educational backgrounds, employment status, previous entrepreneurial activities, start-up motivations, business characteristics, and entrepreneurial activity. The survey distinguishes full-time and part-time entrepreneurship and includes information about business survival, particularly during the first three years. It is useful for identifying younger entrepreneurs and investigating relationships between prior employment, motivation, demographics, and entrepreneurial outcomes during the 2000s. Its principal limitation is that it does not systematically provide the complete Big Five, self-efficacy, and procrastination measures requested. It is therefore best suited for historical entrepreneurship analysis and as a complementary source for psychological research.

returned_title: Global Entrepreneurship Monitor (GEM): Adult Population Survey, 1998–2017
justification: Very relevant international entrepreneurship dataset containing observations from Germany throughout much of the 2000s. The Adult Population Survey investigates entrepreneurial participation, business creation, founder age, gender, education, employment circumstances, entrepreneurial motivation, perceived opportunities, fear of failure, and perceived entrepreneurial capabilities. Researchers can isolate German respondents and young entrepreneurs to investigate how motivation, entrepreneurial self-perception, and demographic characteristics relate to business creation and early entrepreneurial activity. The dataset provides a particularly useful measure of perceived entrepreneurial capabilities as an approximation of entrepreneurial self-efficacy. Limitations include the absence of comprehensive Big Five and procrastination measures and the lack of detailed longitudinal firm performance over five years.

returned_title: Global Entrepreneurship Monitor (GEM) – Official Entrepreneurship Survey Datasets
justification: Official repository of Global Entrepreneurship Monitor survey data, including historical Adult Population Survey datasets from the 2000s. The surveys include individual-level characteristics of entrepreneurs and prospective founders, entrepreneurial motivations, perceived capabilities, fear of failure, business development stages, and demographic characteristics. German observations can be used to examine entrepreneurship among younger age groups and compare entrepreneurial motivations across years. The repository is especially useful for obtaining historical survey waves and investigating psychological perceptions associated with entrepreneurial decisions. However, these surveys do not provide comprehensive standardized Big Five assessments, procrastination measures, or continuous five-year tracking of individual firms.

returned_title: IAB/ZEW Start-up Panel Linked with Administrative Employment Histories
justification: Especially relevant for the requirement to connect entrepreneurial success with previous employment history. This research initiative links the IAB/ZEW Start-up Panel with administrative employment information from the German Federal Employment Agency. The combined data enable analysis of founders' previous employment and unemployment experiences alongside detailed characteristics and subsequent performance of their new businesses. The underlying start-up panel includes businesses founded during the 2000s and followed across subsequent years. Potential outcomes include firm survival, employment creation, and business development. The underlying panel also contains founder personality measures in later waves, making it potentially valuable for studying psychological predictors of business success. Researchers should verify which personality variables are available in the linked research version and whether access can be authorized.

returned_title: BIBB/BAuA Employment Survey 2018 – Personality Traits and Employment
justification: Exceptionally close match for the requested psychological variables, although the survey was conducted in 2018 rather than the 2000s. This German supplementary employment survey contains information from 8,010 employed respondents and explicitly measures the Big Five personality traits, self-efficacy, locus of control, procrastination, risk-taking, and work-related psychological characteristics. Linked information from the main employment survey provides occupational characteristics and demographic variables. It is particularly useful for investigating relationships between psychological self-characterization, employment, and professional success. Researchers can select younger respondents or self-employed individuals where identifiable. Its main limitations are the later collection period and the absence of detailed longitudinal start-up performance over the first five years. It is a strong complementary psychological dataset rather than a complete solution to the historical entrepreneurship research question.

returned_title: IAB Establishment Panel (Germany, 1993–2019)
justification: Relevant supplementary longitudinal business dataset covering the entire 2000s. The IAB Establishment Panel is an annual representative survey of German establishments that collects information about employment, workforce composition, organizational structures, management practices, investment, business conditions, and economic performance. Researchers can examine younger establishments to investigate organizational development and employment dynamics over their initial operating years, subject to sample availability. The data provide useful measures of firm-level success and industrial management characteristics. However, founder-specific psychological attributes, Big Five personality measures, self-efficacy, and procrastination are not core survey variables. This dataset is best suited for studying organizational and employment-related determinants of business performance.

returned_title: ZEW Research Data Centre – High-Tech Start-up Panel in Germany, 2006 and 2007
justification: Relevant historical dataset covering German technology-oriented start-ups during the requested decade. The ZEW Research Data Centre lists the High-Tech Start-up Panel for 2006 and 2007 among its research data products. It may provide a useful complementary source for studying business formation, innovation, entrepreneurial characteristics, and organizational development among younger high-technology firms. Its principal advantage is the direct connection to German start-up activity during the 2000s. However, the available landing-page description does not establish whether detailed employment histories, five-year financial outcomes, Big Five traits, motivation, self-efficacy, or procrastination were collected. Researchers should consult the dataset documentation before treating it as a direct match.

returned_title: BIBB/BAuA Employment Survey 2018 (BIBB/BAuA-Erwerbstätigenbefragung 2018) – Scientific Use File
justification: BEST MATCH. This nationally representative survey of 20,012 employed persons in Germany was conducted between October 2017 and April 2018. It provides detailed information on digitalization, working conditions, telecommuting, working hours, and occupational characteristics. Crucially, it includes variables on the frequency of working from home, contractual home-office agreements, weekly hours worked remotely, and whether hours worked at home are recognized as working time. It is the underlying dataset for the study 'Homeoffice und suchthaftes Arbeiten in Deutschland' by Christian Ebner, Beatrice van Berk, and Daniela Rohrbach-Schmidt (2023), which examines the relationship between working from home and workaholism using approximately 6,000 German employees. This makes it the strongest available match for the requested research.

returned_title: BIBB/BAuA Employment Survey 2018 – Official Dataset Metadata and Variable Documentation
justification: Official dataset landing page maintained by the German Federal Institute for Vocational Education and Training (BIBB). Provides metadata, documentation, and information about accessing the 2017–2018 employment survey. Particularly useful for identifying variables measuring home-office frequency, formal telework agreements, recognition of home-office hours as working time, occupational demands, and working conditions. The dataset supports investigations of workaholism, digitalization, and employment outcomes among German workers.

returned_title: BIBB/BAuA Employment Survey 2018 – Special Variables Dataset (Sondervariablen)
justification: Supplementary dataset associated with the 2017–2018 BIBB/BAuA Employment Survey. Contains additional variables that may support more detailed analyses beyond the standard Scientific Use File. Relevant for researchers investigating workplace characteristics, digitalization, telecommuting arrangements, and workaholism. Access to special variables may require an application through the BIBB Research Data Centre. Researchers should verify which additional measures are included before requesting access.

returned_title: BIBB/BAuA Employment Survey 2018 – Campus File
justification: An anonymized educational version of the 2018 BIBB/BAuA Employment Survey, based on approximately two-thirds of the original sample. Provides an accessible alternative for learning survey analysis methods and exploring employment conditions in Germany during 2017–2018. Potentially useful for preliminary investigations of home-office arrangements and working conditions. However, additional anonymization means that the availability of specific telework and workaholism variables must be verified. The full Scientific Use File is preferable for the proposed research.

returned_title: BAuA Working Time Survey 2017 – Scientific Use File, Version 2
justification: A highly relevant complementary dataset collected in Germany in 2017 by the Federal Institute for Occupational Safety and Health (BAuA). Covers working-time arrangements, telework, working from home, flexibility, job demands, work-life balance, and physical and mental health. The survey explicitly distinguishes employees with formal telework agreements from those performing work tasks at home without such agreements. Published analyses show that 12% of German employees had a formal telework agreement in 2017, while approximately 31% worked from home at least occasionally without an agreement. Particularly useful for examining how remote-work arrangements relate to working hours, psychological strain, and indicators associated with workaholism. It does not necessarily contain the same workaholism measures as the BIBB/BAuA Employment Survey.

returned_title: Harmonized BIBB/BAuA Employment Survey 2006, 2012, and 2018 (H-ETB)
justification: A harmonized longitudinal-comparison dataset combining three waves of Germany's BIBB/BAuA Employment Surveys, including the crucial 2018 wave collected during 2017–2018. Useful for examining how digitalization, employment conditions, occupational demands, and working arrangements changed throughout the 2010s. Provides a broader historical perspective for studying the relationship between technological change, remote working, and employee well-being. Because harmonization retains variables suitable for comparisons across survey waves, researchers should verify whether the detailed telework-agreement, working-time-recognition, and workaholism measures from 2018 remain available. The original 2018 dataset is the better choice for reproducing the specific workaholism study.

returned_title: Social Structure of German Sport Youth (Sozialstruktur der deutschen Sportjugend), 1958 — GESIS ZA0234
justification: Highly relevant historical dataset examining leisure activities, social relationships, personal development, and family influences among young people in West Germany. Surveyed 1,879 sports club members aged 15–25 in 1958, providing a close pre-1960s comparison. Variables include club membership duration, leisure and sporting activities, parental influence on leisure organization, upbringing, socialization, educational and occupational circumstances, cultural interests, relationships with older generations, religious attitudes, and social integration. Particularly useful for investigating how organized youth activities shaped adolescents' friendships, identities, social attitudes, and development. Does not specifically evaluate youth leisure clubhouses or include a separate parent survey.

returned_title: Youth Leisure Activities in the GDR, 1969 (Freizeitverhalten Jugendlicher) — GESIS ZA6036
justification: Relevant late-1960s East German research dataset examining young people's leisure activities and interests. Associated research documentation includes studies of leisure behavior according to parents' occupational groups, parental socioeconomic influences, cultural participation, and the relationship between education and leisure. Particularly useful for exploring how family background and social circumstances influenced adolescents' recreational choices during the 1960s. Provides historical context for youth leisure participation in East Germany, although direct measures of clubhouse effects and parent-youth comparisons require verification in the documentation.

returned_title: Leisure in the Ruhr Area, 1970 (Freizeit im Ruhrgebiet 1970) — GESIS ZA0649
justification: Closely related to the research topic because it explicitly measures leisure activities taking place in clubhouses, residential neighborhoods, and private homes. Conducted in May–June 1970 in West Germany's Ruhr region, immediately after the target decade. Variables include preferred leisure pursuits, frequency of activities in clubhouses, opportunities for recreation near home, obstacles to leisure participation, organized sporting activities, sports club membership, and preferences for leisure facilities. Useful for investigating the relationship between recreational infrastructure, housing environments, and participation in organized leisure. The survey covers the broader population rather than exclusively adolescents.

returned_title: Youth Welfare Survey, Offenbach District, 1980 (Jugendhilfe-Untersuchung, Kreis Offenbach) — GESIS ZA1258
justification: Exceptionally close thematic match, although conducted in 1980 rather than the 1960s. Surveyed approximately 3,080 young people aged 12–22 in the Offenbach district of West Germany. Covers leisure activities, friendship networks, frequency and location of recreational activities, club membership and participation, boredom, housing conditions, access to personal rooms, neighborhood environments, family relationships, parenting experiences, household composition, and shared family activities. Particularly valuable for examining relationships between youth leisure participation, friendships, family life, housing, and personal development. Could provide a comparative framework for analyzing earlier youth clubhouse programs, but cannot directly establish their effects during the 1960s.

returned_title: Sofortresonanzen DDR Fernsehen 6. Woche 1983 (SFR 6/83)
justification: Highly relevant survey dataset collected on February 9, 1983, by the GDR State Committee for Television, Department of Sociological Research. Measures television audience participation, viewing behavior, and evaluations of programs watched during the preceding week. Includes assessments of entertainment value, informational content, presenters, target age groups, and audience preferences. Particularly useful for studying perceptions of informational and entertainment programming and evaluations of television personalities. Part of GESIS's historical GDR television audience research collection.

returned_title: Sofortresonanzen DDR Fernsehen 50. Woche 1982 (SFR 50/82)
justification: Survey conducted on December 16, 1982, examining audience participation and evaluations of recently broadcast television programs. Includes perceived entertainment value, humor, program quality, desired improvements, and informational value of particular broadcasts. Especially relevant for analyzing audience responses to entertainment and informational programming. Provides historical survey evidence of television consumption patterns in the GDR during the early 1980s.

returned_title: Sofortresonanzen DDR Fernsehen 46. Woche 1984 (SFR 46/84)
justification: Highly relevant dataset collected on November 16, 1984, addressing television viewing behavior and evaluations of programs broadcast during the previous week. Additional questions examine reception and evaluation of the informational program 'Umschau,' interest in program topics, knowledge of television schedules, preferences for youth programming, and the influence of shift work and parents on viewing behavior. Includes demographic variables such as household size, age, gender, education, occupation, continuing education, and political party membership. Particularly valuable for examining informational programming, audience interests, viewing patterns, and demographic differences.

returned_title: Sofortresonanzen DDR Fernsehen 36. Woche 1985 (SFR 36/85)
justification: GDR television audience survey conducted on August 31, 1985. Records exposure to and evaluations of television programs broadcast during the preceding week. Includes assessments of presenters, entertainment value, perceived realism of televised drama, audience expectations, and television program preferences. Useful for investigating presenter ratings, program reception, audience satisfaction, and entertainment preferences during the mid-1980s.

returned_title: Sofortresonanzen DDR Fernsehen 23. Woche 1987 (SFR 23/87)
justification: Survey from 1987 examining television audience participation and evaluations of recently broadcast programs. Includes informational value, perceived realism, presenter assessments, audience opinions, and interest in problems discussed in particular broadcasts. Relevant for studying how East German viewers evaluated informational content, program credibility, presenters, and socially relevant subjects. Provides evidence of television reception and audience interests in the late 1980s.

returned_title: Sofortresonanzen DDR Fernsehen 35. Woche 1988 (SFR 35/88)
justification: Audience research dataset from 1988 measuring television viewing and evaluations of programs broadcast during the previous week. Includes assessments of entertainment value, realism, presenters, humor, program components, and the practical usefulness of informational television content. Also examines viewing frequency and audience preferences for youth programming. Relevant for analyzing entertainment and informational value, presenter ratings, and audience segmentation.

returned_title: Sofortresonanzen DDR Fernsehen 28. Woche 1989 (SFR 28/89)
justification: GDR television audience survey conducted in 1989. Covers participation in and evaluations of recently broadcast programs, including assessments of performers, presenters, musical variety, and overall satisfaction with East German television. Also examines audience responses to specific cultural and political programming. Particularly relevant for research on music-related entertainment, presenter evaluations, audience satisfaction, and changing television preferences toward the end of the 1980s.

returned_title: Sofortresonanzen DDR Fernsehen 39. Woche 1982 (SFR 39/82)
justification: Representative household survey from 1982 investigating television viewing behavior and evaluations of programs broadcast during the preceding week. Includes detailed assessments of entertainment programming, an international popular-music festival broadcast, presenters, program design, and audience responses to portrayals of young people's experiences. Particularly relevant for examining popular-music programming, entertainment preferences, presenter ratings, and youth-oriented television content in the GDR.

returned_title: Sofortresonanzen DDR Fernsehen 14. Woche 1982 (SFR 14/82)
justification: Survey dataset from 1982 covering audience participation and evaluations of television programs watched during the preceding week. Includes perceived entertainment value, realism, awareness of specific programs, and audience responses to television drama and youth-oriented programming. Useful for investigating television exposure, program awareness, perceived entertainment value, and reception of different television genres in the early 1980s.

returned_title: Sofortresonanzen DDR Fernsehen 13. Woche 1985 (SFR 13/85)
justification: Survey from 1985 addressing television viewing behavior, recent program exposure, and audience evaluations. Includes entertainment value, realism, audience expectations, interest in cultural programming, preferred program topics, and viewing frequency. Also investigates occupational characteristics, physical and mental workload, and fatigue after work, allowing connections between respondents' social circumstances and television preferences. Particularly relevant for examining entertainment needs, program interests, and socioeconomic influences on television consumption.

returned_title: Landtagswahl im Saarland 2012 (ZA5642) – GESIS
justification: Highly relevant survey dataset from Forschungsgruppe Wahlen, archived by GESIS, covering the 2012 Saarland state election. A strong match for research on voting intentions, party preferences, candidate evaluations, coalition preferences, political attitudes, and voter demographics. Particularly relevant for examining political conditions following the collapse of Saarland's Jamaica coalition. The questionnaire and variable documentation should be consulted to verify coverage of minimum wage, debt brake, economic perceptions, and political scandals.

returned_title: Landtagswahl im Saarland 2017 (ZA6948) – GESIS
justification: Highly relevant election survey conducted in connection with the March 26, 2017 Saarland state election. Listed in the GESIS state election studies collection under study number ZA6948. Suitable for investigating voting intentions, party and candidate evaluations, coalition preferences, political issues, and demographic differences in electoral behavior. Especially useful for studying evaluations of Annegret Kramp-Karrenbauer and Anke Rehlinger, CDU-SPD competition, and government performance. Exact questionnaire coverage should be verified in the GESIS documentation.

returned_title: Forschungsgruppe Wahlen – Saarland 2017 Election Survey Results
justification: Official survey-based election analysis from Forschungsgruppe Wahlen for the 2017 Saarland election. Provides results on preferred minister-president, evaluations of Kramp-Karrenbauer and Rehlinger, coalition models, perceived party competence in solving political problems, structural economic change, and voting patterns by age. Particularly useful for candidate evaluations, coalition preferences, economic issue attitudes, and demographic comparisons. The landing page provides aggregated survey graphics rather than individual-level microdata.

returned_title: GESIS – German State Election Studies (Landtagswahlstudien), 1962–Present
justification: Official GESIS research data collection containing representative surveys on German state elections, including Saarland election studies ZA5642 (2012) and ZA6948 (2017). Provides access to study descriptions, questionnaires, variable documentation, and available research datasets. The most useful starting point for identifying individual survey questions about voting intentions, party evaluations, candidate preferences, economic perceptions, coalition formation, and demographic characteristics. Particularly valuable for comparing Saarland electoral attitudes across the 2010s.

returned_title: German Longitudinal Election Study (GLES) – Surveys and Long-Term Tracking, 2009–2017
justification: Major longitudinal election research program covering German political attitudes and electoral behavior throughout the 2010s. Includes survey measures of voting intentions, party identification, candidate evaluations, political issues, ideological preferences, and respondent demographics. Potentially useful for analyzing Saarland respondents within national surveys and comparing state-level political attitudes with broader German trends. National samples may contain relatively few Saarland respondents, so state-specific representativeness and sample sizes must be checked.

returned_title: WahlREPORT Saarland 2012 and 2017 – Infratest dimap
justification: Survey-based election analysis products covering both Saarland state elections during the 2010s. Examine voter behavior, party performance, demographic differences, electoral shifts, and political attitudes surrounding the elections. Useful supplementary sources for studying coalition preferences, candidate evaluations, economic concerns, and the political context of voting decisions. These are analytical reports based on survey research rather than openly downloadable individual-level datasets; access to underlying microdata is not established.

returned_title: Saarland State Election Opinion Polls – Wahlrecht.de
justification: Historical collection of Saarland state election voting-intention polls, including surveys conducted around the 2012 and 2017 elections. Provides party-level polling estimates, polling organizations, fieldwork dates, and sample sizes where available. Particularly useful for constructing time series of voting intentions and comparing polling trends across electoral cycles. Does not provide individual-level respondent demographics, candidate evaluations, or detailed issue-attitude variables.

returned_title: Saarländischer Landtag – Historical Voting Intention Polls (Wahlwerk)
justification: Structured historical polling database covering Saarland state parliament voting intentions, including numerous surveys from the 2010s. Contains party vote-share estimates from organizations such as Forschungsgruppe Wahlen, Infratest dimap, Forsa, and INSA, together with fieldwork dates and sample sizes. Useful for analyzing changes in party support, election forecasting, and political trends between the 2012 and 2017 Saarland elections. The database contains aggregated polling results rather than individual-level responses.

returned_title: GESIS Research Data Center Elections – Politbarometer and German State Election Surveys
justification: Official research infrastructure providing access to German election surveys, including state election studies and Politbarometer datasets collected by Forschungsgruppe Wahlen. Relevant for locating detailed survey microdata covering political attitudes, party and candidate evaluations, voting intentions, government performance, economic assessments, and respondent demographics. Particularly useful for identifying supplementary surveys conducted during the 2010s and checking whether specific questions about political scandals, minimum wages, or the debt brake were included.

returned_title: Opinions and Values of Egyptian Students in West Germany (1964) — GESIS ZA3331
justification: Excellent match and the most directly relevant dataset. Conducted in 1964 by the United States Information Agency (USIA), this survey specifically examines Egyptian students living and studying in West Germany. It is highly relevant to research on students' experiences in Germany, social integration, educational experiences, political opinions, international affairs, economic development, and personal values. The study corresponds directly to the requested population, geographical setting, and historical period. Its subject matter is closely aligned with the research interests in media consumption, attitudes toward Egypt and other countries, development, religion, foreign assistance, and future intentions. Archived by GESIS Data Archive under study number ZA3331, it is the primary dataset recommended for this research.

returned_title: Situation of Afro-Asian Students in the Federal Republic of Germany (1960) — GESIS ZA0195
justification: Very strong supplementary match. Conducted in February 1960 by Prodosh Aich and the Research Institute for Sociology at the University of Cologne, this survey explicitly includes Egyptian students studying in West Germany. The target population consisted of male students from Egypt, India, Indonesia, Iran, and Jordan who had completed at least two semesters of study by the winter semester of 1959–1960. Additional students from Ghana, Nigeria, and Norway formed comparison groups. Interviews took place in Berlin, Hamburg, Munich, Heidelberg, and Tübingen. Particularly valuable for investigating the experiences of Egyptian students within German universities, their social circumstances, and their integration into German society. Its multinational design also permits comparisons between Egyptian students and students from other countries. The dataset provides historically relevant evidence from the beginning of the 1960s, although its coverage of specific political and media-related questions should be verified in the questionnaire.

returned_title: Food for Justice: Power, Politics, and Food Inequalities in a Bioeconomy – Protest Surveys, Berlin, 2020 and 2024
justification: Best match for the research need. This dataset, published through GESIS by the Food for Justice research project, investigates food justice movements and agrifood protests in Germany, particularly the annual 'Wir haben es satt!' demonstrations in Berlin in 2020 and 2024. It covers participants' sociodemographic characteristics, protest motivations, political attitudes and practices, demands for agricultural and food-system justice, and food-related behaviors. Topics include household food consumption, food production and self-cultivation, and food waste management. The research combines in-person interviews and online surveys, supporting comparisons between the 2020 and 2024 protest participants. The dataset's embargo ended on July 1, 2026, making it especially relevant for current research.

returned_title: Befragung 'Wir haben es satt!' 2020 – Berlin Protest Survey
justification: Directly relevant survey dataset covering participants in the 'Wir haben es satt!' demonstration held in Berlin on January 18, 2020. Conducted by researchers from Freie Universität Berlin in cooperation with the Institute for Protest and Social Movement Research, the survey examines participants' demographic backgrounds, political orientations, mobilization pathways, protest motivations, organizational involvement, and attitudes toward sustainable agriculture and fair food production. It also investigates ethical consumption and food-related lifestyle practices. Provides a valuable 2020 baseline for comparison with the 2024 protest survey and for investigating changes in Germany's food justice movement.

returned_title: Food for Justice: Power, Politics, and Food Inequalities in a Bioeconomy (Berlin, 2020) – B2FIND Dataset Record
justification: Research dataset discovery record documenting the Food for Justice investigation of Germany's agrifood movements, specifically the 'Wir haben es satt!' protest in Berlin. The project conducted protest surveys in 2020 and 2024 to investigate activists' characteristics, political engagement, food-system demands, and agricultural and nutritional practices. Particularly useful as an additional metadata discovery route for locating the relevant research data and understanding its geographical and temporal coverage. This is a discovery record rather than an independent survey dataset.

returned_title: Food for Justice – GESIS Research Data Record for Protest Surveys 2020 and 2024
justification: Official GESIS dataset landing page linked by the Food for Justice research team. The dataset addresses social movements mobilizing against food inequalities, with particular emphasis on the Berlin 'Wir haben es satt!' protests in 2020 and 2024. It includes information on protesters' motivations, justice demands, sociodemographics, political activities, and food-related practices, including food preparation, household consumption, self-production, and waste management. This is the most relevant institutional access point for obtaining data and documentation supporting comparative analysis of the two protest years. It refers to the same dataset as the first entry.

returned_title: Farmers' Voices in European Protests: Diverse Complaints, Emotional Tones, and Policy Responses
justification: Complementary dataset covering the 2024 farmers' protests in Germany, France, Belgium, and the Netherlands. It contains coded information derived from 2,232 open-ended survey responses concerning farmers' motivations for protesting, agricultural policy grievances, emotional expressions, and policy responses at national and European levels. Relevant for contextualizing the German agricultural policy conflicts of 2024 and comparing farmers' demands with those of food justice activists participating in Berlin's 'Wir haben es satt!' demonstration. However, it does not specifically survey the Berlin food justice movement, does not provide a 2020 comparison, and does not include the original open-ended responses.

returned_title: Typologie der Wünsche (TdW) 1980 – Consumer Typology and Lifestyle Survey
justification: Excellent match. The Typologie der Wünsche series, conducted by Hubert Burda, is a comprehensive German consumer and market research survey examining purchasing behavior, product preferences, lifestyle, media consumption, and demographic characteristics. The series includes detailed information about consumer goods, brand preferences, household products, leisure activities, and purchasing habits. The 1980 dataset (GESIS ZA1087) provides an early baseline for studying consumer behavior in West Germany. Particularly relevant because the research program covers many of the requested consumer domains.

returned_title: Typologie der Wünsche (TdW) 1984 – Consumer Behavior, Brands, and Media Usage
justification: Very strong match for the requested large-scale consumer behavior survey. This 1984 wave belongs to the German Typologie der Wünsche market-media research series. The series investigates consumption patterns, brand recognition and preferences, purchasing decisions, media habits, lifestyle characteristics, and socioeconomic demographics. From 1984 onward, the survey series incorporated visual presentations of brands and products using packaging images and logos. Particularly suitable for historical research on brand preferences and consumption patterns in 1980s West Germany. The precise variables available in this wave should be checked against its questionnaire and codebook.

returned_title: Typologie der Wünsche (TdW) 1986 – German Consumer and Lifestyle Survey
justification: Highly relevant historical consumer research dataset from 1986, archived by GESIS under study ZA1571. Part of a comprehensive market-media survey series designed to investigate consumer preferences, purchasing behavior, product ownership, media usage, and lifestyle segmentation. The broader research program covers consumer categories including food, health, travel, household goods, automobiles, personal care, and consumer electronics. Demographic characteristics support comparisons across population groups. A strong candidate for investigating brand preferences and consumer segmentation during the mid-1980s, although individual category coverage requires verification.

returned_title: Typologie der Wünsche (TdW) 1987 – Consumer Preferences and Market Research
justification: Strong match for analyzing consumer behavior in late-1980s West Germany. This archived wave of the Typologie der Wünsche survey series provides a potential source for detailed market segmentation, product preferences, consumer lifestyles, media consumption, and demographic characteristics. The series is particularly relevant for research requiring consumer attitudes and preferences rather than expenditure statistics alone. Comparing this wave with earlier surveys may support analyses of changing consumption patterns, subject to differences in questionnaire content.

returned_title: Typologie der Wünsche (TdW) 1989 – Consumer Behavior and Brand Preferences
justification: Excellent candidate for studying consumer markets immediately before German reunification. The 1989 wave belongs to the extensive Typologie der Wünsche consumer research series, which combines information about lifestyles, purchasing behavior, product and brand preferences, media use, and socioeconomic characteristics. The series' broad consumer-product coverage makes it especially promising for studying food, travel, automobiles, electronics, household products, health-related consumption, and personal grooming. The archived documentation should be consulted to confirm the exact variables and sample size.

returned_title: Media Analysis (MA 81) – West German Media Consumption and Purchasing Behavior
justification: Strong complementary dataset covering West Germany in 1980. The survey includes detailed information on newspaper and magazine readership, television viewing, radio listening, advertising exposure, cinema attendance, travel frequency and destinations, ownership of televisions and radios, food and beverage shopping habits, and preferred retail outlets. It also contains extensive demographic variables, including age, gender, occupation, education, income, household composition, and ownership of durable consumer goods. Particularly useful for connecting consumer characteristics with advertising exposure and media behavior. Access to the archived data requires authorization from the data depositor.

returned_title: Household Panel 1984 (Haushaltspanel 1984) – Consumer Electronics and Brand Ownership
justification: Highly relevant specialized household consumer survey conducted by MARPLAN in January–February 1984. Contains 7,346 observations from a multistage probability sample of German-speaking individuals aged 14 and older in West German private households. Records ownership, quantity, brands, acquisition years, purchase locations, prices, and product characteristics for televisions, video recorders, video cameras, cameras, radios, stereo systems, cassette recorders, portable audio equipment, car radios, and watches. Particularly valuable for detailed historical analysis of consumer electronics ownership, purchasing decisions, and brand choices. Its limitation is that it focuses primarily on electronics rather than the full range of consumer categories.

returned_title: Konsummuster im Wandel – Household Budgets and Private Consumption in West Germany, 1952–1998
justification: Relevant historical consumption dataset spanning the entire 1980s. Compiles information about household budgets and private consumption in West Germany between 1952 and 1998. Includes expenditure categories such as food, beverages, clothing, and other household consumption, with distinctions between household types and income groups. Useful for identifying long-term trends in expenditure patterns and comparing the economic circumstances of different household categories. However, it is primarily a historical household-budget dataset rather than a detailed individual-level brand-preference or media-use survey.

returned_title: German General Social Survey (ALLBUS) – Cumulation 1980–2023
justification: Large representative German social survey series beginning in 1980, with repeated cross-sectional surveys covering demographic characteristics, household structure, employment, economic circumstances, social attitudes, and selected aspects of behavior and lifestyle. Particularly useful for contextualizing consumer behavior across gender, education, occupation, income, and household characteristics during the 1980s. The cumulative dataset facilitates comparisons across survey years. It is less suitable for detailed purchasing histories, individual brands, grocery products, grooming products, or household appliances, but provides valuable socioeconomic context.

returned_title: German Microcensus Trend File – Household and Demographic Surveys, 1962–2016
justification: Large-scale German household survey resource with historical data covering 1980, 1982, 1985, 1987, and 1989. Includes harmonized demographic, household, family, employment, and socioeconomic variables. Useful for characterizing the composition and economic circumstances of German households during the 1980s and providing population benchmarks for consumer research. Its principal limitation is the absence of the extensive product-specific purchasing and brand-preference information found in commercial market-media surveys.

returned_title: Reiseanalyse – German Holiday and Travel Behavior Survey Series
justification: Relevant supplementary survey series for the travel and tourism component of the research request. The Reiseanalyse program investigates holiday frequency, destinations, travel duration, transportation choices, trip organization, travel agents, information sources, and lifestyle-related travel preferences. Earlier waves covering the 1980s are archived by GESIS. The linked 1990 reference survey documents the series and identifies earlier archived studies. Particularly useful for analyzing holiday purchasing decisions and travel consumption, although it does not cover the complete range of household goods and brand preferences.

returned_title: Stadtentwicklung und Wohnmilieu von Halle und Halle-Neustadt 1984 (Urban Development and Residential Environment in Halle and Halle-Neustadt, 1984)
justification: Excellent match. This GESIS dataset contains a standardized survey of 360 adult residents in selected residential neighborhoods of Halle and Halle-Neustadt, German Democratic Republic, conducted in August 1984. It examines housing conditions, residential satisfaction, neighborhood relationships, attachment to residential areas, local shopping and service facilities, cultural and leisure amenities, and everyday mobility. Variables cover workplace location, commuting routes and burdens, transportation used for work and leisure, shopping destinations, recreational activities, satisfaction with housing, and reasons for dissatisfaction. Its combination of housing, neighborhood ties, local amenities, commuting, and residential belonging makes it one of the strongest matches for the research need.

returned_title: Jugend in Leipzig 1982 (Youth in Leipzig, 1982)
justification: Excellent match for research on younger urban residents. Conducted between March and April 1982 by the Central Institute for Youth Research in Leipzig, this survey investigates housing conditions, residential satisfaction, neighborhood environments, mobility, and attachment to Leipzig. Variables include length of residence, feelings about the residential location, intentions to remain or relocate, reasons for staying or leaving, preferred residential neighborhoods, location of housing relative to employment, commuting time, and accessibility of neighborhood facilities. It also examines housing in newly developed residential areas, apartment amenities, leisure activities, and social participation. The geographical coverage includes Leipzig and the surrounding districts of Leipzig-Land and Borna. Particularly valuable for investigating residential belonging and intentions to move.

returned_title: Stadtentwicklung und Wohnmilieu – Magdeburg 1986 (Urban Development and Residential Environment in Magdeburg, 1986)
justification: Highly relevant historical urban survey conducted in Magdeburg in 1986, during the German Democratic Republic period. The study belongs to the collection of sociological investigations of urban development and residential environments undertaken by the Hochschule für Architektur und Bauwesen Weimar. It uses standardized oral interviews to investigate residents' experiences of urban living environments. It is a promising source for comparative research on housing and neighborhood conditions in an East German city during the 1980s. The detailed questionnaire should be consulted to establish coverage of specific variables such as neighborhood relationships, commuting, residential satisfaction, and relocation intentions.

returned_title: Soziologische Untersuchung – Gotha/Innenstadt 1981 (Sociological Investigation of Gotha City Center, 1981)
justification: Excellent thematic match. This 1981 survey investigates housing conditions and everyday experiences of residents in the historic city center of Gotha, German Democratic Republic. Variables include satisfaction with apartments and residential neighborhoods, apartment size, household composition, length of residence, neighborhood relationships, feelings of belonging, and willingness to relocate during housing modernization. It also examines workplace locations, commuting burdens, transportation choices, shopping facilities, local services, cultural and recreational amenities, and leisure destinations. Additional questions address environmental disturbances, neighborhood improvement initiatives, and satisfaction with social contacts. Particularly useful for studying relationships between housing quality, neighborhood attachment, local infrastructure, and urban mobility.

returned_title: Freizeit und Wohnbedingungen Jugendlicher im Dorf 1987 (Leisure and Housing Conditions of Young People in Villages, 1987)
justification: Relevant supplementary dataset for comparing urban and rural residential experiences in the German Democratic Republic. Conducted in spring 1987 by the Central Institute for Youth Research, it surveys people aged 16–27 in selected villages in the districts of Neubrandenburg, Potsdam, and Gera. Topics include housing conditions, satisfaction with local services and amenities, commuting time, employment opportunities, leisure activities, neighborhood relationships, friendship networks, attachment to one's home community, and intentions to remain or migrate. Although the population is rural rather than urban, the close overlap in survey variables makes it valuable for comparative studies of residential satisfaction, community belonging, leisure opportunities, and mobility.

returned_title: Leben in der DDR 1990 (Life in the German Democratic Republic, January 1990)
justification: Relevant supplementary survey conducted in January 1990, before German reunification, covering adult residents of the DDR districts of Potsdam, Leipzig, and Schwerin. The dataset contains 1,528 observations and 350 variables examining living conditions and subjective evaluations of social and economic circumstances. Topics include housing conditions, satisfaction with everyday life, employment, social security, cultural and leisure opportunities, availability of services, and perceptions of the housing market. Although collected immediately after the 1980s and not specifically focused on urban neighborhoods, it provides valuable contextual evidence about residential living conditions and satisfaction at the end of the German Democratic Republic.

returned_title: International Social Survey Programme: Social Relations and Support Systems – ISSP 2001 (Social Networks II), ZA3680
justification: Excellent match for the research need. This cross-national social science survey dataset covers all 29 specified countries and territories, with data collected primarily between 2000 and 2002. It examines social relations, personal networks, family connections, friendship networks, social support, interpersonal trust, and participation in social groups. Variables include frequency of contact with parents, siblings, children, relatives, and friends; geographic proximity to family members; and availability of social support. The dataset is classified under Social behaviour and attitudes, SOCIAL STRATIFICATION AND GROUPINGS, and Family life and marriage. It is part of the International Social Survey Programme (ISSP), which conducts annual cross-national surveys using standardized questionnaires. Although this particular module was administered in 2001, related modules from 1986 and 2017 enable some longitudinal comparisons. This is the strongest match because its geographic coverage, subject classifications, survey methodology, and collection period correspond directly to the query.

returned_title: International Social Survey Programme: Social Networks – Cross-National Survey Series (1986, 2001, 2017)
justification: Highly relevant survey series for cross-national and cross-time research on social relations and social networks. The series includes Social Networks and Support Systems (1986), Social Relations and Support Systems (2001), and Social Networks and Social Resources (2017). It investigates relationships with family members and friends, participation in associations, interpersonal contacts, social obligations, social trust, and access to support resources. The 2001 wave includes all 29 requested countries and territories, making it particularly suitable for comparisons during the 2000s. The 1986 and 2017 waves offer additional historical and subsequent observations. Although the ISSP conducts surveys annually, its Social Networks module is not administered every year, and the three waves are not exact replications. Researchers should therefore assess questionnaire and variable comparability before conducting longitudinal analyses.

returned_title: International Social Survey Programme: Social Networks and Social Resources – ISSP 2017, ZA6980
justification: Strong supplementary dataset for extending analysis of social relations and social networks beyond the 2000s. The survey covers numerous countries included in the query, including Australia, Austria, the Czech Republic, Denmark, Finland, France, Germany, Great Britain, Hungary, Israel, Japan, New Zealand, the Philippines, the Russian Federation, Slovenia, South Africa, Spain, Switzerland, and the United States. It measures personal networks, social contacts, access to social resources, social support, and characteristics of respondents' relationships. Its standardized cross-national design facilitates comparisons with the ISSP 2001 Social Relations and Support Systems dataset where questions are sufficiently comparable. Data were collected primarily between 2017 and 2019, so this dataset does not independently satisfy the requested 2000s period. Its principal value is supporting cross-time comparisons with the 2001 survey.

returned_title: International Social Survey Programme (ISSP): Annual Cross-National Social Science Survey Data Collection
justification: Relevant overarching data collection for researchers requiring repeated annual cross-national surveys of social attitudes, social stratification, family relationships, and social networks. The ISSP provides standardized survey datasets across participating countries, with a different thematic module typically administered each year. Relevant 2000s modules include Social Relations and Support Systems (2001), Family and Changing Gender Roles (2002), Citizenship (2004), and Social Inequality (2009). These datasets enable comparisons of social relationships, family structures, social participation, socioeconomic characteristics, and attitudes across countries and survey years. Geographic coverage varies by module, but the 2001 Social Networks module includes all 29 requested countries and territories. The collection is particularly useful for investigating social changes over time, although individual topics are not measured annually and longitudinal analysis requires harmonization of comparable variables.

returned_title: International Social Survey Programme: Social Relations and Support Systems – ISSP 2001, GESIS Data Catalogue Record
justification: Official GESIS dataset landing page for the most directly relevant survey. This record identifies the dataset under the exact requested subject classifications: Social behaviour and attitudes, SOCIAL STRATIFICATION AND GROUPINGS, and Family life and marriage. Its geographic coverage includes Australia, Austria, Brazil, Canada, Chile, Cyprus, the Czech Republic, Denmark, Finland, France, Germany, Great Britain, Hungary, Israel, Italy, Japan, Latvia, New Zealand, Northern Ireland, Norway, the Philippines, Poland, the Russian Federation, Slovenia, Spain, South Africa, Switzerland, and the United States. The dataset contains internationally harmonized information on family ties, social contacts, social support systems, and interpersonal networks, collected between 2000 and 2002. The catalogue provides study documentation, methodological details, geographic coverage, and access to the archived survey data. It is an alternative access point for the same ZA3680 dataset identified in the first result, rather than a separate survey.

returned_title: Flash Eurobarometer 313: User Language Preferences Online (2011) – GESIS Data Archive
justification: Exact match for the research need. This European Commission survey, conducted from January 28 to February 1, 2011, collected data from 13,752 internet users aged 15 and older across all 27 requested European countries. It directly measures users' online language preferences, including languages used to read or watch internet content, languages used to write emails, comments and messages, and the frequency of using languages other than one's native language. It also investigates preferences for websites in users' own languages, willingness to use English-language websites, and attitudes toward multilingual website availability. The dataset contains 107 variables and supports individual-level and cross-country analysis. It is particularly suitable for studying online content language preferences, digital communication languages, and multilingual internet behavior during the 2010s.

returned_title: Flash Eurobarometer 313: User Language Preferences Online – European Union Open Data Portal
justification: Official European Union dataset catalogue entry for the 2011 User Language Preferences Online survey. It covers Belgium, Germany, Spain, Greece, France, Ireland, Italy, Luxembourg, Netherlands, Austria, Portugal, Finland, Slovenia, Cyprus, Malta, Slovakia, Bulgaria, Czech Republic, Denmark, Estonia, Latvia, Hungary, Poland, Romania, Sweden, United Kingdom, and Lithuania. The survey examines preferred languages for browsing websites, consuming online information, and communicating digitally. It also documents whether users prefer websites in their native language and whether language barriers prevent them from accessing information. This is an alternative official access point for the same underlying dataset archived by GESIS, rather than an independent survey.

returned_title: Flash Eurobarometer 313: User Language Preferences Online – B2FIND Research Data Catalogue
justification: Research data catalogue record providing detailed metadata and access information for the 2011 Eurobarometer survey on online language preferences. The dataset includes respondents' mother tongues, languages used to consume internet content, languages used for online writing and communication, and language choices across activities such as entertainment, news consumption, online banking, shopping, employment searches, and professional communication. It also measures preferences for native-language websites and attitudes toward English-language alternatives. Geographic coverage includes all 27 requested countries. This record provides another discovery and access route to the same underlying GESIS dataset.

returned_title: Flash Eurobarometer 313: User Language Preferences Online – GESIS Research Data Catalogue
justification: Primary research data landing page for study ZA5473, published by the GESIS Data Archive in 2011. It provides the dataset's methodology, bibliographic information, geographic coverage, sampling details, and access information. The survey contains approximately 500 interviews per country and examines internet users' language choices when reading, watching, writing, and communicating online. It also measures preferences for websites in respondents' own languages and acceptance of websites in other languages. The dataset is classified under Media and Language and linguistics, making it an especially precise thematic match. This is the primary catalogue record for the same dataset identified by DOI 10.4232/1.10730.

returned_title: Political Attitudes, Political Participation and Voting Behavior in Reunified Germany 1994 (ZA3065)
justification: Excellent match. This GESIS dataset contains pre-election and post-election surveys conducted in East and West Germany around the 1994 federal election. It covers voting intentions, electoral participation, previous voting behavior, political interest, satisfaction with democracy, economic evaluations, and political attitudes. Its separate East and West German samples make it particularly valuable for examining political differences following reunification.

returned_title: Political Attitudes, Political Participation and Voting Behavior in Reunified Germany 1998 (ZA3066)
justification: Excellent match. This survey examines political attitudes, electoral participation, and voting behavior surrounding Germany's 1998 federal election. It belongs to the same research series as the 1994 study, enabling comparisons across elections and between East and West Germany. Particularly relevant for investigating party preferences, democratic satisfaction, political engagement, and electoral change during the 1990s.

returned_title: German General Social Survey (ALLBUS) – Cumulation 1980–2014 (ZA4584)
justification: Excellent match for longitudinal research on political and social attitudes. The cumulative dataset includes German surveys conducted in 1990, 1991, 1992, 1994, 1996, and 1998. It contains measures of political participation, satisfaction with democracy, evaluations of government performance, political orientations, socioeconomic conditions, and social values. From 1991 onward, its coverage of both East and West Germany makes it especially useful for studying political integration and changing attitudes after reunification.

returned_title: Politbarometer 1977–2024 (Partial Cumulation, ZA2391)
justification: Highly relevant longitudinal survey series covering every year of the 1990s. Politbarometer provides repeated observations of German public opinion, including party preferences, voting intentions, evaluations of political parties and politicians, and attitudes toward current political developments. It is especially valuable for tracking shorter-term fluctuations in political attitudes and electoral preferences. The cumulative dataset supports comparisons over time, although the availability of individual variables and regional distinctions should be checked.

returned_title: German National Election Study – Post-Election Study 1998 / German CSES Study (ZA3073)
justification: Strong match for electoral behavior and democratic attitudes in Germany during the 1998 federal election. This German election study contributes to the Comparative Study of Electoral Systems and supports research on voting decisions, political parties, electoral participation, and evaluations of democratic institutions. It is particularly useful for investigating the relationship between citizens' political orientations and electoral choices in reunified Germany.

returned_title: International Social Survey Programme: Role of Government III – ISSP 1996 (ZA2900)
justification: Excellent match for attitudes toward government, public institutions, and social welfare responsibilities during the 1990s. The 1996 ISSP Role of Government module examines citizens' expectations of government, opinions about state intervention, public spending, and the division of responsibilities between government and individuals. The German component includes East and West German respondents, making it useful for studying regional differences in welfare preferences and political values.

returned_title: International Social Survey Programme: Social Inequality III – ISSP 1999 (ZA3430)
justification: Strong match for the equality, inequality, and social exclusion dimension of the research. The 1999 ISSP module includes Germany and investigates perceived social inequality, fairness, social mobility, income differences, and attitudes toward economic redistribution. It is particularly useful for understanding how socioeconomic position and perceptions of inequality relate to political values and expectations of government at the end of the 1990s.

returned_title: International Social Survey Programme: Social Inequality Cumulation 1987, 1992, 1999, 2009, and 2019
justification: Useful for studying changes in attitudes toward inequality and redistribution across the 1990s. The cumulative ISSP series combines comparable questions from several survey waves, including 1992 and 1999. Researchers can select German respondents and examine developments in beliefs about economic fairness, social mobility, income inequality, and government responsibility. It complements electoral surveys by providing a detailed socioeconomic perspective on political attitudes.

returned_title: International Social Survey Programme: Role of Government Cumulation 1985, 1990, 1996, 2006, and 2016
justification: Highly relevant for comparing attitudes toward state institutions and government responsibilities over time. The cumulative dataset includes the 1990 and 1996 survey waves, with German observations available for relevant participating waves. It supports research into public expectations of government, welfare provision, economic intervention, and political values. Researchers should verify German participation and geographic coverage for each wave before undertaking East–West comparisons.

returned_title: German Federal Election Studies 1949–2009
justification: A valuable collection of historical German election surveys, including studies associated with federal elections in 1990, 1994, and 1998. These surveys are useful for investigating reported voting behavior, party identification, political participation, electoral preferences, and attitudes toward political institutions. The collection provides an important starting point for identifying individual election studies and comparing democratic behavior before and after reunification.

returned_title: Political Attitudes, Political Participation and Voting Behavior in Reunified Germany – Election Study Series 1994–2002
justification: Particularly relevant research series covering German federal election studies conducted in 1994, 1998, and 2002. Its repeated survey design provides opportunities to investigate political attitudes, electoral participation, party preferences, and democratic satisfaction over time. The separate East and West German survey components are particularly suitable for examining regional political differences during the 1990s. The 1994 and 1998 studies directly match the requested period, while the 2002 wave can support follow-up analysis.

returned_title: German State Election Studies – Elections in the New Federal States 1990 (ZA1966)
justification: Relevant for examining electoral behavior and political orientations in eastern Germany immediately following reunification. The GESIS state election collection includes a study of the 1990 elections in the new federal states. It provides an opportunity to investigate early electoral preferences and political participation in the former East Germany. This dataset is particularly useful when combined with national election studies to assess differences between eastern and western political behavior.

returned_title: Integrated Dataset of German State Election Studies 1962–2004
justification: Useful for examining political behavior across German federal states, including elections held during the 1990s. The integrated collection combines historical state election studies and can support analyses of regional electoral preferences, political orientations, and voting behavior. Its geographic coverage is particularly relevant for exploring differences between eastern and western German states following reunification. Researchers should check the documentation for the availability of specific years and attitude measures.

returned_title: German General Social Survey (ALLBUS) – Historical Individual Surveys, 1990–1998
justification: Excellent source for detailed individual-level surveys conducted throughout the 1990s. The ALLBUS archive provides access to separate survey waves for 1990, 1991, 1992, 1994, 1996, and 1998. Depending on the wave, these surveys address political attitudes, participation, trust and satisfaction with political institutions, social values, and socioeconomic characteristics. The 1991 survey included substantial samples from both East and West Germany, making the historical waves particularly valuable for studying the political and social consequences of reunification.

returned_title: World Values Survey (WVS) – Wave 6 (2010–2014)
justification: One of the strongest matches for the research need. Provides nationally representative, cross-national survey microdata on religious affiliation, importance of religion, religious attendance, beliefs, gender roles, attitudes toward homosexuality, trust, tolerance, science, political participation, and demographics. Includes Algeria (2014), Ghana (2012), Jordan (2014), Malaysia (2012), Nigeria (2012), and Singapore (2012). Particularly useful for comparing religious values and social attitudes using standardized questions across countries.

returned_title: World Values Survey (WVS) – Wave 7 (2017–2022)
