justification: Cross-national survey covering religious beliefs, practices, morality, gender equality, sexuality, attitudes toward science, social trust, political behavior, and demographic characteristics. Includes relevant countries such as Indonesia, Mongolia, and Viet Nam, although some interviews occurred after 2019. Particularly valuable for examining changes in religious values and comparing late-2010s attitudes with earlier WVS waves. Country-specific survey years should be checked before restricting analyses to the 2010s.

returned_title: World Values Survey – Longitudinal Multiple-Wave Dataset (1981–2022)
justification: Harmonized cross-national survey dataset combining seven WVS waves, including observations collected during the 2010s. Contains measures of religious identification, religious practices, moral attitudes, interpersonal trust, family values, political participation, and demographic characteristics. Useful for studying differences across the target countries and examining changes in religiosity, tolerance, gender attitudes, and political values over time. Researchers can filter survey observations by country and interview year.

returned_title: Pew Research Center – The World's Muslims Survey Dataset (2011–2012)
justification: Highly relevant cross-national survey of Muslim populations conducted between October 2011 and November 2012 in 26 countries and territories. Includes questions on religious affiliation, religious practices, prayer, fasting, religious identity, beliefs, gender roles, marriage, divorce, sexuality, science, religious law, democracy, and tolerance toward other faiths. Particularly relevant to Indonesia, Malaysia, and Jordan, among other countries. The survey provides detailed individual-level information on relationships between religion, social values, and political attitudes. Its Muslim-focused sampling must be considered when making comparisons with general-population surveys.

returned_title: Pew Research Center – The World's Muslims: Unity and Diversity (2012)
justification: Research collection based on large-scale surveys examining religious beliefs and practices among Muslim populations across Africa, Asia, and the Middle East. Covers religious identity, prayer, fasting, religious commitment, interpretation of religious teachings, and differences in religious practices. Especially useful for studying religious diversity and variation in religiosity across Muslim communities in the target regions. Associated survey microdata and documentation are available through Pew Research Center's religion datasets.

returned_title: Pew Research Center – The World's Muslims: Religion, Politics and Society (2013)
justification: Report and associated survey dataset examining relationships between religion and political or social attitudes among Muslim populations, primarily using 2011–2012 fieldwork. Covers support for religious law, democracy, women's rights, divorce, polygamy, moral judgments, science, and religious freedom. Relevant to research on state-religion relations, sexuality, gender roles, and interreligious tolerance. The underlying survey data can support cross-national comparisons involving Muslim populations in several target countries.

returned_title: Afrobarometer – Round 5 Survey Data (2011–2013)
justification: Cross-national public opinion survey covering African countries, including Ghana, Kenya, Malawi, and Nigeria. Contains individual-level information on religious affiliation, trust, social identities, gender equality, political participation, democratic attitudes, institutional confidence, and demographic characteristics. Particularly valuable for analyzing relationships between religion, social trust, political behavior, and gender attitudes in sub-Saharan Africa during the early 2010s.

returned_title: Afrobarometer – Round 6 Survey Data (2014–2015)
justification: Large-scale comparative survey with coverage of Algeria, Ghana, Kenya, Malawi, and Nigeria. Includes information on religious affiliation, political attitudes, democracy, institutional trust, gender equality, social tolerance, political participation, and socioeconomic characteristics. Especially useful for comparing religious identity and social or political values across North and sub-Saharan Africa using standardized survey instruments. Provides broader African geographical coverage than the World Values Survey for the same period.

returned_title: Afrobarometer – Round 7 Survey Data (2016–2018)
justification: Cross-national African survey conducted during the late 2010s, including Ghana, Kenya, Malawi, and Nigeria. Measures religious affiliation, social tolerance, interpersonal and institutional trust, gender equality, democratic values, political participation, and demographic characteristics. Particularly relevant for studying social distance, acceptance of different social groups, trust, and relationships between religion and political attitudes. Complements earlier Afrobarometer rounds for examining changes during the decade.

returned_title: Pew Research Center – Sub-Saharan Africa Survey Dataset (2008–2009)
justification: A closely related baseline dataset preceding the requested decade. Contains more than 25,000 interviews across 19 sub-Saharan African countries, including relevant target countries such as Ghana, Kenya, Malawi, and Nigeria. Provides detailed measures of religious beliefs, religious practices, knowledge of other religions, interreligious tolerance, and attitudes toward Christianity and Islam. Especially useful for analyzing religious coexistence, social distance, and religious identity. Although fieldwork predates 2010, it complements surveys conducted during the 2010s.

returned_title: Pew Research Center – Religion Datasets Collection
justification: Official repository providing access to individual-level datasets, questionnaires, codebooks, and methodological documentation from Pew Research Center's religion surveys. Relevant collections include international surveys on religious identity, beliefs, religious practices, political attitudes, gender roles, and interreligious relations. Particularly useful for locating comparable survey variables and identifying which target countries participated in specific surveys conducted during the 2010s.

returned_title: World Values Survey – Wave 6 Data Archive, Association of Religion Data Archives
justification: Alternative research archive for World Values Survey Wave 6 data collected during 2010–2014. Provides access to survey materials relevant to religion, religious practices, moral beliefs, social trust, gender attitudes, and political values. Includes several target countries, notably Algeria, Ghana, Jordan, Malaysia, Nigeria, and Singapore. Particularly convenient for researchers seeking to examine religion-related variables through a specialized social science religion data archive.

returned_title: World Values Survey – Wave 6 International Household Survey Network Catalog
justification: Dataset catalog record for the World Values Survey 2010–2014, covering approximately 60 countries and societies and more than 85,000 respondents. Includes Algeria, Ghana, Jordan, Malaysia, Nigeria, and Singapore. Documents internationally comparable measures of religious beliefs, religious identity, social values, tolerance, gender roles, interpersonal trust, political attitudes, and demographic characteristics. Useful for establishing country coverage and identifying relevant survey documentation.

returned_title: Pew Research Center – South and Southeast Asia Survey Dataset (2022)
justification: A highly relevant thematic match, although fieldwork occurred after the requested 2010s period. Covers Cambodia, Indonesia, Malaysia, Singapore, Sri Lanka, and Thailand. Based on 13,122 adult respondents, it measures religious affiliation, religious beliefs and practices, religious identity, nationalism, and attitudes toward religious pluralism. Particularly useful for cross-national comparisons of Buddhism, Islam, religious tolerance, and religious identity. It can complement 2010s datasets but should not be treated as evidence collected during that decade.

returned_title: Pew Research Center – International Religion Survey Data Collection
justification: Centralized collection of cross-national religion survey microdata covering religious beliefs, worship, morality, interreligious tolerance, religious identity, and political attitudes. Includes 2010s survey datasets as well as earlier and later studies. Particularly valuable for identifying detailed questionnaire items concerning religious practices, family religious background where available, religious diversity, and religion's relationship with politics and society. Country coverage and fieldwork dates vary by survey.

returned_title: International Relations (June 1962) – USIA, GESIS Study ZA1975
justification: An exceptionally strong match for the research need. This cross-national public opinion survey was conducted in June 1962 in France, Great Britain, West Germany, and Italy, covering 5,146 respondents. It investigates Cold War security, attitudes toward the United States and Soviet Union, confidence in American foreign policy, nuclear weapons testing, nuclear test-ban treaties, disarmament, alliance commitments, and support for the European Common Market. The dataset contains 167 variables and provides individual-level survey responses suitable for comparative quantitative analysis.

returned_title: European Public Opinion and Foreign Policy: A Continuity Dataset (1952–1970)
justification: An excellent match covering public opinion in France, Great Britain, Germany, and Italy throughout the 1960s. This harmonized dataset combines historical United States Information Agency surveys into a repeated cross-sectional dataset containing 81,755 observations and 340 variables. Topics include Cold War tensions, the risk of war, nuclear weapons, disarmament, NATO, attitudes toward the United States and Soviet Union, European integration, and knowledge of the Cuban Missile Crisis. Its harmonized structure makes it particularly valuable for comparing political attitudes across countries and tracking changes before and after major Cold War events. Data and documentation are available in CSV and Stata formats.

returned_title: European USIA Report Collection – Roper Center for Public Opinion Research
justification: A highly relevant historical collection of public opinion research reports produced by the United States Information Agency. It includes numerous surveys from the 1960s covering France, Great Britain, West Germany, and Italy. Particularly relevant reports include West European Attitudes toward Disarmament (1961), Attitudes toward the European Common Market in Britain and in Three Member Nations (1962), Public Opinion Trends in Western Europe in the Wake of the Cuban Crisis (1963), West European Opinion on the Outcome of the Cuban Crisis (1963), Public Opinion about NATO and Nuclear Issues in Western Europe (1963), and The Sino-Soviet Conflict through Western European Eyes (1963). This collection is especially useful for finding historically specific survey results on nuclear war, NATO, China, the USSR, and European integration. The collection primarily provides research reports rather than a single harmonized individual-level dataset.

returned_title: West European Attitudes toward Disarmament (1961) – USIA Report R476
justification: A United States Information Agency public opinion research report dated August 1961 covering Great Britain, West Germany, France, and Italy. It directly addresses European public attitudes toward disarmament during a period of intense Cold War confrontation. It is relevant for studying the political climate preceding the Cuban Missile Crisis and comparing national views on international security and arms control. The report is indexed as R476 in the Roper Center's European USIA collection.

returned_title: Attitudes toward the European Common Market in Britain and in Three Member Nations (1962) – USIA Report R490
justification: A December 1962 USIA public opinion report covering Great Britain, West Germany, France, and Italy. It specifically examines attitudes toward the European Common Market during the period when Britain was seeking membership in the European Economic Community. It is particularly relevant for comparing British public opinion with attitudes in the three founding member states and for investigating support for European economic and political integration during the Cold War. The report is cataloged as R490.

returned_title: Public Opinion Trends in Western Europe in the Wake of the Cuban Crisis (1963) – USIA Report R491
justification: An especially relevant USIA research report from July 1963 covering Great Britain, West Germany, France, and Italy. It examines European public opinion following the October 1962 Cuban Missile Crisis. The report provides a historically focused source for investigating how this major Cold War confrontation influenced public attitudes toward international security and East-West relations. Its timing makes it valuable for assessing public opinion in the immediate aftermath of the crisis. Cataloged as R491.

returned_title: West European Opinion on the Outcome of the Cuban Crisis (1963) – USIA Report R495
justification: A July 1963 USIA report examining public assessments of the outcome of the Cuban Missile Crisis in Great Britain, West Germany, France, and Italy. This source directly matches the requirement for historical survey evidence concerning the Cuban Missile Crisis. It is particularly useful for comparative research into European reactions to Cold War crisis management and perceptions of the confrontation between the United States and Soviet Union. The report is identified as R495 in the collection.

returned_title: Public Opinion about NATO and Nuclear Issues in Western Europe (1963) – USIA Report R493
justification: A July 1963 public opinion report covering Great Britain, West Germany, France, and Italy. Its focus on NATO and nuclear issues closely matches the research need concerning collective security, nuclear war, and Western defense arrangements during the Cold War. It offers a contemporaneous source for comparing national attitudes toward NATO and nuclear security policy shortly after the Cuban Missile Crisis. The report is cataloged as R493.

returned_title: West European Public Opinion on Disarmament (1963) – USIA Report R496
justification: A July 1963 USIA public opinion report covering Great Britain, West Germany, France, and Italy. It directly addresses public opinion on disarmament during the period following the Cuban Missile Crisis. This report is well suited to studying cross-national differences in attitudes toward arms control, nuclear security, and efforts to reduce Cold War military tensions. It complements the 1961 disarmament report, potentially allowing researchers to examine changes in public attitudes over time. Cataloged as R496.

returned_title: The Sino-Soviet Conflict through Western European Eyes (1963) – USIA Report R497
justification: A July 1963 USIA research report covering Great Britain, West Germany, France, and Italy. It examines Western European public perceptions of the conflict between China and the Soviet Union. This is particularly relevant to the research requirement concerning attitudes toward China and the USSR during the Cold War. It provides a focused historical source for understanding how European publics perceived divisions within the communist bloc and their implications for international relations. Cataloged as R497.

returned_title: Attitudes toward the Common Market in Western Europe (1963) – USIA Report R494
justification: A July 1963 public opinion report covering Great Britain, West Germany, France, and Italy. It focuses on attitudes toward the European Common Market, making it a direct match for research on public support for European economic integration. Its timing is particularly significant because it follows the French veto of British entry into the European Economic Community in January 1963. It can support comparative historical analysis of national differences in public support for European integration. Cataloged as R494.

returned_title: Trends in Western European Estimates of US and Soviet Strength (1963) – USIA Report R492
justification: A July 1963 USIA report covering Great Britain, West Germany, France, and Italy. It examines public perceptions of the relative strength of the United States and Soviet Union. It is relevant for investigating Cold War security perceptions, assessments of the superpower balance, and changes in European attitudes following the Cuban Missile Crisis. The report offers comparative evidence on how Western European publics evaluated the two competing superpowers. Cataloged as R492.

returned_title: West European Opinion on Nuclear Inspection and US Resumption of Nuclear Tests (1962) – USIA Report R482
justification: An August 1962 USIA report covering Great Britain, West Germany, and France. It examines public attitudes toward nuclear inspections and the resumption of American nuclear weapons testing. Although Italy is not included in the listed geographic coverage, the report closely matches the research interest in nuclear disarmament, test-ban verification, and Cold War security policy. Its collection date shortly before the Cuban Missile Crisis makes it particularly useful for establishing pre-crisis public attitudes. Cataloged as R482.

returned_title: Trend in West European Opinion on the Tactical Use of Nuclear Weapons (1962) – USIA Report R487
justification: An August 1962 USIA report examining public opinion on the tactical use of nuclear weapons in Great Britain, West Germany, and France. It directly addresses attitudes toward nuclear warfare during the Cold War. The report is particularly valuable for investigating public acceptance or rejection of nuclear weapons as instruments of military defense before the Cuban Missile Crisis. Italy is not listed among the covered countries, but the report provides a strong thematic match for comparative nuclear security research. Cataloged as R487.

returned_title: The Image of US Nuclear Strength in Western Europe (1962) – USIA Report R484
justification: An August 1962 USIA report covering Great Britain, West Germany, and France. It focuses on European perceptions of American nuclear strength during the Cold War. The report is relevant to research on nuclear deterrence, perceptions of American military capabilities, and European confidence in Western security arrangements. Its pre-Cuban Missile Crisis timing makes it useful for examining the relationship between nuclear power perceptions and international security attitudes. Cataloged as R484.

returned_title: Trend in West European Confidence in the US (1964) – USIA Report R488
justification: An August 1964 USIA report covering Great Britain, West Germany, France, and Italy. It focuses on trends in European public confidence in the United States during the Cold War. This provides a relevant source for comparing national attitudes toward American leadership and the transatlantic relationship in the years following the Cuban Missile Crisis. It is particularly suitable for examining changes in confidence in the United States across the four countries. Cataloged as R488.

returned_title: Small Arms Survey – Global Firearms Holdings Database (2017)
justification: Highly relevant dataset providing country-level estimates of civilian, military, and law enforcement firearms holdings in 2017. Includes estimates of registered and unregistered civilian firearms, total firearms in civilian possession, and firearms per 100 inhabitants. Covers all 27 current EU member states and the United Kingdom. Particularly useful for comparing firearms ownership and availability across European countries during the 2010s.

returned_title: Small Arms Survey – Civilian Firearms Holdings, 2017
justification: Provides standardized estimates of civilian firearm ownership by country for 2017, including registered and unregistered firearms, population-adjusted ownership rates, and estimation methods. Suitable for cross-national statistical analysis of firearm prevalence in Belgium, Denmark, Germany, Greece, Spain, Finland, France, Ireland, Italy, Luxembourg, the Netherlands, Austria, Portugal, Sweden, the United Kingdom, and other European countries. Particularly valuable for examining relationships between firearms availability, regulation, and violent crime.

returned_title: UNODC – Firearms Trafficking and Illicit Arms Flows Database
justification: Official United Nations dataset covering firearms trafficking, seizures, tracing, and criminal justice responses. Includes information on firearms seized, found, or surrendered, as well as firearm types, seizure locations, suspected offences, and trafficking-related characteristics. Data originate primarily from the United Nations Illicit Arms Flows Questionnaire. Particularly relevant for investigating illicit firearms markets, cross-border trafficking, and law enforcement responses in EU countries. Historical coverage and reporting completeness vary by country.

returned_title: UNODC – Firearms Seizures and Seizure Events
justification: Specialized firearms trafficking dataset documenting firearm seizures and seizure events. Information can be disaggregated by weapon type, location, legal justification, weapon modifications, and associated criminal activities. Includes categories such as illicit possession, illicit manufacturing, illicit trafficking, violent crime, drug trafficking, and organized crime. Particularly useful for studying law enforcement activity and the characteristics of illegal firearms circulating in European countries.

returned_title: UNODC – Firearms Tracing Outcomes
justification: Provides information on tracing outcomes for firearms seized, found, or surrendered by national authorities. Relevant to research on illicit firearms origins, trafficking investigations, and international law enforcement cooperation. Can complement national seizure statistics and help assess firearms tracing capabilities across European countries. Availability of historical observations depends on national reporting.

returned_title: UNODC – Intentional Homicide Victims Database
justification: Internationally comparable homicide statistics compiled by the United Nations Office on Drugs and Crime. Includes country-level intentional homicide data and, where reported, breakdowns by the mechanism used, including firearms. Relevant for examining trends in firearm-related homicide across EU member states and the United Kingdom between 2010 and 2019. Particularly useful when combined with firearms ownership and regulatory indicators.

returned_title: Eurostat – Police-Recorded Offences by Offence Category
justification: Official Eurostat dataset covering police-recorded criminal offences across European countries, with historical observations extending from 2008 onward. Includes intentional homicide and other serious offences classified according to international crime statistics standards. Covers EU member states and UK jurisdictions, making it useful for constructing comparative crime indicators for 2010–2019. Although not exclusively focused on firearms, it provides important contextual information for analyzing firearms-related violence and criminal justice outcomes.

returned_title: European Sourcebook of Crime and Criminal Justice Statistics – Original Data
justification: Highly relevant comparative European crime and criminal justice dataset containing historical statistics on police-recorded crime, criminal proceedings, and justice system outcomes. Its historical editions include information on intentional homicides involving firearms, including observations from 2011–2016. Covers numerous EU member states and the United Kingdom. Particularly valuable for constructing a cross-national panel of firearm-related homicide and comparing national criminal justice responses during the 2010s.

returned_title: European Sourcebook of Crime and Criminal Justice Statistics – 2021 Edition
justification: Provides harmonized comparative criminal justice statistics for European countries, including data covering 2011–2016. Contains specific indicators for completed intentional homicides involving firearms, including offence rates and offender statistics. Highly suitable for research on firearm use in violent crime, national variations in lethal violence, and the relationship between firearms availability and homicide rates. Important limitations include missing national observations and differences in police recording practices.

returned_title: Flemish Peace Institute – Project TARGET: Gun Violence and Firearms Trafficking in Europe
justification: One of the strongest matches for the research topic. Project TARGET collected quantitative and qualitative information on firearms trafficking and gun violence in 34 European countries, including all 27 current EU member states and the United Kingdom. Its comparative analysis incorporates historical firearms homicide observations extending through much of the 2010s, with country-specific coverage. The project also examines illicit firearms markets, firearm acquisition, criminal use, and trafficking routes. Particularly valuable for combining statistical evidence with institutional and regulatory analysis.

returned_title: Flemish Peace Institute – Project TARGET Country Studies
justification: Provides detailed country-level empirical research on firearms trafficking and gun violence, with dedicated studies covering Belgium, Estonia, the Netherlands, Poland, Spain, and Sweden, alongside Serbia. The studies examine patterns of illicit firearms possession, firearm use in crime, trafficking networks, and national law enforcement responses. Although the geographical coverage of detailed case studies is narrower than the full EU, the evidence is particularly useful for understanding differences between European firearms markets during and around the 2010s.

returned_title: Gunviolence.eu – European Firearms Violence Country Profiles
justification: EU-funded firearms violence information platform coordinated by the Flemish Peace Institute. Provides country profiles for all 27 current EU member states, integrating information on firearms incidents, relevant research, legislation, and national policy. Particularly useful for locating country-specific evidence on criminal firearms use, regulation, and trafficking. The platform also provides an incident-monitoring component, although its current incident data should not be assumed to provide complete historical coverage of 2010–2019.

returned_title: Gunviolence.eu – European Firearms Legislation and Policy Information
justification: Provides a comparative starting point for researching European firearms legislation, including relevant EU-level and national policy frameworks. Useful for identifying legal restrictions on civilian ownership, firearm acquisition, possession, and trafficking. Particularly relevant to research examining whether differences in firearms regulation are associated with ownership rates or gun violence. This is a structured policy information resource rather than a ready-made longitudinal legal dataset; historical legal changes must be verified individually.

returned_title: UNODC – Firearms Trafficking Data Catalogue
justification: Official catalogue of firearms trafficking datasets covering multiple dimensions of illicit firearms activity, including seizures, firearm tracing, criminal justice responses, and weapon characteristics. Particularly useful for identifying complementary indicators of firearms trafficking and enforcement across European countries. Supports research on organized crime, international trafficking networks, and the effectiveness of firearms control measures. Historical data availability must be checked separately for each indicator and country.

returned_title: Eurostat – Crime and Criminal Justice Statistics
justification: Official European statistical portal providing access to harmonized datasets on crime, criminal justice, intentional homicide, criminal suspects, prosecutions, and convictions. Covers EU member states and includes historical UK statistics. Relevant for constructing national criminal justice indicators and contextualizing firearms-related offences during 2010–2019. Particularly useful for evaluating differences in police-recorded violence and justice system outcomes across countries, although firearms-specific variables are limited.

returned_title: SIPRI – Arms Transfers Database
justification: International database documenting transfers of major conventional weapons between countries, with annual historical observations covering the entire 2010–2019 period. Useful for studying international arms trade relationships, export controls, and the broader European security environment. Covers European countries as importers and exporters. However, the database focuses on major conventional weapons rather than civilian firearms or illicit small-arms trafficking, so it should be treated as a supplementary source rather than a direct measure of civilian firearm ownership or criminal firearms flows.

returned_title: SIPRI – Arms Transfers Import and Export Data
justification: Interactive international arms transfers database enabling country-specific analysis of weapons imports and exports over time. Researchers can examine international transfer relationships involving EU member states and the United Kingdom during the 2010s. Relevant to international politics, arms export regulation, and interstate security cooperation. Primarily measures transfers of major conventional arms, meaning it does not directly capture civilian gun ownership, illegal firearms trafficking, or most small-arms transactions.

returned_title: Small Arms Survey – Global Firearms Holdings Government Questionnaire
justification: Documents the official government data collection framework underlying the Small Arms Survey firearms holdings estimates. Covers legal civilian firearm ownership, private security firearms, military holdings, and law enforcement firearms. Particularly useful for evaluating measurement differences between European countries and understanding how national administrative firearms records contribute to international estimates. This is a methodological and data collection resource rather than an independent historical dataset.

returned_title: Party Preferences Czech Republic 2000 (Trend) — GESIS Study ZA3891
justification: Exact match and the strongest dataset for this research need. This study combines monthly Czech public opinion surveys conducted in 2000 by the Institute for Public Opinion Research (IVVM) and its successor, the Centre for Public Opinion Research (CVVM). It covers January, February, March, April, May, June, September, October, November, and December 2000, with 11,346 respondent observations in total. The dataset focuses on political party preferences, electoral participation and voting behavior, trust in political leaders and institutions, satisfaction with democracy, attitudes toward European integration, economic perceptions, and respondent characteristics. It is particularly suitable for examining changes in Czech political attitudes throughout 2000 and their relationships with religiosity, household living standards, region, and community size. Archived by GESIS with English-language documentation. This should be the primary dataset for the proposed research.

returned_title: Party Preferences Czech Republic 2000 (Trend) — GESIS Data Catalogue
justification: Alternative catalogue record for the exact 2000 monthly survey dataset. The metadata confirms coverage of the Czech Republic from January through December 2000 and identifies the study as part of the Party Preferences Czech Republic series. The surveys represent Czech residents aged 15 and older. Individual monthly samples range from approximately 1,000 respondents to 2,079 in December. The catalogue classifies the dataset under political behaviour and attitudes, government and political systems, and elections, matching all three requested subject categories. This is the same underlying dataset as the first result, rather than an independent data collection.

returned_title: CVVM Public Opinion Survey Archive — Czech Social Science Data Archive
justification: Official repository for public opinion datasets produced by the Czech Centre for Public Opinion Research (CVVM). Its monthly survey program covers political orientation, party identification, election intentions, trust in government and political institutions, attitudes toward international organizations, economic evaluations, and household living standards. The archive provides individual survey datasets, questionnaires, and metadata, making it valuable for identifying original survey waves and verifying the variables included in the combined GESIS dataset. It also supports extending the analysis beyond 2000 to other years in the 2000s. Availability of particular historical monthly waves should be checked in the catalogue.

returned_title: CVVM Our Society 2002 — March (Naše společnost 2002 – březen)
justification: Relevant supplementary dataset from the Czech monthly public opinion survey program, collected in March 2002. Conducted by CVVM at the Institute of Sociology of the Czech Academy of Sciences, it contains 1,072 observations and 184 variables. Its documented themes include domestic politics, political parties, mass media, and international relations. It provides a useful comparison with the 2000 survey series, particularly for studying party preferences and political attitudes in the period surrounding the 2002 parliamentary elections. The archive includes survey data and the original Czech questionnaire, allowing researchers to verify the availability of specific political and demographic variables.

returned_title: Party Preferences Czech Republic 1998 (Trend) — GESIS Study ZA3889
justification: Closely related predecessor to the 2000 dataset, drawn from the same Czech monthly public opinion survey series. It combines surveys conducted during 11 months of 1998 and includes political party preferences, previous voting behavior, election participation, confidence in political figures, satisfaction with democracy, attitudes toward EU membership, economic transformation, religious belief, and living standards. Although collected before the requested period, it is valuable for establishing baseline attitudes and examining changes between the 1998 parliamentary election and the political environment of 2000. Its common survey framework makes it particularly useful for longitudinal comparisons with GESIS Study ZA3891.

returned_title: Die Reichstagswahlen und Reichspräsidentschaftswahlen in Kiel 1925–1932 (The Reichstag Elections and Reich Presidential Elections in Kiel, 1925–1932) — GESIS ZA8080
justification: Exact match for the research need. This dataset, compiled by Wolfram Schulz and archived by GESIS, contains voting-district-level election results for 156 Stimmbezirke (voting districts) in Kiel, German Reich. It covers all six requested elections: Reichstag elections in May 1928, September 1930, July 1932, and November 1932, plus Reich presidential elections in 1925 and 1932. The dataset contains 50 variables and is available in SPSS and Stata formats. Results were collected from contemporary newspapers, including the Schleswig-Holsteinische Volkszeitung and Kieler Neueste Nachrichten. Important limitation: The records provide vote counts but do not include voter turnout or results for minor fringe parties. Published in 2008, with dataset version 1.0.0 dated April 13, 2010. This is the strongest available match because its geographic coverage, electoral periods, and voting-district granularity correspond exactly to the query.

returned_title: Wahlstatistische Datenbank für Schleswig-Holstein 1919–1938 — Arbeitskreis zur Erforschung des Nationalsozialismus in Schleswig-Holstein (AKENS)
justification: Highly relevant complementary historical election database covering Schleswig-Holstein between 1919 and 1938, including Kiel. Its holdings include election results at the municipality, district, and individual polling-station levels. The database explicitly includes Stimmbezirk-level results for Kiel and covers Reichstag and presidential elections during the Weimar Republic. It can supplement the GESIS dataset with additional historical election records and geographic context. Coverage and availability of individual Kiel polling-station records should be checked for each requested election.

returned_title: German Weimar Republic Data, 1919–1933 — ICPSR Study 42
justification: Relevant supplementary dataset containing German electoral and demographic information from the Weimar Republic. It includes Reichstag election returns for 1920–1933 and Reich presidential election results for 1925 and 1932, including runoff elections. The dataset records party and candidate vote totals, eligible voters, and electoral participation, making it useful for contextualizing Kiel's electoral patterns within national and regional trends. However, its geographic units are Kreis, Land/Regierungsbezirk, and Wahlkreis rather than individual Kiel voting districts. It therefore does not independently satisfy the requested Stimmbezirk-level granularity.

returned_title: Wahlstatistische Datenbank, Schleswig-Holstein 1919–1938 — AKENS Historical Election Data Archive
justification: An additional entry point to AKENS historical electoral statistics covering Schleswig-Holstein during the Weimar Republic and National Socialist period. The archive documents election results from 1919 through 1938, including Reichstag elections, presidential elections, and other votes. Its records include results from individual polling districts in selected cities, including Kiel. It is particularly useful for locating historical election tables and complementary records for the July and November 1932 elections. This is an alternative access point to the AKENS collection listed above, not necessarily an independent dataset.

returned_title: Eurobarometer 19 (March–April 1983)
justification: Highly relevant historical survey conducted in West Germany between March 28 and April 19, 1983, during Yuri Andropov's leadership of the Soviet Union. Provides individual-level public opinion data from the Cold War period. Potentially useful for investigating West German attitudes toward international relations, European political alignment, political institutions, and contemporary security concerns. The timing makes it particularly valuable for studying attitudes during the early Andropov period, although the availability of questions specifically addressing Andropov and comparative US–Soviet strength requires verification.

returned_title: West German Election Study 1987 (Trend Studies / Politbarometer)
justification: Representative West German political opinion surveys covering January 1986 through February 1987, containing 14,375 observations. Includes political attitudes, party preferences, party and politician sympathy scales, voting intentions, and evaluations of contemporary political issues. Relevant for examining relationships between political affiliation, security attitudes, and foreign policy preferences during the late Cold War. Particularly useful for party sympathy and political-demographic analysis, although it does not cover Andropov's leadership.

returned_title: German General Social Survey (ALLBUS) – Cumulation 1980–2014
justification: Major longitudinal survey resource covering West Germany throughout the 1980s. Includes political orientations, party identification, party sympathy, political interest, institutional confidence, socioeconomic characteristics, and extensive demographic information. Useful for contextualizing Cold War security perceptions within broader West German political culture and examining how ideological orientation, education, occupation, and economic position relate to international political attitudes. The 1980s observations can be selected for historical analysis. Specific questions comparing the USA and USSR or evaluating Andropov are not confirmed.

returned_title: International Social Survey Programme: Role of Government I/II – ISSP 1985–1990
justification: Internationally comparative survey containing West German observations collected between May and August 1985. Covers attitudes toward government responsibilities, political institutions, public policy, and economic intervention. Relevant for examining West Germans' political and economic values during the Cold War and comparing their views with those of American respondents. Provides useful background for understanding ideological differences between capitalist democracies, although direct US–Soviet military comparisons and Andropov-specific questions are outside its confirmed scope.

returned_title: International Social Survey Programme: Role of Government I–V ADD ON (1985–2016)
justification: Harmonized cross-national survey dataset incorporating the 1985 Role of Government study, including West German respondents. Relevant to research on economic systems, government intervention, political values, and public expectations of state institutions. Offers opportunities to compare West German and American attitudes toward economic and governmental responsibilities. Its harmonized structure supports comparative analysis, but it is a supplementary rather than direct source for perceptions of Soviet leadership or Cold War military power.

returned_title: Regular European Survey No. 2 (December 1968)
justification: Historical West German public opinion dataset produced by the United States Information Agency (USIA). Particularly relevant because its documented questionnaire includes perceptions of the alignment of German interests with the USA versus USSR, American cooperation with Europe, military strength, NATO, Soviet threats to Western Europe, and confidence in American foreign policy. These topics closely match the requested Cold War security-attitude measures. However, data were collected in December 1968–January 1969 rather than the 1980s. It is therefore most useful as an earlier methodological reference for identifying comparable USIA surveys conducted during Andropov's leadership.

returned_title: Crime in the Modern City (Kriminalität in der modernen Stadt) – Duisburg Longitudinal Panel Study, 2002–2019
justification: Excellent match. This longitudinal criminological study, conducted by Klaus Boers and Jost Reinecke, investigates the development of adolescent delinquency, victimization, and deviant behavior in Duisburg. Beginning in 2002, the study surveyed students in the 7th and 9th grades. The younger cohort was followed through 13 survey waves until 2019, covering approximately ages 13 to 30, while the original 9th-grade cohort was followed for two waves. Variables include self-reported delinquency, victimization, school experiences, parenting styles, family relationships, peer groups, conflict behavior, attitudes toward crime, social control, lifestyles, leisure activities, and consumption. The linked university research page provides study documentation, methodological reports, and codebooks for longitudinal analysis.

returned_title: Crime in the Modern City – Duisburg 2002–2003 Two-Wave Panel
justification: Highly relevant to the original 7th- and 9th-grade student cohorts. This two-wave panel follows Duisburg students surveyed in 2002 and 2003, allowing researchers to investigate changes in adolescent delinquency, victimization, school experiences, peer relationships, and social attitudes. It is particularly useful for comparing the initial developmental patterns of both school-grade cohorts. The university's documentation collection includes methodological information about the Duisburg two-wave panel.

returned_title: Crime in the Modern City – Duisburg 2002–2005 Four-Wave Panel
justification: Strong match for longitudinal research on adolescent delinquency during the early 2000s. This four-wave panel follows the younger Duisburg student cohort from 7th grade in 2002 through 2005. It supports the investigation of changes in offending, victimization, school experiences, conflict behavior, crime-related attitudes, peer influences, family environments, and leisure activities. The longitudinal structure enables analysis of individual developmental trajectories during adolescence.

returned_title: Crime in the Modern City – Duisburg 2002–2007 Six-Wave Panel
justification: Excellent match for studying the transition from adolescence toward adulthood. This six-wave panel follows members of the original 2002 Duisburg 7th-grade cohort through 2007. The study examines self-reported crime, victimization, social control, family and peer relationships, conflict behavior, attitudes toward criminal activity, and leisure and consumption patterns. Its longitudinal design is especially valuable for investigating how school environments, social relationships, and changing lifestyles relate to delinquency trajectories.

returned_title: Crime in the Modern City – Duisburg 2002–2013 Ten-Wave Panel
justification: Highly relevant longitudinal dataset covering the transition from early adolescence to young adulthood. The ten-wave panel tracks the original Duisburg 7th-grade cohort from 2002 through 2013. It provides opportunities to analyze the persistence and desistance of delinquent behavior, experiences of victimization, changing attitudes toward crime, family and peer relationships, social integration, leisure activities, and transitions into vocational education and employment. The university documentation includes a methodological report for this panel.

returned_title: Crime in the Modern City – Duisburg 2013 (GESIS ZA8863)
justification: Directly relevant archived research dataset from the Duisburg longitudinal study. Published by GESIS, this dataset contains the 2013 survey wave, with 2,849 observations and 775 variables. It belongs to the research project that began in 2002 with 7th- and 9th-grade students. The dataset includes information about peer groups, leisure activities, social attitudes, delinquency, victimization, family relationships, conflict behavior, lifestyles, and consumption. Its subject classifications closely match the requested fields, including crime and law enforcement, legal systems, psychology, family life, community life, leisure, social behavior, vocational training, and employment. It is a wave-specific dataset rather than the complete linked longitudinal panel.

returned_title: Crime in the Modern City – Duisburg 2019 (GESIS ZA8866)
justification: Relevant final survey wave of the Duisburg longitudinal research project. The 2019 data provide information about participants who were originally recruited as students in 2002 and had reached approximately age 30. The dataset is especially useful for examining adult delinquency, victimization, social relationships, lifestyles, and employment-related outcomes in the context of earlier adolescent experiences. It can support research on long-term developmental patterns when used with appropriately linked earlier waves. The GESIS record provides access information and documentation.

returned_title: Crime in the Modern City – Duisburg Longitudinal Study Research Data and Project Documentation
justification: Official German Research Foundation project record for the study underlying the requested longitudinal datasets. The project investigates adolescent delinquency and deviance in relation to urban social environments, lifestyles, leisure and consumption patterns, ethnic and cultural orientations, and formal and informal social control. Its Duisburg component began in 2002 and followed participants into adulthood. This project landing page is useful for identifying the research design, principal investigators, related publications, and the broader longitudinal data collection. It is a project record rather than a direct dataset download.

returned_title: Rolling Cross-Section Campaign Survey with Post-election Panel Wave (GLES 2013)
justification: Excellent match and the most directly relevant dataset for the research need. Part of the German Longitudinal Election Study (GLES), this survey examines political attitudes, voting intentions, electoral behavior, party and candidate evaluations, political issues, media consumption, interpersonal political communication, economic perceptions, and sociodemographic characteristics surrounding the 2013 German federal election. Data were collected between July 8 and November 3, 2013, using computer-assisted telephone interviews. Its rolling cross-sectional design permits daily analysis of campaign dynamics, while the post-election panel wave supports investigation of changes in political preferences and actual voting behavior. GESIS study ZA5703, version 2.0.2.

returned_title: German Longitudinal Election Study (GLES) – Election Campaign Panel 2013
justification: Highly relevant longitudinal survey of eligible German voters during the 2013 federal election campaign. The election campaign panel is designed to investigate changes in political attitudes, party preferences, vote intentions, candidate evaluations, issue positions, and campaign engagement across successive survey waves. Particularly valuable for studying individual-level changes in political behavior, campaign effects, media exposure, political discussions, and the relationship between economic perceptions and electoral decisions. The GESIS landing page provides access to the GLES study collection and documentation.

returned_title: German Longitudinal Election Study (GLES) – Cross-Section Pre-Election and Post-Election Surveys 2013
justification: Strong match for analyzing voter attitudes and behavior before and after the September 2013 German federal election. The GLES cross-sectional surveys provide information on electoral participation, voting decisions, political interest, party identification, candidate perceptions, issue priorities, political trust, economic evaluations, and demographic characteristics. The pre-election and post-election structure facilitates comparisons between stated voting intentions and reported electoral behavior. The post-election study also contributes to the German component of the Comparative Study of Electoral Systems (CSES).

returned_title: Candidate Campaign Survey 2013, Survey and Electoral/Structural Data (GLES)
justification: Directly relevant supplementary dataset examining political attitudes, campaign activities, political communication, and issue positions among candidates participating in the 2013 German federal election. The survey covers candidates from CDU, CSU, SPD, FDP, Alliance 90/The Greens, and Die Linke. Data collection took place between October 16, 2013, and January 10, 2014. The dataset combines candidate survey responses with electoral and structural information, enabling comparisons between candidate positions, party strategies, and voter preferences. Particularly valuable for research on political representation, campaign organization, party competition, and candidate behavior. GESIS study ZA5716.

returned_title: German Longitudinal Election Study 2013 – Short-term Campaign Panel Control Group II
justification: Relevant supplementary dataset from the GLES 2013 election campaign research program. This online panel survey covers individuals eligible to vote in the 2013 German Bundestag election. It provides a comparison group for the short-term campaign panel, supporting research on changes in political attitudes and electoral preferences across the campaign period. Particularly useful for investigating campaign effects and assessing differences between repeated survey participants and comparison-group respondents. The GESIS documentation identifies the study as the second control group associated with the 2013 short-term campaign panel.

returned_title: German Longitudinal Election Study 2013 – Long-term Panel and Election Campaign Panel Intermediate Survey
justification: Relevant longitudinal survey resource linking the GLES 2013 long-term panel and election campaign panel. It is useful for studying political attitudes and electoral preferences in the context of the 2013 federal election and for examining continuity and change in political orientations across survey periods. The intermediate survey provides additional observations for researchers investigating the relationship between longer-term political predispositions and short-term election campaign dynamics. GESIS documentation identifies the study as the 2013 intermediate survey of the long-term and election campaign panels.

returned_title: Long-term Online Tracking Survey for the 2013 Bavarian State Election (GLES)
justification: Strong supplementary match for the state-election component of the research need. This GLES study focuses on the 2013 Bavarian state election, which occurred shortly before the September 2013 federal election. The online tracking design is relevant for examining electoral preferences and political attitudes in a regional campaign context. It can support comparisons between federal and state electoral dynamics, especially regarding party competition and voter decision-making. Listed by GESIS under study number ZA5736, the dataset is particularly useful for investigating the interaction between regional and national electoral politics.

returned_title: Quick Survey on the Federal Parliament Election 2013 (Blitzumfrage zur Bundestagswahl 2013)
justification: Relevant supplementary survey specifically focused on the 2013 German federal election. The dataset belongs to the GESIS collection of election-related research data and is classified under political behavior and attitudes, government and political systems, and elections. It provides an additional election-specific survey source for studying political opinions and electoral behavior around the 2013 Bundestag election. Particularly useful for supplementing the more extensive GLES panel and cross-sectional studies. GESIS study ZA5937.

returned_title: German Longitudinal Election Study (GLES) – Election Studies and Campaign Research Data Collection
justification: Authoritative landing page for the broader collection of German election research datasets, including the 2013 federal election studies. The collection encompasses rolling cross-sectional campaign surveys, election campaign panels, long-term panels, pre-election and post-election cross-sections, candidate studies, and other election-related research components. It is especially useful for identifying complementary datasets that jointly cover political attitudes, voting intentions, actual electoral behavior, candidate evaluations, issue positions, political communication, and sociodemographic characteristics. The collection also supports comparisons between the 2009, 2013, and 2017 federal elections.

returned_title: German State Election Surveys – GESIS Election Studies Collection
justification: Relevant resource for locating representative election surveys conducted around German state elections, including studies from the 2010s. The collection contains surveys associated with state electoral contests and provides opportunities to examine political attitudes, voting intentions, party preferences, and regional electoral behavior. Particularly useful for extending research beyond the 2013 federal election to regional political contexts and investigating relationships between federal and state party competition. The GESIS collection includes the 2013 Bavarian election tracking study and historical state-election survey data.

returned_title: Politbarometer – German Political Opinion and Election Survey Data
justification: Valuable complementary source for investigating German public opinion and electoral preferences during the 2010s, including the 2013 federal election period. The Politbarometer survey series, conducted by Forschungsgruppe Wahlen and archived by GESIS, provides repeated measurements of political opinions and attitudes. Its annual cumulative datasets support longitudinal analysis of changes in public opinion and political preferences. Particularly useful for contextualizing GLES findings within broader trends in German electoral politics and comparing attitudes across multiple election periods.

returned_title: German Longitudinal Election Study – Election Research Data and Documentation
justification: Dedicated GLES data access resource identified by the WZB Berlin Social Science Center. It provides access to research data and documentation covering German federal elections beginning in 2009, including the 2013 election. The available study types include election campaign panels, rolling cross-sectional surveys, long-term tracking studies, candidate surveys, media content data, and election-related cross-sections. Particularly valuable for researchers seeking multiple complementary sources on voting behavior, campaign communication, political attitudes, party evaluations, and media effects during the 2013 election campaign.

returned_title: Comparative National Development Project (Uruguay), 1966 — GESIS ZA0401
justification: Excellent match to the research requirements. Conducted in Uruguay in 1966 under the direction of Seymour M. Lipset, this survey investigates university students' attitudes toward political, social, and economic issues, educational problems, and the role of elites in developing countries (the Third World). Topics include motivations for university enrollment, career aspirations, educational satisfaction, university functions, political involvement, political discussions, international affairs, and social values. The study includes demographic and socioeconomic background information useful for examining differences in attitudes. Its subject classifications explicitly cover higher education, social behaviour and attitudes, and political behaviour and attitudes. This is the closest match to the requested dataset.

returned_title: University Students' Values, Vocations, and Political Orientations: Uruguay, 1966 (ICPSR 7064)
justification: Excellent match. This 1966 survey of university students in Uruguay examines educational experiences, professional expectations, political orientations, social values, and attitudes toward national and international economic issues. Questions address agrarian reform, government intervention, foreign investment, Latin American economic integration, the Cuban Revolution, political participation, and student and faculty involvement in politics. Educational variables include secondary schooling, academic aspirations, university expectations, and parental and grandparental education. Demographic variables explicitly include age, sex, marital status, number of siblings, religion, and occupation. The dataset forms part of a comparative Latin American university student research project and is particularly suitable for investigating student attitudes, educational problems, and political orientations in developing societies. It appears to be an alternative archival version of the GESIS study listed above.

returned_title: Multi-National Student Survey, 1967–1968
justification: Potentially relevant comparative dataset examining university students' political attitudes, social values, educational experiences, and perceptions of national and international problems during the late 1960s. The survey investigates student political participation, demonstrations, organizational membership, political ideology, religious beliefs, social progress, national priorities, and attitudes toward contemporary political issues. Background variables include age, sex, citizenship, university, field of study, anticipated occupation, father's occupation, family income relative to national income levels, and religious affiliation. Occupational and family-income information may support analysis of socioeconomic background and social class. However, the available description does not establish whether Uruguay was among the participating countries, so geographical coverage must be verified before using this dataset.

returned_title: Uruguay Public Opinion Survey Collection — Roper Center for Public Opinion Research
justification: Useful supplementary source for historical political and social attitudes in Uruguay. The Roper Center identifies 19 Uruguayan survey datasets from the 1960s. Topics represented across its Uruguay collection include political preferences, electoral behaviour, government evaluations, economic conditions, international relations, and social conflict. These historical surveys may provide contextual evidence about public attitudes during the period when university students were becoming politically active. However, this is a collection landing page rather than a single student-focused dataset, and individual surveys must be examined to determine whether they include educational attitudes, student respondents, or the requested demographic variables.

returned_title: European Values Study 1990: Integrated Dataset (EVS 1990, ZA4460)
justification: Excellent match. The second wave of the European Values Study provides cross-national survey data collected between 1990 and 1993, including Great Britain and Northern Ireland. The Great Britain sample contains 1,484 respondents interviewed between June and September 1990. Topics include religious beliefs and practices, moral values, political participation, confidence in institutions, democracy, social trust, tolerance, family relationships, marriage, gender roles, employment, job satisfaction, materialism versus post-materialism, subjective well-being, and demographic characteristics. Particularly suitable for comparing British values with those of other European countries during the early 1990s.

returned_title: European Values Study 1999: Integrated Dataset (EVS 1999, ZA3811)
justification: Excellent match. The third wave of the European Values Study covers 33 European countries and regions, including Great Britain and Northern Ireland. It includes British survey data collected in 1999 and addresses religion, morality, politics, work, leisure, family relationships, social capital, solidarity, democracy, and work ethics. Relevant variables examine trust in political institutions, attitudes toward democracy, immigration and social tolerance, gender roles, marriage, religious participation, personal happiness, economic values, and socioeconomic characteristics. Particularly valuable for examining British attitudes at the end of the 1990s and comparing them with other European societies.

returned_title: European Values Study 1999: Great Britain National Dataset (ZA3777)
justification: Highly relevant country-specific dataset containing interviews with 1,000 respondents in Great Britain between October and November 1999. Unlike the integrated European dataset, this national dataset also retains additional country-specific variables. It addresses religious commitment, moral attitudes, political values, democracy, social trust, immigration, work orientations, family life, marriage, gender expectations, social relationships, and individual well-being. Demographic information supports analysis by age, gender, education, employment, income, and other social characteristics. Especially appropriate for research focused specifically on British society in 1999.

returned_title: European Values Study 1981–2017: Trend File (ZA7503)
justification: Excellent match for longitudinal research. This harmonized dataset combines multiple waves of the European Values Study, including the 1990 and 1999 surveys conducted in Great Britain. It enables researchers to investigate changes in religious beliefs, moral attitudes, political confidence, democratic values, social trust, tolerance, family orientations, gender roles, employment values, happiness, and post-materialist orientations. Its standardized variables facilitate comparisons between British respondents in 1990 and 1999 and with respondents from other European countries. Particularly useful for examining how British social and political values evolved throughout the 1990s.

returned_title: European Values Study, 1990 (EVS '90) – DANS Dataset
justification: Highly relevant archival dataset associated with the 1990 European Values Study. It contains comparative information on religiosity, church involvement, moral values, political conservatism and progressivism, institutional confidence, intolerance, materialism and post-materialism, political involvement, psychological well-being, marriage, family, abortion, education, and work. Background variables include household characteristics, occupation, employment, income, education, social class, political affiliation, religious identification, and organizational membership. Particularly useful for studying relationships between social stratification, religious values, political attitudes, and family orientations in Britain and other participating countries.

returned_title: World Values Survey: Wave 2 (1990–1994)
justification: Relevant complementary international survey dataset covering social, cultural, religious, political, and economic values during the early 1990s. Topics include democratic legitimacy, confidence in government, political participation, interpersonal trust, tolerance, religious beliefs, family values, gender roles, job preferences, subjective well-being, and materialist versus post-materialist priorities. It supports international comparative research, although European Values Study observations from this period are maintained separately. Researchers studying the United Kingdom should use the EVS 1990 dataset for the corresponding British observations rather than assume they are duplicated in this WVS release.

returned_title: World Values Survey: Longitudinal Time-Series Dataset (1981–2022)
justification: Useful complementary longitudinal dataset containing harmonized international survey observations across seven World Values Survey waves, including surveys conducted during the 1990s. Variables cover religion, morality, democracy, political trust, immigration-related tolerance, national identity, family relationships, gender equality, employment preferences, life satisfaction, post-materialism, and demographic characteristics. It is particularly suitable for examining international trends and placing British findings within a broader comparative framework. However, British observations from the European Values Study in 1990 and 1999 must be obtained from EVS datasets because they are not automatically included in the WVS time-series file.

returned_title: Integrated Values Surveys (IVS) 1981–2022: European Values Study and World Values Survey
justification: Excellent conceptual match for the requested research because it brings together the European Values Study and World Values Survey research programs. The integrated framework encompasses European and international surveys on moral, religious, political, social, economic, and family values. It supports comparative analyses of attitudes toward democracy, institutions, immigrants, gender roles, religion, social trust, subjective well-being, and materialism versus post-materialism. The underlying EVS component contains British observations from 1990 and 1999. Particularly valuable for researchers seeking to examine British values during the 1990s within a broader European and global context. The landing page provides information on constructing the integrated data file from the component trend datasets.

returned_title: German General Social Survey (ALLBUS) 1982 (ZA1160)
justification: Strong match for survey research on social conditions, moral values, family relationships, parenting, religion, and political attitudes among adults in West Germany. Conducted from February to May 1982, the survey covers attitudes toward marriage and family, desired characteristics of children, educational goals, religious beliefs and practices, political orientations, and the importance of different aspects of life. Includes detailed demographic characteristics. Particularly relevant for examining intergenerational values and social change during the 1980s, although retrospective memories of the 1950s are not its primary focus.

returned_title: German General Social Survey (ALLBUS) – Cumulation 1980–2014 (ZA4584)
justification: Highly relevant longitudinally comparable collection of repeated cross-sectional surveys of German adults. The 1980–1988 waves cover West Germany and West Berlin, providing information on social values, family structures, religious affiliation, political attitudes, social participation, and socioeconomic characteristics. Useful for identifying changes in moral orientations, parenting attitudes, and social conditions throughout the 1980s. Its detailed demographic variables support comparisons between generations, including adults who experienced the postwar period.

returned_title: German General Social Survey (ALLBUS) – Cumulation 1980–2008
justification: Relevant harmonized survey dataset containing West German adult respondents from 1980, 1982, 1984, 1986, and 1988. Covers religious values, marriage and family life, political behavior, social attitudes, and demographic characteristics. Especially useful for comparing adults from different birth cohorts and investigating how experiences of postwar Germany may relate to values and political orientations in the 1980s. Retrospective questions about the 1950s and youth-group membership would need to be verified at the variable level.

returned_title: World Values Surveys and European Values Surveys, 1981–1984, 1990–1993, and 1995–1997
justification: Strong thematic match for moral values, religion, parenting, family relationships, political beliefs, and social attitudes. Includes survey data from the early 1980s, allowing examination of West German adults' views on morality, child-rearing, marriage, religious practices, political participation, and social institutions. Detailed demographic variables include age, sex, occupation, household composition, income, and geographic characteristics. Particularly useful for studying generational differences in values, although detailed memories of the 1950s and historical youth-group affiliation are not central components.

returned_title: DJI Youth Survey 1992 and 1997 – Cumulated Dataset (ZA3608)
justification: Supplementary dataset examining moral orientations, social conditions, political attitudes, identity, family relationships, and youth experiences in Germany. Includes questions about life satisfaction, discussions with parents, political values, social belonging, and demographic characteristics. Useful for comparing the attitudes of younger generations with those of adults surveyed during the 1980s. However, data collection occurred in 1992 and 1997, making this a secondary rather than direct match for research focused on West Germany during the 1980s.

returned_title: Flash Eurobarometer 223: Euro Introduction in Malta (2008)
justification: The most directly relevant dataset for this research. Conducted shortly after Malta adopted the euro on January 1, 2008, this survey examines Maltese citizens' experiences with the currency changeover, their satisfaction with the transition, and their perceptions of its success. It provides evidence about public attitudes, practical difficulties, familiarity with the new currency, and concerns surrounding the introduction of the euro. Particularly useful for studying the immediate social consequences of euro adoption.

returned_title: Flash Eurobarometer 223: Euro Introduction in Malta — European Commission Data Portal
justification: Official European Commission dataset landing page for the 2008 post-adoption survey in Malta. Provides access to survey results and statistical tables, including demographic breakdowns. Researchers can examine how experiences and satisfaction with the euro changeover differed across population groups. This is an alternative access point to the same underlying survey represented by the GESIS dataset above.

returned_title: Flash Eurobarometer 207: Introduction of the Euro in the New Member States (2007)
justification: A comparative public opinion survey conducted before Malta adopted the euro. Includes Malta and other newer EU member states, examining knowledge of euro coins and banknotes, awareness of euro adoption, expectations, and attitudes toward the common currency. Particularly valuable as a pre-adoption baseline against which to compare Maltese citizens' experiences and perceptions after January 2008. Enables analysis of changes in public confidence, expectations, and acceptance of the euro.

returned_title: Flash Eurobarometer 221: Dual Circulation Period in Malta — Daily Monitoring of the Cash Changeover
justification: A survey focused on the practical introduction of euro cash in Malta during January 2008, when the euro and Maltese lira circulated simultaneously. It is particularly relevant for examining everyday experiences with the new currency, including the use of euro banknotes and coins in transactions and the progress of the cash changeover. The GESIS Flash Eurobarometer study overview provides a route to locating this survey and its associated documentation.

returned_title: Eurostat: Harmonised Index of Consumer Prices (HICP) — Monthly Data
justification: Official Eurostat monthly consumer price dataset covering Malta before and after euro adoption in January 2008. It enables analysis of changes in inflation and consumer prices during the transition, including comparisons with other euro-area countries. Especially useful for investigating whether concerns about price increases following the currency changeover corresponded to measurable inflation. Researchers can examine monthly price developments during 2007–2009 and compare them with public perceptions recorded in Eurobarometer surveys.

returned_title: Eurostat: Harmonised Index of Consumer Prices — Annual Data
justification: Provides annual consumer price indices and inflation rates for Malta, allowing researchers to assess medium-term economic developments around euro adoption. The dataset supports comparisons of inflation before and after 2008, as well as comparisons between Malta and other European economies. It complements the monthly inflation data by offering a broader perspective on changes in the cost of living, one of the principal social and economic concerns associated with adopting the euro.

returned_title: Sofortresonanzen DDR Fernsehen 52. Woche 1983 (SFR 52/83)
justification: Excellent match. This GESIS survey, conducted in December 1983, examines East German television audience participation, viewing behavior, and evaluations of specific broadcasts. It includes assessments of the entertainment program 'Ein Kessel Buntes', its female host, humor, scripts, and overall quality; reasons for not watching 'Theo Adam lädt ein'; expectations concerning the film 'Sabine Kleist, sieben Jahre'; and satisfaction with Christmas and holiday programming, including children's television. Demographic variables include household size, age, gender, education, occupation, continuing education, party membership, voluntary activities, and television reception conditions. The study uses a representative household sample drawn from registered television subscribers in the GDR.

returned_title: Sofortresonanzen DDR Fernsehen 50. Woche 1982 (SFR 50/82)
justification: Highly relevant GESIS dataset collected in December 1982. Investigates television viewing and audience evaluations of programs broadcast during the preceding week. Questions address the entertainment value, humor, and quality of 'Klock 8, achtern Strom'; preferred Saturday evening entertainment; holiday vacations and opportunities to watch television; reception of 'Verkehrskompass'; and viewing frequency and evaluations of the series 'Busch singt'. Particularly useful for examining holiday viewing practices, entertainment preferences, television series, and differences between demographic groups.

returned_title: Sofortresonanzen DDR Fernsehen 6. Woche 1983 (SFR 6/83)
justification: Directly relevant survey from February 1983 examining audience participation and evaluations of East German television. Includes questions about the entertainment value, presenter, and target age group of 'Bong'; information value and regular viewing of 'Porträt per Telefon: Heinz Quermann'; assessments of 'Magdeburger Motive'; and humor, audience loyalty, and suggested improvements concerning 'Klock 8, achtern Strom'. Especially valuable for research on entertainment hosts, audience preferences, program evaluations, and age-related viewing behavior.

returned_title: Sofortresonanzen DDR Fernsehen 36. Woche 1985 (SFR 36/85)
justification: Strong match for research on East German television films, presenters, and audience evaluations. Conducted in August 1985, this GESIS survey measures participation in and evaluations of recently broadcast programs. It examines presenters of 'Sport aktuell', the suspense and perceived realism of the television crime film 'Polizeiruf 110 – Ein Schritt zu weit', audience expectations, and reactions to the television film 'Die dritte Frau', including preferences for individual characters. Also includes questions about film preferences and awareness of television programming information. Suitable for analyzing audience responses to particular films and presenters across demographic groups.

returned_title: Sofortresonanzen DDR Fernsehen 23. Woche 1987 (SFR 23/87)
justification: Relevant GESIS audience survey conducted in June 1987. Examines viewing participation and assessments of programs from the preceding week. Specific questions investigate the perceived realism and informational content of the film 'Der Freischütz in Berlin', audience preferences for its principal characters, and prior knowledge of Carl Maria von Weber. It also evaluates the presenter, entertainment content, and informational quality of 'Wennschon – Dennschon', alongside responses to 'Wildschweinjagd' and 'Wettlauf mit der Zeit'. Useful for studying television films, entertainment presenters, audience perceptions, and demographic differences.

returned_title: Sofortresonanzen DDR Fernsehen 28. Woche 1989 (SFR 28/89)
justification: Highly relevant survey conducted in July 1989, shortly before the collapse of the GDR. Measures television viewing and evaluations of individual broadcasts. Includes audience ratings of the host and performers appearing in 'Showkolade', reception of the series 'Pfundgrube', assessments of its female presenter and musical diversity, knowledge of Lion Feuchtwanger and his novel 'Narrenweisheit', and satisfaction with DDR television programming. Also investigates evaluations of television coverage of the World Festival of Youth and Students in Pyongyang. Particularly useful for examining late-1980s entertainment programming, presenters, audience satisfaction, and television preferences.

returned_title: Sofortresonanzen DDR Fernsehen 46. Woche 1984 (SFR 46/84)
justification: Relevant representative television audience survey conducted in November 1984. Investigates viewing participation and evaluations of programs broadcast during the preceding week.
